{"id":"11626217","title":"AI Improve Readability: Turn Any Text into Scannable Web Content","slug":"ai-improve-readability-turn-any-text-into-scannable-web-content","content":"

Type / in any comment or description field and select \"AI Improve Readability\" to transform your text using Nielsen Norman Group research.

\n

How to Access AI Improve Readability

  1. Click in any comment or description field

  2. Type / (forward slash) to open the menu

  3. Select \"AI Improve Readability\"

  4. Watch your text transform instantly

The Science Behind Web Readability

Research from the Nielsen Norman Group shows web users read differently than print readers. Jacob Nielsen's landmark study revealed three critical principles:

  1. Concise writing improves comprehension by 58%

  2. Scannable formatting increases usability by 47%

  3. Objective tone boosts user satisfaction by 27%

Combined, these improvements deliver 124% better overall usability.

What AI Improve Readability Does

Makes Text Concise

  • Removes unnecessary words and phrases

  • Shortens complex sentences

  • Eliminates redundant information

  • Cuts filler words that slow reading

Creates Scannable Format

  • Adds numbered lists for sequential information

  • Creates bullet points for related items

  • Breaks long paragraphs into digestible chunks

  • Uses clear headings and structure

Applies Objective Tone

  • Removes subjective language

  • Focuses on facts and actionable items

  • Uses direct, professional language

  • Eliminates emotional or biased phrasing

Real-World Impact

Teams using AI-optimized readability report:

  • 42% faster task completion

  • 67% fewer clarification requests

{"id":"docs-api-rest-api","title":"REST API","slug":"docs-api-rest-api","content":"Hypertask's public REST API is available at `https://app.hypertask.ai/api/v1`. Use it to list projects, create and update tasks, manage comments, assign users, read inbox notifications, and manage task drafts.

All requests and responses use JSON. Query parameters use `snake_case`. Some request body fields keep their existing API names, including `sectionId` and `userToAdd`; use the names shown in this reference. Task descriptions, comments, and drafts are **HTML**, not Markdown.

## Authentication

Send an API key in the `Authorization` header:

```bash
Authorization: Bearer htk_...
```

Create API keys in the Hypertask app with `Ctrl+K` -> `REST API`. Each user can have up to 10 active keys. The full key is shown once when it is created, and keys can be revoked from the same modal.

```bash
export HT_API_KEY=htk_...

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $HT_API_KEY" \
  "https://app.hypertask.ai/api/v1/user/context"
```

Error responses use this general shape:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Validation error",
  "message": "project_id must be a positive integer",
  "details": {
    "field": "project_id",
    "code": "invalid_type"
  }
}
```

## Error handling

Queries that include invalid date parameters receive API-level validation instead of server exceptions. For invalid or malformed `updated_since` filter values, the API returns HTTP 200 with a clear "invalid date" answer:

```http
200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "success": true,
  "data": [
    {
      "task_id": 123,
      "title": "Example task",
      "updated_at": "2026-08-01T10:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

Previously, malformed date filters triggered a server crash. Now, the API surface treats malformed dates as user input and handles them gracefully with a sanitized response, maintaining the HTTP 200 shape while clearly communicating that the filter value was not a valid date.

## Images in task descriptions and comments

When an API request writes a task description or comment that references an uploaded image or image link, the image appears inline by default. Set `inline_images` to `false` in the request to keep it as an attachment or link instead. Uploading images to someone else's comment adds attachments without changing their text.

## API validation for tasks

When creating or updating tasks, Hypertask validates required and optional fields at the API level. Invalid inputs return a 400 Bad Request instead of a 500 server error, making it easier for agents and clients to handle failures gracefully:

- Null or empty `description` values trigger validation errors with a clear message.
- Out-of-range values for numeric fields (for example, priority or estimate) are rejected with an explanatory error.
- The API also validates field types; sending a string where a number is expected returns `code: invalid_type` in the error details.

This behavior improves robustness of AI-driven workflows by surfacing actionable validation feedback rather than generic server errors.

Example: Invalid task description

```http
400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Validation error",
  "message": "description cannot be empty",
  "details": {
    "field": "description",
    "code": "required"
  }
}
```

Example: Out-of-range priority

```http
400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Validation error",
  "message": "priority must be between 0 and 4",
  "details": {
    "field": "priority",
    "code": "out_of_range",
    "value": 5
  }
}
```

## REST API structure and migration

Hypertask's REST API has completed its migration from the legacy Pages Router to the App Router. Writes for key resources (tasks, projects, sections, and notifications) now use the App Router exclusively. The old Routes have been retired once the new-structure flag was fully enabled, eliminating duplicate code paths and simplifying the codebase.

### Typed API client

**Benefits:**
- Full type safety across client implementations.
- Automatic validation via Zod, reducing runtime errors.
- Generated from a single source of truth (OpenAPI).

**Notes:**
- The new client uses shared contracts; existing utilities and parsers can depend on the same schemas.
- All derived clients now use the unified App Router endpoints.

### Router migration (final state)

All writes for these resources now use App Router endpoints:

```text
POST /api/v1/tasks              # create/update via App Router
POST /api/v1/projects
POST /api/v1/projects/:projectId/sections
POST /api/v1/notifications
```

The legacy Routes have been retired. The schema and response shapes remain the same as before; existing clients require no change.

### Sections and notifications (typed writes)

A typed writer now handles `sectionId` and `notificationId` parameters for sections and notifications, fully integrated with the App Router:

- **Sections:** Section creates, renames, moves, and deletes use the typed writer.
- **Notifications:** Reading, marking as unread, archiving, and unarchiving flows use the typed writer.

All these operations now proceed via the consolidated App Router endpoints.

### Session validated identity

Previously, several public API routes accepted an unsigned `nookies_user` cookie as the authenticated user identity. This has been tightened to prevent account takeover via forged cookies:

- Routes that set `nookies_user.id` now require a valid, matching signed `ht_session` cookie with the same `id` value to succeed.
- The following route families are affected:
  - Auth routes (e.g., `/api/auth/*`)
  - MCP routes (`/api/mcp/*`)
  - Other 64 public sub-paths previously relying on unsigned nookies_user
  - All associated webhook and logged-out call sites

Verified live on production: forging `nookies_user={"id":6}` now returns 401 instead of 200+ full data, and forging `{"id":1}` for any other user also returns 401.

Compatibility: The consensus across the auth, MCP, public, webhook, logged-out, and Bearer-auth request families is that this change does not affect existing integrations or tools:

- Auth requests with standard `Authorization: Bearer $HT_API_KEY` continue to work.
- MCP tools retain their same param schema.
- Public integrations that already manage `ht_session` via the app workload continue untouched.
- Work that previously shipped `nookies_user` directly (e.g., via server-to-server calls) should now explicitly sign or add `ht_session` with the same `id`, but it is a rare pattern in practice.

If your pattern relies on unsigned `nookies_user` outside these call sites, validate the signed session instead.

### Session paging (Rows)

When fetching sessions via the Sessions rows API and using `?prefer=paged=true`, response deltas are now computed from a session history paging key rather than from a historic row snapshot. This ensures accurate incremental updates across large session histories and makes pagination consistent with subsequent API changes on session detail and parent/subtask payloads. The same session history paging key is used to fetch selected transcripts via the `.transcripts` endpoint.

### Board detail and parent/subtask payloads

The board detail responses for the Sessions rows API and session detail endpoints now include parent and child subtask payloads directly in the board-level response. This makes it easier for clients to compute relationships and summaries without additional follow-up calls. Parent and child lists are arrays of child task objects (subtasks) always attached to the applicable session and board.

The App Router migration is now complete and the legacy Routes have been retired. For questions or edge cases during this transition, contact support or raise a ticket in Hypertask with your specific use case.","excerpt":"Complete reference for Hypertask's public REST API endpoints.","category":"Agents","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840366,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/api/rest-api/"}

##### Hello guided start

Call `hypertask_user_context` with `action: "hello"` for a guided start in MCP v2 (consolidated tools, on for Everyone). The legacy catalog exposes `hypertask_hello`. `GET https://mcp.hypertask.ai/api/mcp/hello` returns the same guide.

| Field | What it contains |
|-------|------------------|
| `agent` | The agent's `id` and `displayName`. It is `null` for a personal user token. |
| `startBoard` | The newest board across all boards the token can see, with `id`, `title`, and `boardUrl`. A missing title falls back to the short name. It is `null` when no board is available. |
| `nextSteps` | Three suggested steps for write agents, or two for read-only agents (no create step). No board means an empty list. Each has `step`, a CLI `command`, an MCP `tool`, and MCP `arguments`. |

Each step uses the tool name and argument shape advertised by `tools/list` for the same credential. For the fictional board Product Launch (`9142`), the default consolidated steps for a write agent are:

| Step | CLI command | MCP tool | MCP arguments |
|------|-------------|----------|---------------|
| See the board | `hypertask task list --project 9142` | `hypertask_tasks` | `{"action":"list","input":{"project_id":9142}}` |
| Create a first task | `hypertask task create --project 9142 --title "My first task"` | `hypertask_tasks` | `{"action":"create","input":{"project_id":9142,"title":"My first task"}}` |
| Read the board rules | `hypertask project playbook 9142` | `hypertask_projects` | `{"action":"playbook","input":{"project_id":9142}}` |

The legacy catalog instead uses `hypertask_list_tasks`, `hypertask_create_task`, and `hypertask_get_board_playbook`, with arguments at the top level (no `action` or `input` wrapper). Read-only agents receive only the list and playbook steps.

The tool description asks MCP clients to say who they are signed in as and offer these steps. For a write agent, for example: "Signed in as Claude Code (agent of Maria Lopez). Your board is Product Launch. Would you like to see the board, create a first task, or read the board rules?"

_Takes no parameters._

## Comments

### `hypertask_comments`

Does: List, add, edit, delete, pin or star ticket comments. Untyped agent notes stay hidden, including replies and mentions. Files require kind. Use question for decisions, qa for verdicts, or done for summaries. People comments use short plain sentences; technical details and status belong in the agent log. A hidden log post answers 202, not 201.
Use when: Use to discuss a ticket or inspect its conversation; list with include_activity also retrieves work history, and pin keeps one answer at the top. For a person to decide, add a ticket comment with a line starting Question: and @mention that person using a real mention, not just their name. The mention notification appears in their Inbox; when Decisions is enabled for them and the notification is visible, the unanswered ticket appears in Inbox, split Decisions: https://app.hypertask.ai/inbox?split=Decisions. A later non-agent comment by that person on the ticket removes it from Decisions. Ordinary mentions are not Decisions. Structured decision records are separate; creating one alone does not create this Question: + @mention workflow. Use a comment, not a page, to request a decision.
Do not use when: Do not use for ticket descriptions or unpublished drafts; use hypertask_tasks or hypertask_drafts instead.

{"id":"docs-changelog-index","title":"Changelog","slug":"docs-changelog-index","content":"## November 10, 2026

### New features

### Improvements

- Improved: Summarize the current task now says what the task is first, then where it stands, then up to three open points. It does not open with a next action.

## November 6, 2026

### Improvements

- Improved: An agent comment or new ticket is refused when it uses a dashed code name, quotes Valentin in plain quote marks, asks a Question in the wrong shape, or leaves out Problem, Fix, Done when, Risk, or Decision. People can still write those.

- Improved: When a provider rejects your own AI key, chat names that key instead of a generic error, and tells you to update it in Settings, under AI, Bring your own key.

## November 3, 2026

### Improvements

- Improved: Inbox rows use the whole line. The sender, ticket number and title sit together on the left with no fixed name column, and the grey preview runs up to the tags, so a short sender no longer leaves an empty gap. The preview leads with why the row is in your inbox, then the latest human comment, then the description, joined by a dot and cut at a whole word before the tags.

- Improved: The AI chat no longer opens by itself when you create a task. It opens when you open it and stays as you left it, on desktop and phone. The three automatic switches in **Settings > General > Task Page** are gone, because nothing opens on its own now.

- Improved: In the <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd> new task box, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Enter</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Enter</kbd> on a Mac) now creates the task and <kbd>Enter</kbd> starts a new paragraph. The hint under the box shows the new shortcut.

- Improved: Board cards now line up in a tidier rhythm. An unmarked card has even padding with no hidden stripe, a card you are working on or one marked as blocked keeps a single 4px stripe, card avatars are a little smaller, column titles sit on the same line as card text, and each column's scroll bar is a plain pill with no arrows. Every other view, the card colours and the way columns behave are unchanged.

## November 2, 2026

### Improvements

- Improved: The Ctrl+J New Task box now puts the microphone just left of a word **Create** button, and a **Dictation** pill takes its place while you speak. The key hints under the box are written in words and switch while dictation runs: `Ctrl Shift D` starts and stops, `Enter` stops and keeps your words, `Ctrl Enter` stops and creates the ticket, `Esc` cancels.

## October 30, 2026

### Improvements

- Improved: After Ctrl+J creates a ticket, the AI chat sidebar now shows up to three one-tap chips with next actions or open decisions based on your original note and your board's rules, instead of questions about wording. When nothing fits, no chips appear.

## October 24, 2026

### Improvements

- Improved: [Included AI now follows your team's plan](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/ai-features/#included-ai-allowance): Free gets a small starter AI allowance on fast budget models, Pro includes more AI on managed models with no keys needed, and BYOK uses your own model keys. Owners and board admins see percent used in Settings > AI Usage. Background AI shares the same allowance; calls on your own key do not use it. Demo chat requires a demo guest session.

- Improved: Choose where AI chat opens by itself with three switches in **Settings > General > Task Page**: on newly created tickets, when you open a ticket, and on boards. They work on desktop and phone and are saved to your account. **Keep AI chat closed always** and **Open AI chat by default** are replaced and carry over to the new switches.

## October 23, 2026

### New Features

- New: Select cards on your phone. Hold a card for about a second and let go to tick it and open the selection bar, then tap other cards to add them. Holding and dragging still moves a card, and a tap still opens it when nothing is selected.

## October 22, 2026

### New Features

- New: Click the hints below the textbox in the desktop Ctrl+J New Task window: Attach opens the file picker, Search opens search, and Board opens the board chooser. Your text stays in the box.

### Improvements

- Improved: After Ctrl+J creates a ticket, the questions and ideas in the AI chat sidebar now help you improve how the ticket is written: a clearer title, missing sections such as the goal or acceptance criteria, plainer wording, vague words to replace, or a missing screenshot or example. They no longer ask about the ticket's subject. Click one to send it in the same chat.

- Improved: Images now appear inline by default when Ctrl+J, AI chat, an MCP client, or the API writes a task description or comment that references an uploaded image or image link. Ask for "attachment only" or "link only" to keep it as an attachment or link. Uploading images to someone else's comment adds attachments without changing their text.

- Improved: In the desktop Ctrl+J New Task window, name the board in your note, for example "on the board Marketing" or "for the project Website", and the task is saved on that board. The board chip switches as you type, so you can see where it will go and change it. A board name without "for", "on", "in" or "to" in front is ignored.

- Improved: Enable **Keep AI chat closed always** in **Settings > General > Task Page** to stop docked AI chat opening automatically on tickets, boards, reloads, and after Ctrl+J task creation. You can still open chat manually, and find the setting by name in the command palette.

- Improved: On a ticket page, choose **Current ticket** in the docked AI chat's scope menu to focus on that ticket's title, description, and comments. The scope stays on **Current board** until you choose it and returns to **Current board** when you leave the ticket. Full-screen chat is unchanged.

- Improved: Slack-style search operators now autocomplete with consistent colours. Use `priority:` (urgent, high, medium, low) and `type:` (ticket, comment), or follow the search tips for `priority:high`, `type:ticket`, `"exact phrase"`, and `-word`. Quoted phrases and word exclusions stay plain text.

- Improved: Shortcut hints below the textbox in the desktop Ctrl+J New Task window now fit on one line. The "Esc Close" hint has been removed; Esc still closes the window.

## October 21, 2026

### Improvements

- Improved: After Ctrl+J creates a ticket, the AI chat sidebar shows 2 to 4 questions and improvement ideas written for that ticket. Click one to send it in the same chat.

## October 20, 2026

### Improvements

- Improved: The AI ticket writer follows the board's saved custom instructions in Ctrl+J compose, AI chat, and CLI/MCP. It keeps the section layout shared by past tickets, keeps sections short, and fills Number, Select, Text, Date, and Checkbox custom fields when instructions or past tickets show them. Values that do not fit the field are skipped.","excerpt":"Shipped improvements to Hypertask.","category":"Changelog","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840374,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/"}

{"id":"docs-cli-commands","title":"CLI Commands","slug":"docs-cli-commands","content":"**Source:** Hypertask CLI `hypertask 0.2.68 (zig)`.

**197 commands.** Run any command with `--help` for its current usage.

## `hypertask`

```text
hypertask 0.2.0 (zig), native Hypertask CLI

Usage: hypertask [--json] [--token <jwt>] [--api-url <url>] <command> ...

Run `hypertask capabilities --json` for the complete command and option catalog.
Agent sessions: run `hypertask chat listen` in the background; answer with `hypertask chat reply <chat-id> --text <text>`.
Run `hypertask help features` for live product features and their destinations.
A Question: comment that @mentions a person using a real mention shows up in their Inbox, split Decisions when enabled: https://app.hypertask.ai/inbox?split=Decisions.
Agent log: `hypertask activity add <ticket> --text <note>` writes it (no --kind, nobody is notified) and `hypertask task agent-log <ticket>` reads it.

AI agents: run `hypertask feedback --kind bug --tool "task get" "what went wrong"` on your own when a hypertask command fails unexpectedly. The kind and the note are kept on the filed ticket for our own team's agents and dropped for customer agents. Never include task, board or comment content.
Unexpected failures send command name and error type only, no task content; disable with HYPERTASK_NO_ERROR_REPORTS=1 or error_reports=false in ~/.hypertask/config.json.

Commands: feedback login logout status token update context teams presence decision user agent agents webhook admin capabilities help project labels section fields task draft search comment pages skills ai messages blockers inbox report time view chat
```

```text
Login to HyperTask via browser

Usage: hypertask login [options]

  --token <jwt>
      JWT token (skip browser auth)
  --code <code>
      Five-minute agent sign-in code

      API URL

      Show help
```

### Guided start after token login

```bash
hypertask login --token <token> --human
```

```text
Signed in as Claude Code (agent of Maria Lopez)
Board: Product Launch
https://app.hypertask.ai/project?id=9142

Next steps your agent can run now:
  1. See the board:          hypertask task list --project 9142
  2. Create a first task:    hypertask task create --project 9142 --title "My first task"
  3. Read the board rules:   hypertask project playbook 9142

Or just ask your agent: "What's on my Hypertask board?"
```

Token login checks the token right away. On success, it shows who you are signed in as and the newest board across all boards the token can see. A missing title falls back to the short name. The example above uses a fictional write agent and board.

The CLI prints the server's steps: read-only agents get two steps, list and playbook, with no create step. If no board is available, `--human` says "No board yet. Create one in your Hypertask web app."

JSON is the default output. It keeps `success`, `saved`, and `configPath`, and adds:

| Field | What it contains |
|-------|------------------|
| `signedInAs` | The signed-in identity, including `name`. |
| `board` | The board's `id`, `title`, and `url`. |
| `nextSteps` | The server's suggested steps (three for write agents, two for read-only agents, none without a board), each with a CLI `command`. |
| `moreBoards` | A hint to run `hypertask project list` when the token can see several boards. |

The CLI waits at most about 1.5 seconds for the guide. If it times out or fails because of a network or server error, login still saves the token. It returns the previous saved-token output without the guided start. Saving a token does not mean the check passed.

{"id":"docs-cli-reference","title":"CLI Reference","slug":"docs-cli-reference","content":"The native Hypertask CLI lets you manage tasks, projects, comments, and notifications from your terminal. The executable is named `hypertask`. The CLI ships as a native Zig binary (htz) and can also be installed via npm. Connecting an agent token? See [Connect a new agent](https://docs.hypertask.ai/connect-an-agent/). ## Find blockers ```bash hypertask blockers --user me hypertask blockers --user 123 --project 15 --project 42 --state waiting --json hypertask inbox list --waiting-on me ``` `blockers` lists tasks waiting on the chosen person across accessible boards. Use `me` or a numeric user ID with `--user`. Repeat `--project` to limit the results to specific board IDs, and add `--json` for JSON output. `hypertask inbox list --waiting-on me` is an alias. Each result includes the marked question, recommendation, task link, board and column, priority, and wait time. Filter with `--state`: - `waiting`: no human reply or reaction after the question. - `answered`: the chosen person replied after the question or reacted to it. - `no-question`: the task has no marked Question. These commands are read-only; they do not clear blockers. ## Install ### Via npm (recommended) ```bash npm install -g @hypertask/hypertask_cli@latest ``` This installs a lightweight npm shim that fetches and runs the official htz binary for your platform, ensuring you always have the latest version. ### Via curl (Linux / macOS) On Linux or macOS, run: ```bash curl -fsSL https://hypertask.ai/install | sh hypertask --version ``` The installer detects x64 or ARM64, downloads the matching binary from the latest [GitHub release](https://github.com/hypertask-ai/cli/releases), and verifies its SHA-256 checksum. It installs to `~/.local/bin` by default. Set `HYPERTASK_INSTALL_DIR` to choose another directory. ### Via PowerShell (Windows x64) On Windows x64, run in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://hypertask.ai/install.ps1 | iex hypertask --version ``` The installer downloads the native executable from the latest [GitHub release](https://github.com/hypertask-ai/cli/releases), verifies its SHA-256 checksum, installs it to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Hypertask` and adds that folder to your user `PATH`. Open a new terminal afterwards to run `hypertask` from anywhere. Set `HYPERTASK_INSTALL_DIR` to choose another directory. ### Fleet auto-install behavior When you merge a commit into the hypertask-ai/cli repository, the VPS fleet runs an automated install workflow: - The trusted runner builds the htz binary in ReleaseFast mode. - It preserves any existing symlinks under `~/.local/bin`. - It only considers the install successful after verifying the installed binary matches the freshly built commit. - Previous verifications and log metadata are retained to detect drift or mismatches. If an install does not succeed, the CI/CD pipeline fails and prevents the commit from being considered merged. ## Inside the Hypertask App When you choose to install Hypertask from the web app, the in-app installer (CLI install dialog) uses the npm shim to fetch the htz binary for you. This keeps the command identical across all install channels. ## General behaviour ### Unknown flags The CLI fails out loud for unrecognized flags and options. An unknown flag results in an error message and an exit code of 2 (non-zero), indicating a configuration or usage error. ```bash hypertask task get HYFA-70 --zzznotaflag 9 # unknown option: --zzznotaflag # exit code: 2 ``` ### Ticket commands ### Reading a ticket by number A bare number is an internal task id, so it can belong to any board. `hypertask task get 8263` names the ticket and board it did read, and when no task has that id it names the two shapes that reach the ticket: the ticket key, or `--project` with the board. ```bash hypertask task get 8263 # no task has id 8263. A bare number is a task id on any board; pass the ticket key, or --project with the board, when it is a ticket number hypertask task get 8263 --project 15 hypertask task get HTPR-8263 ``` ### Reading a ticket from its app link A ticket link copied from the address bar works wherever the CLI takes a ticket. The board and the ticket number are read from the link, so a pasted link does what `8263 --project 15` does. A `#comment-` anchor, a query string and later path segments are ignored, and a `--project` that names another board is refused instead of reading the wrong one. ```bash hypertask task get https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/8456 hypertask comment list https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/8456 --limit 5 ``` ### Comment text from a file `comment add --file ` reads the comment text from a file, and that file holds HTML, the same as `--text`. Add `--markdown` when the file holds Markdown instead. ```bash hypertask comment add HTPR-2992 --file comment.html ``` `--html-file` is not a `comment add` flag; it belongs to `report create` and `report update`. A wrong flag is refused with exit code 2, and the error lists the flags that command does accept. ### Unknown commands A command that does not exist is answered as a command: `hypertask task lst HYFA-70 --project 15` prints `unknown command: lst`, the commands that do exist, and `did you mean: list`, instead of blaming the flag that followed it. When the guessed word lives under another command, the answer says where the work is. From v0.2.35, `hypertask task comments HYFA-70` answers `unknown command: comments` and `a ticket's comments are read with: hypertask comment list `. A board's columns are sections, and the answer says so. From v0.2.36, `hypertask board --help` and `hypertask board sections --project 15` both answer `board columns are sections: hypertask section list --project `. The same version accepts `column` and `columns` as names for `section`, so `hypertask columns list --project 15` reads the columns. ```bash hypertask columns list --project 15 # same output as: hypertask section list --project 15 ``` ### Agent log An agent's work notes belong in a ticket's agent log, not in comments for people. `hypertask activity` is the same command as `hypertask comment`, so `activity add` writes that log: the note is saved and nobody is notified. ```bash hypertask activity add HTPR-1 --text "Checked the deploy log; the build passed." # Saved to the agent log (no comment, nobody notified). ``` Post a comment for people with `--kind question`, `qa` or `done`. Read the log back with `hypertask task agent-log `, and `hypertask activity last ` answers where the log is read instead of listing the comment commands. From v0.2.38. ### Ticket identifiers The two share one number range, so a bare number is the internal id, and that id can sit on any board. A read names the ticket it landed on: ```bash hypertask task get 1172 # 1172 is task id 1172: HTPR-481 on Hypertask. A bare number is an internal id on any board; # pass the ticket number, or --project with the board, when the board matters ``` A write cannot be undone, so a write that names a bare number writes nothing: ```bash hypertask activity add 1172 --text "note" # nothing was written: 1172 is task id 1172: HTPR-481 on Hypertask. # Pass the ticket number to write to the ticket, or id:1172 to write to that task # exit code: 2 ``` ticket number plus `--project `, or `id:` when you mean the internal id. This covers `comment add`, `activity add`, `task update`, `task assign`, `task unassign`, `task description restore` and `task inbox move`. ### Error reports From v0.2.18, when a command fails unexpectedly (a server error, a network problem, a response the CLI cannot read, or an internal error), the CLI sends Hypertask one short report so the failure becomes a bug ticket. The report holds only the command name (like `task create`), the error type, the HTTP status, the CLI version and your operating system. It never includes task content, ids, arguments or your token. Your own mistakes (an unknown flag, a missing task, no permission) are never reported. Reporting never changes the error message or exit code, and gives up after about 1.5 seconds. To turn it off, set `HYPERTASK_NO_ERROR_REPORTS=1`, or add `"error_reports": false` to `~/.hypertask/config.json`. ### v0.2.16 CLI Release (2026-10-12) This release fixes a crash when running AI reviews on large pull requests. The CLI now passes PR text to the review program through standard input instead of a command-line argument, preventing shell argument limits: - **No crash on large PRs:** AI review commands now work on arbitrarily large pull requests without hitting shell argument limits. - **Internal program path consistency:** The review program running on the server matches the code stored in the repository, verified in QA. To upgrade to v0.2.16: ```bash npm install -g @hypertask/hypertask_cli@latest hypertask --version ``` ### v0.2.15 CLI Release (2026-10-11) This release fixes a bug in agent emoji handling for CLI inbox operations. The CLI now correctly distinguishes between agent and human reactions: - Agent emoji reactions are no longer counted as human reactions in the CLI inbox. - Human reactions are no longer dropped when loading or processing inbox data. Previously, the CLI would treat an agent's emoji as if it came from a person, potentially causing selection or counting errors in inbox actions like bulk archive. This fix ensures accurate reaction tracking for agents monitoring tasks. To upgrade to v0.2.15: ```bash npm install -g @hypertask/hypertask_cli@latest hypertask --version ``` ### v0.2.19 CLI Release (2026-10-15) CLI 0.2.19 improves error reporting when network problems occur during command execution. - **Read retries and clearer errors:** If the server does not respond while the CLI waits, it now retries once and surfaces the actual error instead of a bare "ReadFailed" message. Use `--help` or the full command list (`hypertask capabilities --json`) to see available updates. This change applies to all commands that involve waiting for a server response, including task listing, task details, and other read operations. --- ## Task listing with label filters ### hypertask tasks list List tasks with optional filtering. ```bash hypertask tasks list [options] ``` **Options:** | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `--query ` | Free-text search. Same flag on every list command. | | `--filter ` | Repeatable structured filter. Keys: `priority`, `section`, `label`, `assignee`, `status`, `updated_since`, `has_pr`. | | `--sort ` | Sort, for example `updatedAt:desc`. | | `--fields ` | Return only these columns, for example `title,url`. | | `--labels ` | Filter tasks by one or more labels. | | `--limit ` | Max rows. | | `--cursor ` | Next page from the previous response. | | `--offset ` | Start listing from the Nth item (for paginated results). | **Behaviour:** - Returns a paginated list of tasks matching the specified filters. - Prefer `--query`, `--filter`, `--fields`, and `--limit` so one call stays small. - Use `--offset` or `--cursor` to walk large collections. ```bash hypertask tasks list --project 15 --filter section=AI Review --filter has_pr=red --fields title,url --limit 20 hypertask tasks list --labels cli,urgent ``` The `tasks list --labels` flag was previously a no-op. It now correctly filters tasks by the provided labels. The `--filter priority` option now accepts both priority names (`urgent`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `none`) and numeric values (0–4), matching the web UI and API. `none` matches tasks without an assigned priority. ## Task move ### hypertask tasks move Move a task from one section to another. This works within a board or across boards. ```bash hypertask tasks move --section hypertask tasks move --to hypertask tasks move --to --to-section ``` **Options:** | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `--section ` | Move the task to this section within the same board. | | `--to ` | Move the task to this board. Use `--to-section` to specify the target section in the new board. | | `--to-section ` | Specify the target section in the board given by `--to`. If omitted, the section defaults to "Backlog". | | `--assignee ` | Change the task's assignee instead of moving it. | **Behaviour:** - If the task is archived, the command fails with: > "Archived tasks cannot move sections or change assignees" - Use `--to ` to move a task to a different board, optionally with `--to-section` to specify a target section in the new board. - Use `--assignee ` to change the task's assignee without moving boards. ```bash # Move a task to another board (defaults to Backlog in the target board) hypertask tasks move INFRA-123 --to 15 # Move a task to another board and specific section hypertask tasks move INFRA-123 --to 15 --to-section 4060 # Move a task to a different section in the same board hypertask tasks move PRODUCT-456 --section "In Review" # Move a task and change its assignee hypertask tasks move PRODUCT-456 --assignee @valentin ``` The `comments add --improve` flag now correctly accepts a bare flag without a value and defaults to readability improvement. ## Project management errors are informative Bug fix Task creation now reports project membership failures with clear guidance instead of showing an internal server error or generic failure when the token lacks access. Previously, using a non-member token to create a task resulted in a generic "hypertask: the server could not complete the command" exit code 4. After this fix, the same command returns: ```bash # Using a token without project 5156 access hypertask task create --project 5156 --section Backlog # error: you are not a project member. Sign in with a valid account or use a token that has access to project 5156. # exit code: 4 ``` This makes CLI errors actionable for debugging out-of-scope work and bot configurations. --- ## Project management ### hypertask project update Update a project (board) by ID. To rename a board, use the `--title` flag: ```bash hypertask project update --title "" ``` **Options:** | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `--title ` | New board title. The title will be trimmed to non-empty and max 200 characters. | | `--description <description>` | Optional board description (HTML). | **Behaviour:** - Board members with write access can rename the board; non-members are blocked with a clear error. - Empty or overly long titles are rejected locally with a helpful message. - Only board members are allowed to update the board: an unknown board ID returns "not found", while a non-member receives "Not allowed to rename this board". ```bash # Rename a board by ID hypertask project update 4060 --title "Agents & Infra" # Update the description as well hypertask project update 4060 --title "Agents & Infra" --description "<p>Infrastructure-related tasks and boards.</p>" ``` <span class="label label--brand">Behavior change</span> Renaming a board from the app previously did not check board membership; agents and users could rename boards they were not members of. Board updates now require write access to the board. Only board members are allowed to update the board. --- You can also manage board columns and saved views with: - `hypertask view create` — Create a saved view. - `hypertask view list` — List saved views for a project. - `hypertask view switch <view-id>` — Switch to a saved view. For more options, run `hypertask project --help`, `hypertask view --help`, or `hypertask tasks --help`. Help names where a topic's help lives. `hypertask help project`, `hypertask project --help` and `hypertask --help project` all print that command's page, so a help request reaches any command, not only `features`. `hypertask help features` lists live product features, and `hypertask help` with no topic prints the top page, which ends with the list of commands. A topic that is not a command answers with where that help lives instead of `unknown command`. ## Delete a board from the CLI Only the board owner or a board admin can delete a board. Sign in to the CLI with an account or token that has that permission. Deletion removes the board and all its tasks. It cannot be undone through the CLI. Check the board ID before continuing. To keep the board for later, archive it instead. First, check the board you want to delete: ```bash hypertask project show <board-id> ``` Then delete it with explicit confirmation: ```bash hypertask project delete <board-id> --yes ``` Replace `<board-id>` with the board's numeric ID. Without `--yes`, the CLI refuses to delete it. Ordinary board membership is not enough. The board must be active. If it is archived, ask its owner to restore it before deleting: ```bash hypertask project archive <board-id> --restore ``` For a reversible alternative, the board owner can archive it: ```bash hypertask project archive <board-id> ```","excerpt":"Complete reference for the Hypertask CLI to manage tasks, projects, comments, and notifications from your terminal.","category":"Agents","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840387,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/reference/"}

{"id":"docs-cli-tasks-assign","title":"CLI Task Assignment","slug":"docs-cli-tasks-assign","content":"Assign users and agents to tasks, clear assignments, and manage workspace leases from the command line.

## Assign a task

### hypertask tasks assign

Assign a person or multiple people to tasks. Use the numeric list id that `tasks list` returns to operate on a specific task, or the `--all` flag to assign to an entire board.

```bash
hypertask tasks assign <ticket_number> --assignee <user-id>
```

```bash
hypertask tasks assign --project <board> --assignee <user-id> --all
```

**Behavior:**

- Adds the specified assignee to one or more tasks.
- When using `--all`, the assignee is added to every task on the board.

**Examples:**

Assign one person to a specific task listed from `tasks list`:

```bash
hypertask tasks assign 40451 --assignee valentin
```

Assign a person to the entire board:

```bash
hypertask tasks assign --project 15 --assignee valentin@team.com --all
```

Re-assigning the same user returns `already-assigned` without creating a duplicate assignment row.

## Clear all assignments

### Empty assignee

Clear a task's assignees by passing an empty string to `--assignee`.

**Behavior:**

- Removes every assignee from the specified task.
- Works with `--all` to clear all assignments from a board.
- Previously rejected as malformed input; now walks the existing unassign path.

**Examples:**

Clear a task's assignees:

```bash
hypertask task update 40451 --field "assignee" --value ""
```

Clear all assignments on a board:

```bash
hypertask tasks assign --project 15 --assignee "" --all
```

**Related:** `--clear-assignees` (see below).

### --clear-assignees flag

Clear a task's assignees using a explicit flag.

```bash
hypertask task update <ticket> --clear-assignees
```

**Behavior:**

- Removes all assignees from the ticket.
- Useful when you want to explicitly signal an unassignment.
- Performs the same operation as passing empty `--assignee`.

Shipped support for empty `--assignee` and `--clear-assignees` to clear all assignees on a task or board.

## Agent details

### hypertask agents get

Show details for a specific agent.

```bash
hypertask agents get --id <agent-id>
```

**Behavior:**

- Prints the agent's mission text, boards, creation time, and revoked state.
- Returns an error if no matching agent is found.
- Requires authentication.

Fixed the `UnknownCommand` error for `hypertask agents get --id`, allowing you to retrieve agent details from the CLI.

## Task claims

The released CLI does not expose a workspace-lease command. Use `hypertask agent take <ticket>` to claim an agent task; see the [generated commands](https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/commands/) for the released command surface.","excerpt":"Use hypertask tasks assign to assign tasks to agents or users.","category":"Agents","created_at":1792923238,"updated_at":1794840392,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/tasks-assign/"}

{"id":"docs-connect-an-agent","title":"Connect a new agent","slug":"docs-connect-an-agent","content":"Follow these steps to connect an AI agent to Hypertask.

1. **Create the agent.** Choose one path:
   - **Agent Chat:** Open [Agent Chat](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents/chat), choose **+ Add agent**, enter a name, and choose **Create**. This creates an agent with no boards and shows its token once. Copy it before choosing **Done**.
   - **From a board:** Open a team board, press **Ctrl+K**, and run **Create agent**. Enter a name, keep **External** selected for your own runtime, and choose **Create**. This adds the agent to that board and opens its agent page. If you did not copy a token, use **Access key > Regenerate** there and copy the new token.

2. **Store the token securely.** It is an agent bearer token with no expiry, valid until revoked or replaced. The agent page's **Access key** section has **Regenerate** and **Revoke** controls. The access key is for a managed agent's own identity, and connecting your own editor (VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code) uses your personal API key from **Settings** (gear icon) → **Connect** → **MCP** instead ([Authentication](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/overview/#authentication)). Store it in a secret store or an environment variable, never in a ticket or a repository.

3. **Give the agent board access.** The person who owns the agent opens [Agents](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents), opens the agent, expands **Board access**, and ticks each board it should work on. Changes save immediately. Turn the agent on first if it is disabled. **Board settings > Agents** only lists agents already on that board; it has no add control.

4. **Connect it.** Use the CLI or an MCP client.

Private agents are visible only to their owner. The owner must have access to the target board. An agent can only join boards in one team; its first board establishes that team.

A board read names that team. `hypertask project list` and `hypertask_projects` with `action: "list"` carry `teamId` on every row, so an agent can group the boards it can see by team before it adds one.

An agent cannot add itself to a board, whatever its role. Promoting it to admin does not fix onboarding. Admin agents can add other agents of the same owner only to boards they already belong to. Ask the agent's owner to grant access first.

### Add a board with the CLI

Run this as the agent's owner, using the owner's own login, not the agent token or an agent-bound connection:

```bash
hypertask agents update --id <agent UUID> --add-project <board id>
```

Use the agent UUID, not its display name, when inviting an agent through the CLI or MCP. See the [CLI reference](https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/commands/#hypertask-agents-update).

## CLI

```bash
npm i -g @hypertask/hypertask_cli
hypertask capabilities --json
```

`hypertask capabilities --json` lists every command the CLI supports. It does not authenticate. To act as the agent, pass the token:

```bash
export HT_TOKEN="<agent token>"
hypertask context
```

You can also pass `--token <agent token>` on a single command. `hypertask login --token <agent token>` works too, but it saves the token in `~/.hypertask/config.json`, so prefer the environment variable on shared machines. See the [CLI reference](https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/reference/).

### After token login

On a private machine, save the token and ask for readable output:

```bash
hypertask login --token <token> --human
```

The CLI prints the server's steps: read-only agents get two steps, list and playbook, with no create step. If no board is available, `--human` says "No board yet. Create one in your Hypertask web app."

Login checks the token right away. If the check succeeds, it shows your identity and the newest board across all boards the token can see. A missing title falls back to the short name. You can then ask your agent to run one of the steps.

Without `--human`, the output is JSON. It keeps `success`, `saved`, and `configPath`, and adds `signedInAs`, `board`, and `nextSteps`. If you can see several boards, `moreBoards` suggests `hypertask project list`. See the [login reference](https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/commands/#hypertask-login) for the fields.

The CLI waits at most about 1.5 seconds for the guide. If it times out or fails because of a network or server error, login still saves the token and shows the previous output. That saved-token message does not confirm the token is valid.

## MCP

Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <agent token>` to the MCP server. The [MCP overview](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/overview/) has client setup, and [Creating agents](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/agents/) shows the configuration snippet.

After connecting, ask your client to call `hypertask_user_context` with `action: "hello"` for a guided start. The reply includes the agent identity, a `startBoard`, and three `nextSteps` for write agents, or two for read-only agents (no create step). With a personal user token, `agent` is `null`. If no board is available, `startBoard` is `null` and `nextSteps` is empty.

The client is asked to say who it is signed in as and offer the returned steps: show the board, create a first task if allowed, or read the board rules. Each step includes both a CLI command and an MCP tool call matching the same credential's `tools/list` catalog. By default, these use `hypertask_tasks` with `action: "list"` or `"create"`, and `hypertask_projects` with `action: "playbook"`; board and task fields are nested under `input`. See the [hello reference](https://docs.hypertask.ai/api/tools-reference/#hello-guided-start).

## Open an agent chat from a ticket

Where agent sidebar chat is available, hover an agent mention or assignee and choose **Chat**. The agent's existing conversation opens beside the current ticket. The profile link still opens the agent page. Human contact cards keep their **Copy email** action.

## Troubleshooting

- **Agent is not a member of the board:** ask the person who owns the agent to grant access under **Agents > agent > Board access** (step 3). Changing its role will not add it to a board.
- **"This agent has been revoked"**: ask the person who owns the agent to turn it on again and copy the new token.
- **"This agent's token was replaced"**: someone regenerated the key. Use the current one.

Regenerating a key invalidates the old one immediately. Agent keys cannot be refreshed, only regenerated.","excerpt":"Create a Hypertask agent, copy its token, give it board access and connect it with the CLI or MCP.","category":"Agents","created_at":1792923239,"updated_at":1794840398,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/connect-an-agent/"}

{"id":"docs-features-agent-chat","title":"Agent Chat","slug":"docs-features-agent-chat","content":"Open [Agent Chat](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents/chat) to choose an agent or a shared board room.

## Choose context in a docked agent chat

When you chat with an agent beside a board or ticket, use the same context dropdown as regular AI Chat. Choose **Current board**, **Current ticket** on a ticket page, a pinned board, or **All boards**. See [docked chat scope](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/chat-board-filter/#docked-ai-chat-scope) for the scope choices.

Your selection goes to the agent with each message, so you can ask about the selected ticket or board without copying its reference into your message. Queued messages keep the context you chose when you sent them. The full-screen Agent Chat page is unchanged.

Agents only receive a context they can still open. If an agent loses access to a board, the board name and ticket title saved with an earlier message are dropped from what it reads next.

For agent builders: MCP chat endpoints include a structured `context` object with `scope` (`ticket`, `board`, or `all`), plus `project_id`, `task_id`, `ticket_number`, `title`, and `surface_path` where applicable. Agent-facing message text also starts with a `Context: ...` line. Chat webhooks carry the same information in `chat.context` and `chat.text`.

## Shared board agent rooms

A board room gives people and agents one shared conversation for a board. It is not a private chat with one agent. Only boards you can access appear in the room list.

1. Open **Agent Chat** and select **Board rooms**.
2. Choose your board. Its room opens automatically. The header lists the board's agents.
3. Write your message and select the send arrow. **Product Bot** receives each new message from a person. Ask it to bring in another agent by that agent's full display name.
4. Read the replies in the shared conversation. Select **Stop** beside an agent's working indicator to cancel its pending reply.

The board needs an active agent named **Product Bot** before you can send messages. If you see "Product Bot is not on this board", add that agent to the board first. Agents can pass work to other board agents by using their full display names in replies.

Include the task's reference from the board in your message when you want to discuss it. Agent replies linked to that task also appear in its activity.

Each exchange allows up to three agent replies. A room allows up to 50 agent replies per day. The header shows the turns used today. When the daily limit is reached, wait until midnight UTC to continue.

Select **Direct chats** to return to individual agents. On a phone, the back arrow returns to the board room list.

## Agent Chat on your phone

Agent Chat uses the full phone screen without the app's usual top bar or bottom tabs. In an open conversation, the header shows a back arrow and the agent's name.

1. Open **Agent Chat** on your phone and tap an agent.
2. Type in the message box. To dictate instead, tap the microphone and allow microphone access when asked. Review the transcribed text before sending.
3. Tap the send arrow to send your message.
4. Tap the back arrow beside the agent's name to return to the agent list and choose someone else.

If the agent is still working, your next message is queued instead of interrupting it. Use **Cancel** on a queued message to remove it. Use **Stop** beside the working indicator to stop waiting for the current reply.

With a keyboard, **Enter** sends a message. Use **Shift+Enter** for a new line. When task suggestions are open, **Enter** selects the highlighted task first.

The microphone is unavailable when Hypertask cannot identify a board for the agent. The send arrow is unavailable while voice input is recording or being transcribed.","excerpt":"Talk to agents on your phone or work with your board's agents in a shared room.","category":"Agents","created_at":1792923239,"updated_at":1794840403,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/agent-chat/"}

{"id":"docs-features-agents","title":"AI Agents","slug":"docs-features-agents","content":"Agents are autonomous workers that create, update, and manage tasks on your boards. They run as service accounts with scoped API keys and can act on their own behalf via bearer tokens. ## Create and configure agents Follow [Connect a new agent](https://docs.hypertask.ai/connect-an-agent/) for the full setup: 1. **Create:** In [Agent Chat](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents/chat), choose **+ Add agent**. This creates an agent with no boards and shows its token once. Alternatively, open a team board and use **Ctrl+K > Create agent** with **External** selected. That path adds the agent to the current board and opens its page. 2. **Copy the token:** Save the Chat token before closing the dialog. If you did not copy a token from board-based creation, use **Access key > Regenerate** on the agent page and copy the new token. The access key is for a managed agent's own identity, and connecting your own editor (VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code) uses your personal API key from **Settings** (gear icon) → **Connect** → **MCP** instead ([Authentication](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/overview/#authentication)). 3. **Add boards:** The person who owns the agent opens [Agents](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents), opens the agent, expands **Board access**, and ticks a board they can access. Turn the agent on first if disabled. Changes save immediately. **Board settings > Agents** only lists agents already attached; it has no add control. Private agents are visible only to their owner. An agent can only join boards in its team; the first board establishes that team. An agent cannot add itself to a board, whatever its role. Admin agents can add other agents of the same owner only on boards they already belong to. Do not promote an agent to admin to onboard it; ask its owner to grant access. For scripted setup, use the [CLI agent commands](https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/commands/#hypertask-agents-create). To add a board to an existing agent, run this with the owner's own login, not the agent token or an agent-bound connection: ```bash hypertask agents update --id --add-project ``` Agent invitations need the agent UUID, not its display name. If you open Agent Chat or list a team's agents and that team has none you can see, Hypertask adds a Hyper AI agent on a board of that team so the list is not empty. This also works when you can use the team but are not yet a member of a board. ## Agent status Agent pages show a single, consistent status. When Hyper AI agents are targeted via chat, they reflect **On demand** rather than **Offline**, because Hypertask launches them on demand to handle your request instead of running as background workers that report a status. Built-in Hyper AI agents are always **On demand** when you message them—their behavior changes from continuous background workers to on-demand launches. This means users won't see a persistent "Offline" status for these agents because they only appear when your conversation activates them. ## Board card agent status New. When you run an agent on a board, a small status chip appears on task cards showing: - **Agent name** — The agent performing the work. - **State** — e.g., "working" when the agent is actively updating tasks. - **Age** — How long since the agent last did something, displayed as "just now," "1m ago," "5m ago," etc. The status updates live with the card data and never triggers an extra request per card. Performance measurements show the chip does not make the board measurably slower. Watch the status chip on board cards to see how your agents are progressing through tasks in real time. ## Agent reactions New. Agents can receive emoji reactions on their comments. A thumb-up on an agent's comment reaches that agent immediately as a signal of acknowledgment or approval. When you respond with a reaction on an agent's comment (for example, ⬆️ or 👍), Hypertask sends that reaction to the targeted agent within seconds. The reaction appears on the task detail page and in the comment feed, and the agent receives the signal even if you're not both online. Agent reactions work across all platforms: desktop, mobile, and through APIs. The reaction is persistent and visible when you return to the task later. For security, reactions on agent comments stop counting toward flag-based triggers after the comment is edited. ## Agent notifications Improved. Agent notifications include mentions directed at agents (e.g., "Reply to @dev-bot"). These are handled with special guard-rules to prevent them from being incorrectly archived during snooze or reminder lookups. The system skips reminder validation when the notification is addressed to an agent, ensuring agent rows stay visible until you explicitly take action on them. ### Guest Hyper AI seeded notifications Fresh guest inboxes now receive 4 seeded notifications from a Hyper AI agent. When available, the Important split is enabled, helping new users immediately experience AI-driven prioritization. ### Agent Connected and First Task email messages Improved. Agent notifications now use a shared onboarding email design for: - **Your agent is connected** — Confirmation email when you sign up and connect an agent - **Your first task** — Email when a task is assigned to your newly connected agent These emails mirror your selected theme colors, typography, and layout tokens, so they match the look and feel of other in-boxed notifications. Subscribe to Agent notifications in your account settings or skip them entirely if you prefer list-only delivery. ## Clear refusals for invalid actions Improved. Agents that try to perform invalid or unauthorized actions now receive clear, early refusals instead of server errors. For example, if an agent attempts to archive a Done task that cannot be archived, it receives a specific “not allowed” message rather than a generic [HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/) response. This makes debugging agent workflows easier and prevents unexpected crashes during bulk operations. Check error messages from your agents when they're stuck—clear refusals point to permission issues, board and column permissions, or task storage states that limit what actions are available. ## Agent chat polling behavior Improved. Agent Chat now uses a simpler, direct method to check agent status instead of flag-driven polling. The previous feature flag for polling has been removed, and the system uses shorter, more consistent checks. Users experience reliable agent status updates without the hidden switch. ## Writing check Agent comments and new tickets are refused when they use a dashed code name, quote Valentin in plain quote marks, ask a Question in the wrong shape, or leave out Problem, Fix, Done when, Risk, or Decision. People can still write those. Put a code name in the agent log. Put his words in a quote block. A Question starts with What this is, then at most three plain points, then Question, My recommendation, Why, Yes, and No, each on its own line. ## Agent governance All agent activities are logged in the board's activity history. You can view who performed each action, when, and the tasks that were modified. This transparency helps teams audit agent workflows and resolve issues quickly.","excerpt":"Create, configure, and manage autonomous agents in Hypertask with MCP, webhooks, and scheduled vs ad-hoc workflows.","category":"Agents","created_at":1792923241,"updated_at":1794840413,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/agents/"}

{"id":"docs-features-agents-dashboard","title":"Agents Dashboard","slug":"docs-features-agents-dashboard","content":"# Agents Dashboard

The **Agents Dashboard** gives you a central view of your agents, including summary statistics, per-agent details, and board-scoped dashboards.

## Access the Agents Dashboard

- **URL**: `https://app.hypertask.ai/agents`
- From any page, use `Cmd+K` (Mac), `Ctrl+K` (Windows/Linux) and search for **"Go to Agents"**.

## Agent list by status

The overview page (`/agents`) groups your agents into three top-level sections:

- **Running** — agents currently active and executing tasks.
- **Quiet** — agents not currently running, but ready to start.
- **Off** — agents paused or stopped.

Each group displays agent cards showing key information.

## Agent cards

Each agent card shows:

- **Agent name** — the agent identifier.
- **Status** — Running, Quiet, or Off.
- **On/Off toggle** — pause or resume the agent.
- **Heartbeat line** for the merge/unblock timer.
- **Avatar** — a generated robot icon for each agent.

### Heartbeat line

The heartbeat line visualizes the agent's 10-minute merge/unblock check:

- **Green dot, short bar** — timer ran within the last 15 minutes.
- **Amber dot, medium bar** — timer ran between 15–30 minutes ago.
- **Red dot, no bar** — timer missed its 10-minute window or no data available.

### Card outlines

A red outline signals a **blocked** agent — no one is actively working on it. This helps you spot bottlenecks at a glance.

### Blocked-summary widget

A blocked-summary widget shows the number of agents currently blocked, helping you prioritize follow-up work.

## Board-scoped agent pages

Each board has its own dedicated agent page showing the agents configured for that board:

- **URL format**: `https://app.hypertask.ai/agents/<board-number>`
- Example: Board 5500 is available at `https://app.hypertask.ai/agents/5500`.

The board page includes:

- Board-specific agent list.
- Toolkit bug totals, including AGTE tickets tagged as bug.
- Configuration source: board, repository, branch, and agent list read from a shared setup.
- Main merge counts or reference links for the board.

Use board pages to inspect board-level agent health and bug tracking per board.

## Per-agent availability

All agents show generated robot avatars from their detail pages and the dashboard. This provides visual recognition without relying on initials or external icons.

### Agent examples

| Agent | Status |
|---|---|
| Preview Bot | Running |
| QA Agent | Quiet |
| Scheduler | Off |

## Performance and reliability

Use the agents page to:

- Spot which agents are actively working.
- Pause or resume agents consuming resources.
- Monitor agent distribution across workflows.
- Identify blocked agents via red outlines and the blocked-summary widget.

## MCP client evaluation frame

When the MCP client eval is enabled, the agents page displays a table of 20 real Hypertask tasks run through the MCP server and CLI. Each row shows pass/fail, token in/out, wall time, and tool call count. This helps you compare MCP to the CLI and catch regressions.

## Working with pages and task detail pages

Agents can reference task detail pages (e.g., `/detail/project-15/<ticket>`) via the production verifier, enabling them to verify lifecycles and create links as part of workflows.

## Troubleshooting

If you don't see an agent in the dashboard, check that:

1. The agent is connected to an active board.
2. The agent schedule has necessary permissions.
3. The agent is associated with your team or scope.

See [AI Agents](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/agents/) and [Scheduling Agents](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/scheduling/) for setup details.

---","excerpt":"View all your agents from a central dashboard, with detail pages for each agent, board-scoped view, and status toggles at a glance.","category":"Agents","created_at":1792923240,"updated_at":1794840408,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/agents-dashboard/"}

{"id":"docs-features-ai-chat-capabilities","title":"What AI chat can do","slug":"docs-features-ai-chat-capabilities","content":"Ask a product question for a documentation-backed answer.
For example: “How do I connect an agent?”
The answer should include its source article.

## Choose your surface

| Surface | Available tools | What it can change | Boundaries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Board sidebar | Board, ticket, comment, inbox, page, skill, agent, and time tools | Accessible tickets, comments, labels, assignments, pages, and supported board settings | The selected scope limits board context. Opening chat grants no extra permissions. |
| Full-screen chat | The same built-in tools as the sidebar | The same supported changes as the sidebar | A chat's scope still matters. Switching screens grants no extra access. |
| Floating chat | The same built-in tools as the sidebar | The same supported changes as the sidebar | Floating changes presentation, not permissions or tools. |
| Phone chat | Built-in chat tools | The same supported board changes | Small screens can use different controls. Tools still enforce account permissions. |
| Connected MCP client | Tools returned by that connection's tool list | Actions allowed by its token and role | Read-only agents cannot write. Clients choose how they use tool guidance. |
| CLI | Commands listed by `hypertask --help` | Supported commands allowed by its login | The CLI runs commands, not an assistant. Its calling agent chooses what to run. |

Built-in chat supports skills and task relationships.
Its tools are not an identical MCP catalogue.
For connection details, see [MCP Integration](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/overview/).
The [MCP Tools Reference](https://docs.hypertask.ai/api/tools-reference/) lists external tools.
The [CLI Reference](https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/commands/) lists available commands.

## Ask about the product

Product questions use the help search tool first.
This includes plans, prices, limits, shortcuts, and setup.
Answers should be short, with relevant article links.
They should not reproduce entire articles.

An undocumented feature is “not documented”, not promised.
You can ask to file a clarification ticket.
A failed lookup does not prove feature absence.

Questions about your work use board tools instead.
Examples include “Find my overdue tickets” or “Summarize comments”.
Help search does not search your private tickets.

## Clickable ticket answers

Ask chat to find your tickets or list recent work.
Answers can include ticket rows beneath a short explanation.
Rows show the title, status, assignees, and priority.
Select a row to open its ticket.
Each group starts with up to five rows.
Select **+N more** to expand that group.
Reopening a conversation refreshes ticket details and permissions.
Tickets you can no longer access disappear.

## Limits

- Chat cannot access boards your login cannot access.
- Tool availability can vary by role and connection.
- A missing tool cannot perform the requested action.
- Chat should explain that limitation, without claiming success.
- Bulk changes can require your explicit confirmation.
- A link does not prove navigation or saving.
- Attachments depend on model and supported file handling.
- Uploading an image does not guarantee image understanding.
- Chat cannot see your screen beyond supplied context.
- Documentation can lag behind newly released changes.

For everyday examples, see [AI Features](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/ai-features/).","excerpt":"Compare built-in chat, connected agents, and the CLI, including permissions and limits.","category":"Features & How-To","created_at":1794036335,"updated_at":1794840419,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/ai-chat-capabilities/"}

{"id":"docs-features-ai-features","title":"AI Features","slug":"docs-features-ai-features","content":"For tools and limits, see [What AI chat can do](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/ai-chat-capabilities/). AI is woven through every part of Hypertask — create tasks, filter your board, smart-label workloads, and manage daily operations without leaving the workflow you already use. 1. **AI-assisted task creation** - Click `AI` in the top-right corner of any board, open the `Ask Hypertask AI` panel, and describe a task in plain English. - AI parses the description and creates a task pre-assigned to you with a title, description, and relevant tags (task types, priorities, area). - Review the generated task before saving; edit fields or refine the prompt and generate again. 2. **Prompt-based filtering** - In the `Board Filter`, type natural-language constraints like: - `show me top-priority bugs` - `tasks assigned to Valentin and due this week` - Use combinations such as `high priority and not blocked`, and press `Enter` to apply. 3. **Smart labels** - Open a label (or the Manage Tags screen) and create a new label marked as a **smart label**. - In the "Smart label — AI keeps this label on matching tasks" field, define which tasks should carry it, for example: - `backend issue, involves DB, high impact` - Save; AI immediately classifies the board up to 500 existing tasks and adds the label to matches. Smart labels show a sparkle icon in label lists. - New tasks are classified when created; edited tasks are re-classified when title or description change; updating the prompt re-runs classification for the entire board. 4. **AI usage without a signed-in user** - AI usage can now be recorded and stored as usage tracks even when calls don't originate from a signed-in user. - This allows external agents or systems invoking the AI APIs to function without requiring active authentication, while still producing usage records available to admins. 5. **Batch-powered background workloads** - Background smart labels and other AI classification runs that involve many tasks are routed to Anthropic's Batch API at half price, allowing cost-efficient processing at scale. - Matching tasks receive their labels automatically; activity is logged in the task activity feed. - AI writes a compact representation of your content and sends it to the embed service, which can reject very long or empty text or refuse very long or empty text. On these failures, the upsert silently rotates the text and upserts without final vectors instead of failing, so comments and pages remain searchable with the relevant tags even when vectors aren't generated. - You don't see extra UI for this—it happens invisibly in the background with consistent results. 6. **AI Chat suggestions for tickets** - Open AI Chat in a ticket panel to get context-aware suggestions tailored to that ticket's specific information. - Previously, suggestions could be generic or fail entirely when the server returned "No output generated"; Haiku 5.5 now returns proper suggestions that match the ticket context. 7. **Faster agent task lists** - AI agents are now much quicker to load their task lists, especially after server warm-up. - Previously slow database reads that fetched task lists have been optimized: the slowest 5% of calls improved from ~129 ms down to ~40 ms. The improvement consistently benefits agents on both warm and cold servers, making AI-driven workflows feel far more responsive. 8. **AI Chat histories** - A spinner marks chats that are replying. The sidebar header and conversation list show it. Each chat keeps its own indicator. It disappears when replying finishes, fails, or stops. - Open AI Chat from the right rail or press `Ctrl/Cmd + I` to see a list of conversations. - In the full-screen chat view (desktop), the history list pages as the window resizes, and you scroll to load more older chats. Pick or filter from that list to open a chat. - On mobile, the list is limited; tap an entry to open its history. - The docked chat always shows your most recent chats inline; use the full-screen view for history navigation. - Your agents are listed in an **Agents** section at the top of the chat title list. Pick one to switch the chat to that agent's conversation in place. Its name shows in the chat title, and choosing it never sends a message. - You can also type `@` in the chat box. Agents are listed first, then boards and other items. Press `Enter` or click to add the agent as a chip and continue writing; nothing is sent until you press Send. - Drag the desktop chat edge to resize. Your account remembers this width in this browser. - Closing, reloading, and changing boards keep your choice. A narrow window temporarily reduces the displayed width. Widening restores your choice. 9. **Comment summaries preserve open questions** - When AI summarizes your comments, it now accurately reflects whether questions have been answered or remain unresolved. - Comment summaries display `Open: ...` for unanswered questions instead of inventing an answer, and retain "still unresolved" language when appropriate. 10. **Bulk archiving avoids server errors** - Agents that attempt to archive many tasks see a clear refusal message instead of a server crash. - An earlier incident had agents trying to archive 31 Done tickets per day, triggering a 500 error. The fix now returns a direct `not allowed` response, keeping workflows smooth and errors visible for observers. ## Run chats together Start a reply, then open another chat. Each chat replies independently. There is no two-chat limit. Existing usage limits still apply. Follow-ups wait only for their own chat. They send in order, even while you read another chat. Select **Stop** in a chat to stop that reply; other chats keep running. ### Keep a conversation across tickets Pin AI chat open in its menu, then open another ticket. Your selected conversation and earlier messages stay in the sidebar. New messages use the ticket you are viewing as context. Select **New chat** to start a separate conversation. Creating a ticket with the task writer puts that ticket's own introduction in the conversation you have open; it never opens the chat for you. ## Image generation removed Hypertask no longer generates new images. Existing images and uploads remain unchanged. Image generation is absent from team settings. Check **Settings → Team → Default models** and **AI features**. The **Ctrl+K** image generation shortcut was removed. Image model mentions were also removed. ## Where AI appears | Area | What AI does | |------|--------------| | **Task creation** | Parses your description into a task with title, description, priority, and tags. | | **Board filtering** | Understands natural-language constraints and builds dynamic filters. | | **Smart Labels** | Keeps labels on tasks that match your AI prompt; changes to tasks or the prompt trigger reclassification. | | **AI Chat** | Global assistant for questions, summarization, and quick actions, with full-screen history paging. | | **Ticket AI suggestions** | Provides context-specific suggestions in ticket panels that mirror the ticket's subject and related data. | | **Bulk AI workloads** | Heavy classification runs use the Batch API to handle large boards efficiently; background jobs go through Anthropic's half-price Batch endpoint. Usage is recorded as usage tracks regardless of whether a signed-in user is present. | | **Agent task lists** | Optimized reads for quick agent workloads; significant speedup for the slowest dataset slices. | | **Task summaries** | Summarize the current task says what the task is first, then where it stands, then up to three open points. It does not open with a next action. | | **Comment summaries** | Summarize comments and preserve whether questions remain open for human follow-up. | ## When the chat opens and closes The AI chat stays where you put it. - It opens when you open it, and closes when you close it. Moving between tickets, boards, My Tasks and the inbox leaves it as it was. - It keeps the same conversation while you move around a team. A new ticket no longer starts a new thread behind your back. - Creating a task leaves it as it was too. A closed chat stays closed; an open one stays open. - Reloading a tab keeps the state you left: open stays open, closed stays closed. ## Task creation with AI writer 1. **Open the New Task box** — Use Ctrl+J on desktop or Cmd+J to open the New Task creator from boards, the inbox, or any view. On the Tasks page, click **New Task** in the toolbar. To change the destination, press Ctrl+Shift+B (or Cmd+Shift+B on Mac). The board picker lists recently visited boards first, then sorts ties alphabetically. It remembers board visits in this browser. Search for a board and press Enter, or click its name. 2. **Describe your task** — Enter a brief description of the work you need done. You can type directly or let AI expand your ideas. The model chip under the note shows the model that will write the task: click it to pick another model or effort level, or use **Reset to default** to go back to the board's default. 3. **Let AI write the task** — Reviews your inputs and generates a complete, structured task with a title, description, priority, and relevant tags. AI respects your board's templates and style when available. 4. **Review and refine** — Edit any field in the generated task. You can press Ctrl+K (desktop) or Cmd+K (Mac) in the description area to refine the AI's work, regenerate, or add more detail. 5. **Save the task** — When you're satisfied, click **Create** (or Enter) to save the task and add it to the board. The task appears immediately in the appropriate column or section. 6. **Answer the follow-up questions** — The new task opens with the AI chat sidebar next to it.
