Under **Questions and ideas for this ticket**, it shows up to three one-tap chips based on your original note and your board's rules, such as a next action to take, a job to split out, or an open decision to settle. Click one to send it in the same chat. When nothing fits, no chips appear. ### Creating tickets through AI Chat Ask AI Chat to create a ticket. Its saved link appears before writing finishes. Open it while its description is being written. The finished title, description, priority and size follow. Saved title or description edits stop automatic replacement. If writing fails, the saved ticket remains. Chat tells you its description is unfinished. Finish that ticket instead of creating another. ### AI writer failure reasons Fix When the AI writer fails to generate a task, the **Ctrl+J New Task** box and the AI Task Writer now show you the real reason for the failure instead of hiding it. Your note is still saved as a task, so you don't lose your work: - **Error messages displayed** — Common errors like quota limits, missing context, or prompt format issues show explainable messages. - **Task created anyway** — Your original description or note is preserved as a task, so you can retry AI later or edit it manually. - **Applies everywhere** — This fix covers task creation from boards, the inbox, and when editing task descriptions. If AI generation is not available (for example, your team has not configured an AI key), the text you entered appears without modification, keeping your workflow uninterrupted. ### AI Task Writer The AI Task Writer is a prompt-based task creation flow that generates complete, shippable tickets from paste inputs. ### How it works today The Task Writer uses the board's saved [custom instructions](https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/settings-profile/#ai-settings) whenever you write a ticket with **Ctrl+J** compose, ask AI chat to **create a ticket**, or use the CLI/MCP task writer. - **Board format** — Keeps the section layout shared by past tickets, such as Problem, Hypothesis, Control, Variation, and a scoring section, while keeping each section short. - **Custom fields** — Fills the board's [Number, Select, Text, Date, and Checkbox fields](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/custom-fields/) when the instructions or past tickets show what to use. For example, a score field can match the score in the title. Values that do not fit the field are skipped. It also uses search to find related tickets instead of inventing them. ### Using the Task Writer - From a board: **Ctrl+J** / Cmd+J and select **Create with AI** — **Task Writer**. - From the command palette: **Ctrl+K** — search for "Task Write" and select it. - From a task: Click the AI icon in the task header and select **Task Writer**. After the Task Writer generates a draft, you can refine it just like any other AI-generated comment or description. When Ctrl+J or AI chat writes a task description or comment that references an uploaded image or image link, the image appears inline in the text by default. Ask for "attachment only" or "link only" to keep it as an attachment or link instead. ## Included AI allowance Free gets a small starter AI allowance on fast budget models. Pro includes more AI on managed models with no keys needed. BYOK uses your own model keys. Owners and board admins see percent used in **Settings > AI Usage**. Background AI, including smart labels and summaries, counts toward the same allowance as interactive AI when it uses Hypertask's key. Calls using [your own provider key](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/byok/) do not use the included allowance. When the included allowance is reached, further calls on Hypertask's key are refused. Your own-key calls can continue. Demo chat requires an active demo guest session. If prompted, start the demo again to keep chatting. ## When AI is not available Behavior change AI features now show clear guidance when a team does not have an AI key configured. Previously, teams without an AI key would see server errors when trying to use AI in agents or the CLI. Now, users receive a concise message directing them to add an AI key through the **Appearance & AI Models** settings page: > "AI features require an AI key. Configure your AI key in Appearance & AI Models." This applies to AI-powered task creation, filters, smart labels, and agent workflows that invoke AI. ## Settings - Choose your preferred AI model in the **Appearance & AI Models** settings page. Different models may produce different responses. - If a provider rejects your own AI key during chat, the message names that key and tells you to update it in **Settings**, then **AI**, then **Bring your own key**. - Adjust leniency of AI-assisted task creation in the same settings area if you prefer more precise or broader suggestions. - Smart label accuracy can be tuned by sharpening or relaxing your prompt; see the "How it stays current" details in the Smart Labels reference. Smart labels and prompts are a best-effort AI signal. They do not substitute for human review. Ensure your prompt manages edge cases or exceptions directly, for example: "NOT: schema changes on branches not yet merged." Use smart labels together with filters and saved views to create reusable patterns for recurring workloads (e.g., `on-call issues`, `quick fillers`, `enterprise integrations`).","excerpt":"AI-powered task creation, voice dictation, text enhancement, and an intelligent co-worker built into your workflow.","category":"AI & Productivity","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840423,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/ai-features/"}

{"id":"docs-features-ai-feedback-from-bot","title":"AI Feedback from a Bot Account","slug":"docs-features-ai-feedback-from-bot","content":"In Hypertask, events such as failed-login activity can be surfaced through an AI Feedback bot account. This account does not represent your personal identity; instead, it serves as a neutral feedback channel that system notifications can write to.

System-level alerts are no longer written directly to your account. Instead, they use the dedicated bot so clear separation exists between user workflow and event logging.

### What is the AI Feedback bot account?

- **Account:** [ai-feedback@crolab.org](mailto:ai-feedback@crolab.org)
- **Purpose:** File reports like failed-login activity for visibility in the team workspace.
- **Identity:** The account is labeled "AI Feedback". Nothing associated with failed-login events is written as your personal account name.

### Use cases

- **Incident logging:** Failed-login attempts can be recorded as structured reports without exposing user identity.
- **Observability:** Team leads and administrators can monitor security-related events through the bot channel without sifting through individual inboxes.

### How it works

When the server logs failed-login activity, the event is written through the AI Feedback bot. For clarity, users who experience a failed login are not notified about how the report appears; only that the report exists in the workspace. This design keeps user workflows uninterrupted while preserving the event log.

[Other AI Features](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/ai-features/)

    Explore other AI-powered features like task creation, smart labels, and AI agents.

[MCP Tools Reference](https://docs.hypertask.ai/api/tools-reference/)

    Review MCP tools you can use to interact with tasks, boards, and more.","excerpt":"Read reports and notifications from an AI Feedback bot account for events like failedlogin logins.","category":"AI & Productivity","created_at":1792971724,"updated_at":1794840428,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/ai-feedback-from-bot/"}

{"id":"docs-features-appearance","title":"Appearance & AI Models","slug":"docs-features-appearance","content":"## Appearance Settings

### Light and dark themes

Hypertask supports both light and dark themes, controlled from your profile or the Command Center.

- **Dark theme** — reduces eye strain when working in low-light environments and is ideal for long coding sessions.
- **Light theme** — provides high contrast for collaborative reviews and when sharing your screen.

You can toggle themes instantly from the settings menu. Preferences are saved per-user.

In AMOLED, floating AI chat has a thin outline and compact corners so it stays distinct from the black page, on desktop and phone. Other themes keep their existing appearance.

### Graphite 2

Choose **Graphite 2** in **Settings → Appearance**. Or open **Ctrl+K**, search **Graphite 2**, and press **Enter**.

Graphite 2 uses a quiet dark-grey palette, IBM Plex Sans, and Iconoir sidebar icons. Task titles use a lighter weight, while tags stay unfilled. Your choice survives a reload. **Dark · Graphite** and the other themes keep their existing appearance.

## Keyboard shortcuts

From the Command Center, use **Ctrl+K** to open the global command palette. While focusing on a task detail, you can also use:

- **Ctrl+O** — Open links from the latest reply in a new tab (Agent Chat and board comments).
- **Alt+Left/Right** — Navigate through tasks or agents in increasing or decreasing order.

These shortcuts are available across boards, chat panels, and the Agents overview.

Some shortcuts are also active in the main command palette when a compatible view is loaded.

## Text editor preferences

### Comments and descriptions

When composing comments or editing task descriptions, you can:

- Dictate **Ctrl+K**, **Ctrl+Space** (on supported browsers): Start voice dictation from the text field.
- Save **Ctrl+Enter**: Send the comment; the task may stay or advance depending on context.
- Open links **Ctrl+O**: When a reply includes a clickable link, open it in a new tab.

The comment composer is pinned to the bottom of task detail panels, keeping it accessible while you read and compose.

## AI models

### Model selection

Hypertask supports multiple AI providers and models. During configuration, agents operate with provider-specific model names. Agent Chat respects the engine configured on an agent:

- **Claude-based agents** use Claude models (for example, claude-sonnet-5).
- **Codex-based agents** use Codex models (for example, gpt-5.6-luna).

The chat lane configuration must align with the agent's engine.

**Claude Haiku 5.5** is the default AI model for everyone, on every plan. Some features, such as AI Task Writer, pick their own model.

To change your defaults, open **Settings → Default models**.

### Quiet mode

Quiet mode controls how agent activity appears in run activities and thread comments. It applies to agents in active runs:

- **Run activity** — by default, agents write detailed progress chatter to the run activity tab. Quiet mode suppresses most run activity logs.
- **Thread comments** — quiet mode disables comment generation. Comments are only posted for specific actions:
  - Question
  - Decision
  - Handoff
  - Done

When running in quiet mode, agents remain fully engaged, but their directional footprint in the task history is streamlined. To enable quiet mode, use the `quiet-run-activity` token or configure it via board-level agent settings.

Quiet mode is useful for workflow histories where you want to review agent behavior via structured run logs, but keep thread conversations focused on human decisions and actions.

## Icons, fonts, and visual tokens

### Sidebar icons

Icon visual standards are managed in the Typography & Sidebar Visuals page. Controlled strokes and consistent spacing ensure icons are legible across light and dark modes.

### Font scale

Typography uses a defined type scale for headlines, descriptions, and UI labels. Choose consistent weights and sizes from the standard set to maintain visual hierarchy.

### Component reuse checklist

When adding UI controls to the app, define the existing component being reused or provide a specific reason. This checklist applies to all UI pull requests and is enforced via the canonical guide and required gate. Each new control must be mapped to an underlying component or documented with a no-reuse justification.

Requests that reference or implement reusable components should include a mapping for each control added. Reviewers use the checklist to verify reusability claims and avoid unnecessary component proliferation.

---","excerpt":"Customize themes, icons, fonts, and select AI models for Hypertask.","category":"Settings & Preferences","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840432,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/appearance/"}

{"id":"docs-features-billing","title":"Billing & Seat Management","slug":"docs-features-billing","content":"Hypertask billing controls license capacity, seat limits, and access tiers. Manage seats, track costs, and safely test billing changes in production without risking database side effects.

## Your billing label in Stripe

Stripe uses your team name as the display name on invoices and in the billing portal. Hypertask never shows internal IDs or the word "undefined". For customers without a team name in the app, the owner's email appears instead. Previously blank or malformatted names are now filled from the team name or owner email; customers that have neither team name nor matching owner remain blank.

> Verify customer names in your Stripe billing portal. If a name appears blank, check that its owning team has a name and that a matching owner email exists.

## Seats

Seats represent active users with individual access to Hypertask. Each seat corresponds to a user with login credentials and full access to the platform features.

**Seat limits by plan:**
- Free plan: Unlimited members and unlimited open tickets. You can own up to 3 boards. Archived boards are not counted. A paid or comped plan has no board limit.
- Paid and team plans: Active seat limits per plan
- Enterprise: Custom seat limits

When you create or add accounts, new seats are allocated automatically. Upgrading your paid plan increases your seat capacity; unrestricted reassignments are tracked for billing reconciliation.

## Cost forecasting

The cost forecast shows estimated consumption for GitHub repositories connected to Hypertask. This view helps you anticipate file storage and integration costs before they hit your budget.

**View your forecast:**
1. Go to the **Cost Forecast** page
2. See per-repository estimates broken down by usage type
3. Compare projections against your current subscriptions

## Testing billing changes safely

Stripe test-mode harness lets you safely test billing flows in production without risking database writes or production incidents.

The test harness:
- Runs **guarded seat billing logic** in a controlled environment
- Uses **in-memory application state** so tests don't affect live data
- Implements **bounded cleanup** to discard test states after execution
- **Never writes to the Hypertask database** during test runs

This means you can safely iterate on seat-loss logic, billing entitlement checks, and upgrade/downgrade flows in production-like conditions without creating cross-tenant leakage or corrupting live seats.

## Seat loss and automatic repair

Automatic repair of lost seats is available in production for affected teams. This feature prevents silent seat loss when users pool in from other teams, and helps maintain billing accuracy.

**How automatic repair works:**
- Detects when active teams have fewer seats than their current plan supports
- Verifies that the team has a valid Stripe payment method on file
- Requires billing-owner input if the active subscription cannot identify a single safe replacement Stripe item, to avoid modifying the wrong subscription item
- Blocks automatic repair and prompts for billing-owner review if:
  - A Stripe item is stored but no longer valid
  - The active subscription does not contain exactly one safe replacement at the stored price
  - Automatic selection could modify the wrong subscription item

Only teams with a payment method on file are eligible for automatic repair, and repair operations are guarded against unsafe mutations to subscriptions.

## License management

Seat allocation follows consistent rules across surfaces:

- New user creation adds a seat to your allocation
- Adding teammates in the app, via CLI, or through API all respect the same capacity checks
- Free plan members are unlimited
- Upgrading your plan increases your tracked capacity and adds seats automatically within the new tier bounds

## Team ownership verification

All billing-affected endpoints now verify team ownership server-side before performing mutations:

| Endpoint | Change |
|----------|--------|
| Checkout session creation | Verifies the authenticated user has billing access to the team before creating a checkout URL |
| Task mutations | Reads billing authority from the authenticated user and enforces access checks before state changes |
| Comment operations | Validates the requesting user's access to the target board and task before posting |

This prevents client-controlled parameter mismatches from bypassing authorization and ensures operations are scoped only to the intended team's resources.

## Stripe customer operations

Stripe customer creation for new accounts now surfaces all errors rather than silently swallowing them. Previously, certain paths returned null on failure without indicating the underlying issue, making debugging difficult. All customer creation paths now properly report errors to help you identify and resolve account or payment configuration problems.","excerpt":"Add and manage seat licenses, view cost forecasts, and test billing flows safely.","category":"Collaboration & billing","created_at":1792923243,"updated_at":1794840437,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/billing/"}

{"id":"docs-features-board-settings","title":"Board Settings","slug":"docs-features-board-settings","content":"Use board settings to plan one board and control its automatic behavior. Set its target and milestones, post health updates, mute notifications, or configure archival, staleness, time tracking, and assignment rules. ## What this affects Board settings apply to individual boards on a project. They govern default behaviors that are applied consistently across tasks when rules are triggered: - **Archive actions** — Automatically archive old tasks or mark them for archival to keep your board clean. - **Project planning** — Set a target date, track milestones, and post the board's current health. - **Board notifications** — Mute ordinary inbox, email, and push notifications from this board only. - **Staleness rules** — Automatically detect tasks that have been idle for a set period and take action. - **Auto-assign rules** — Set per-column rules so new or unassigned tasks get attention where they belong. - **Time totals** — Optionally show accumulated tracked time on task cards and in table view. - **Synchronized IndexedDB defaults** — For authenticated Board and Table routes, the synchronized IndexedDB read model is now enabled by default to keep data in sync across opened tabs without manual refresh. You can still opt into the local model by using `?local_db=0` in the URL. Board settings are stored at the board level, so you can tailor behaviors per workflow. Changes here apply immediately; monitor the effect on your active tasks. ## Reach You can open board settings from: - **Ctrl+K command palette** — Search for **"Board settings"** and select your board. The board and team you opened from are now preselected. - **Board menu** — Open a board's menu and choose **Settings**. ```markdown Clear expired backlog and automate housekeeping. Identify tasks that haven't moved recently. Propagate responsibilities to unassigned cards. Keep data in sync across browsers by default for authenticated board and table routes. ``` ## Ticket prefix Each board has a deterministic ticket prefix (e.g., HTPR, YPER4, HYFA). Owners can rename the prefix from board settings without changing existing ticket numbers. Prefixes are 2–5 letters or digits, unique within the team, and appear as live previews. ### How to change a prefix From the app: 1. Open a board. 2. Click **Settings** > **Board** > **General**. 3. Find **Ticket prefix**. 4. Enter a new prefix (2–5 characters, letters or digits) and press Enter. 5. Old ticket IDs continue to resolve, so links, comments, and PRs that reference them stay accurate. From the CLI: ```bash hypertask project update --prefix NEWXY --project 15 ``` The prefix is editable on the **Create board** screen (defaulted to the automatic suggestion) and available to agents via the same `project update --prefix` flag. ### Discovering ticket prefix settings From the command palette, type **"ticket prefix"** to jump to this setting. The search returns **"Settings: Ticket prefix (board)"** for the current board. Use this to quickly locate the prefix configuration when you need to update it. ### Rationale - **Instant updates:** The displayed ID is built from the board's current prefix and the ticket's number, so changing the prefix is a quick update instead of rewriting every ticket. - **Backwards compatibility:** Old ticket IDs keep resolving via aliases, just like old numbers already do. - **Avoid clashes:** Moved tickets take the next free number, so prefixes and numbers never conflict, even after deleting tickets or changing prefixes. Prefixes are currently limited to these known values: HTPR, YPER4, and HYFA, which are used by existing agents. Changing those prefixes will require updating agent checks accordingly. ## Board notifications Open **Settings → Board → General**, then turn **Board notifications** off to mute one board. The change applies immediately and persists across refreshes. Muting a board stops its ordinary: - Inbox notifications, including snoozed items returning later. - Push notifications. - Immediate and digest emails. - Assignment, reaction, task-move, and due-date alerts. Your global notification channel settings stay unchanged, and other boards continue notifying you. Direct replies from managed agents still appear in your inbox so an explicit agent request can return its answer. Turn **Board notifications** on again whenever you want to resume delivery. ## Project planning Open **Settings → Board → Planning** to keep the board's outcome and current health in one place. - Set the board's **target date**. - Add dated **milestones**, then mark them complete as the project advances. - Post a short health update as **On track**, **At risk**, or **Off track**. - Review the 20 most recent updates with their author and timestamp. Any board member can read planning and post a health update. Only the board owner or an admin can change the target date or milestones. Target and milestone changes save immediately. Press **Ctrl+Enter** or **Cmd+Enter** to post a health update from the message field. ## Auto-archive Configure automatic archival of tasks that no longer require attention. Archive is different from deletion—it keeps history while removing items from the active view so you don't have to manually clean up stale columns. ### Available options Rules you can set per board: - **Enable auto-archive** — Turn the rule on/off. - **Archive after** — Choose how many days tasks remain before archival. - Common presets: 90, 120, 180, 365. - **Archive unused** — Automatically archive tasks that have not been touched recently (see Staleness). ### How it behaves When a task crosses your configured threshold: - The board removes the task from column counts. - Tasks are moved to the board's Archive section. - History (comments, attachments, subtasks) remains intact. Tasks in any column are eligible: backlog, in-progress, review, and so on. Use the **Archive after** setting on columns you keep as a long-running backlog. Combine with staleness for a two-layer cleanup rule. ## Set a column work limit Use a work limit to spot crowded columns without blocking task moves. 1. Open the board and click a column title. 2. In **Manage board columns**, open that column's settings. 3. Enter a positive whole number in **Work limit**. 4. Leave the field to save the limit. The column count shows active tasks / limit and turns red above the limit. The count includes active tasks hidden by filters. Archived and deleted tasks do not count. You can still create and move tasks when the column is over its limit. Clear **Work limit** to remove the limit. The limit belongs to the column, so saved views share it. ## Staleness detection Staleness rules keep track of active tasks that have not been moved, updated, or interacted with in a defined window. This helps surface forgotten items that might need re-evaluation or removal. Configuration: - **Stale after** — Number of days since the last change/due date. - Suggested ranges: 30, 60, 90. - **Auto-assign stale tasks** (Optional) — Toggle the rule that moves or re-assigns stale tasks to a specific column or assignee. - **Stale reminders** (Optional) — Get notified when tasks reach the staleness threshold so you can prioritize review or cleanup. When staleness is enabled, Kanban cards show the task's age on the board before its age in the current column. Fresh cards show muted ages. Cards become amber at the warning threshold and red at the hot threshold. Use Ctrl+K to toggle staleness for the board or the current view. ### Filtering stale vs healthy Every staleness filter is named so that typing **stale** in the filter menu finds all of them: - **Stale in column** — days since the task last changed column, falling back to its creation date if it has never moved. - **Stale without comment** — days since the last comment, falling back to creation if nobody has ever commented. - **Stale on board** — days since the task was created, regardless of activity (not affected by column moves or comments). - **Not stale** — the inverse: both the column age and the comment age are under the warn threshold. This deliberately ignores board age: a long-lived task that is still being moved and discussed is not stale. All four filters apply the per-board staleness threshold automatically, so a filtered board always agrees with the ages shown on the cards. Staleness only accounts for updates to the task record. Activities like commenting or toggling status updates the last-touch date automatically. ## Auto-assign rules Define rules that automatically assign or re-assign tasks to specific members. This is useful for ensuring that new pull requests, backlog items, or triage items land with the right people without manual overhead. ### Per-column auto-assign on column move In addition to setting a default for the entire board when a task is created or is unassigned, you can configure a per-column auto-assign rule: whenever a task is moved into this column, it will be assigned to the specified person or group. Ctrl+K "Auto-assign for this column" opens the per-column configuration. To configure per-column auto-assign: 1. From the board or section header, open the context menu (or use Ctrl+K "Auto-assign for this column") and select the section where you want the rule. 2. Pick an assignee (group or individual) to apply as tasks are moved into that column. The assignment is additive and idempotent—moving a task back into another column and then into this column again respects the rule. 3. When the rule applies, all tenants receive a notification and the assignee is messaged in the source channel if notifications are set up for the board. Auto-assign runs within the effective membership and session context enforced for board write access. Use board-visibility gating to control which users gain or retain write access to the board; ID-based attempts outside that context are scoped to the session owner's permissions. ### Calling auto-assign via CLI/MCP When auto-assign is triggered by CLI or MCP tools, the assignee lookup is evaluated in the context of the authenticated user or tool's session. Actions cannot be authorized by leases or background jobs outside that session; approvals are enforced through the board's membership and write-access model. ### How to configure (defaults) - **Target columns** — Specify which columns should apply auto-assign triggers: - Any column that can receive tasks (e.g., In Progress, Review). - **Assign to** — Select a project member or a role-based assignment: - Individual users. - Groups (e.g., "Testers," "Backend team"). - **Optional priority filter** — Apply only to tasks with certain priority levels (e.g., Urgent, High). ### Scenarios - **Backlog channel** — Assign new backlog items to reviewers or maintainers. - **Review overload** — Auto-assign completed items to QA reviewers when they become "In Review". - **Slack alerts** — Combine with board notifications to alert assignees when auto-assign runs. Pair auto-assign rules with open notifications (e.g., open issue in Slack team) to ensure assignees know their attention is needed without just silently moving cards. ## Autosave drafts Changes to board settings are saved automatically. If you navigate away or refresh the page, your settings persist: - **No manual save needed** — All toggles, number inputs, and column mappings are applied instantly. - **Revert behavior** — If you make a mistake, the board defaults (detected from project/staleness rules) can be used as a backup; update the offending rule and save again. ## Logging and history Hypertask tracks rule executions at the board level for review: - **Rule runs** — Historically, Hypertask logged rule runs to a log table (Admin role visible). - **Rule hygiene** — To keep logs manageable, Hypertask retains only recent rule executions (e.g., last 14–30 days) on the log table, while preserving a full backup in a more extensive repository for administrative use. Hygiene protects performance and schema stability over time. Project owners should rely on boards and historiques for governance rather than logs after a few days. ## Synced IndexedDB defaults You can choose between two read models for Boards and Tables: - **Synchronized IndexedDB (default)** — Active when no `?local_db=0` in the URL. Keeps data in sync across opened tabs and browsers smoothly, at the cost of higher CPU and a small memory overhead. Use this if you regularly open the same board in multiple tabs or devices. - **Local IndexedDB (optional)** — Activated by appending `?local_db=0` to the URL. Reads and writes stay in the local browser state, giving high performance with less CPU and a smaller footprint. Data may not reflect changes from other tabs or browsers until you reload. This defaults to the synchronized model for authenticated Board and Table routes. The system preserves the opt-out via URL flags, so local flow can still be opted into for testing or performance-sensitive workflows. ## Auto-error routing targeting Bugs When auto-error tickets are routed to sections, Hypertask now targets the exact Bugs section by default instead of the board's default column. This applies globally for boards with a specific Bugs section. Boards without a clearly defined Bugs section fall back to the current default section behavior. Changes take effect after board settings are saved. If you see Bugs incorrectly routed to another section, double-check that the Bugs section exists with a unique name and that you're using the latest board settings cache after this release.","excerpt":"Manage planning, notifications, auto-archive, staleness detection, time tracking, and per-column auto-assign rules.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840443,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/board-settings/"}

{"id":"docs-features-board-visibility","title":"Board & Subtask Visibility","slug":"docs-features-board-visibility","content":"Every board has a **Visibility** setting that controls which task and subtask encodings are exposed. This setting is applied consistently across all surfaces where a board is viewed or acted upon and can be overridden in the **Board hierarchy**. ## Board visibility modes A board's top-level setting is configured from the board's header, using **Ctrl+K** → "Edit board visibility" (or via the context menu). The available modes are: | Mode | Description | Conflicts with inherited | |--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------| | **Visible** | All task and subtask fields are shown. | No | | **Basic** | Only the `title` and `description` of tasks are shown. | Partial (core fields may still be inherited) | | **Dimmed** | Visibility applies to the owning team only (BYOK & free teams are effectively Hidden). | No (inherits from parent if permitted) | | **Hidden** | Layout shows only the owning team; other teams see an empty placeholder. | Only the owning team | ## Saved-view access control Security fix Saved-view endpoints now respect board membership data. Before requests are processed, Hypertask validates whether a user has access to the board that owns the saved view: - **Block access** – requests from users not on the board (including through chat API and MCP) are met with a `404 Not Found` result. - **Reject unauthorized reuse** – callers cannot rename, delete, or switch to saved views on boards they cannot access. - **Preserve their own data** – your own board still lists its saved views, exactly as before. This change ensures saved-view endpoints are scoped strictly, preventing cross-board data leakage through saved-view references or AI‑assisted view actions. ## Profile details in board detail answers Security fix Board detail answers now safely expose profile information. Before this fix, a board detail answer would show every profile field of the board owner and task assignees, including private details. After this fix: - **Private profile visibility** – Board members no longer see private profile details of the board owner or assignees. - **Limited exposure** – The old board detail answer now shows each person with only their `id`, `name`, and `photo`. - **Consistent behavior** – This applies to API responses that include profile details for tasks and owners, so public references (links, summaries, and views) respect the same privacy boundaries. ### Why this matters - Boards with strict visibility settings can share detail previews without leaking sensitive profile data. - Agents and MCP tools that query board details show profile data consistent with visible vs. hidden modes. - Saved-view and AI-chat integrations that render profiles stay within the same privacy model as other board filtering. ## Board access for reads Security fix Hypertask now properly restricts board-visible resources (tasks, pages, tables, and column names/settings) to users who have access to the board. Standard tasks, tables, and pages show only work that belongs to boards you are a member of. Before this fix: - **Page access leak** – a page would keep its old-board access even after its task moved to another board, so users without access to the new board could still open and search the page. - **Column visibility leak** – any logged-in user could read another board’s column names and settings, including through search filters and tables. - **Cross-board exhaust** – a board member could search across all boards and open test pages, exposing additional columns and configuration. After the fix: - **Moving a task moves its pages** – when you move a task to another board, its pages are now restricted to users with access to that board. Users who cannot see the new board cannot open or search the page. - **Columns are board-scoped** – columns and their associated layout/filter settings from boards you're not on are hidden. Only your boards contribute to search results and table columns. - **Search is scoped properly** – global search, filtered tables, and the search screen only return content you have board access to; cross-board data is filtered out at the backend. ### Why board-aware access matters - **Prevents unauthorized access** across unrelated workspaces at a single login. - **Aligns searches and tables** with your effective board memberships. - **Keeps pages in context** – pages follow their task and stay visible only to the people who can see the new board. ## Board access for writes All write paths consistently enforce membership-based access before mutating targets. Members cannot bypass access checks by switching identities or relying on CLI/MCP identities different from the session owner. This applies across CLI task and comment mutations (e.g., `task create`, `task update`, `comment add`), MCP task/comment tools (`board_update_task`, `board_add_comment`, `legacy_comment`), and the REST API (`board_update_task`, `board_add_comment`, and the legacy comment endpoint `/api/board/comment`). Write actions are now strictly tied to the authenticated user's session and the board's membership settings; no identity swap creates a separate write context. ### Why write gating matters - Matching access semantics between reads and writes prevents accidental cross-board updates. - Boards with constrained visibility (Basic, Dimmed) can rely on a stable access model even when multiple identities are involved. - CLI, MCP, and REST workflows stay aligned: no identity switch or hidden flag can bypass board membership checks. - Auto-assign and auto-archive operations are restricted to the effective membership context; claims or leases cannot authorize actions outside the session owner's permissions. You can read more about access control for downloads in the [Images and Attachments](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/images/) documentation, which documents that files are only reachable for people who see the parent ticket. ## Rail and sidebar behavior When you disable the **Rail** (sidebar) in Appearance settings, the following applies: - **Rendering**: On client-side hydration, the rail is immediately hidden. Before hydration completes, an early SSR pass may briefly render it alongside the main view. - **User-visible fix**: Rail-off users no longer see this flash during page load. After the initial SSR render is removed under strict hydration guards, the UI stabilizes without the rail ever being visible. - **Consistency**: The rail-off state is enforced across all pages and views, ensuring a clean workspace for users who prefer a focused, rail-free app surface. --- ## Why use visibility modes? - **Free and BYOK users** set a board to **Dimmed** so only the owning team sees its tasks. People on other teams see placeholders. Invitees join as an Admin or a Member. - **Boards that are shared externally** may set visibility to **Basic** to limit detailed data that isn't relevant to external collaborators. - **Bot agents and scheduled MCP pipelines** may use **Disabled** subtask visibility in saved views to reduce payload size and operational noise. - **Kanban vs table layout compatibility**—low-detail modes ensure consistent views regardless of whether you are looking at cards or a table, without changing board-level visibility. --- ## Keyboard shortcuts From a board's header: - **Ctrl+K** → **Edit board visibility** (opens a context menu with the four board modes) - **Ctrl+K** → **Save view** (creates or updates a saved view with any displaySubtasks mode) From any board or task list: - **Ctrl+S** (on a view) → **Save as view** (opens a dialog; includes a **Display subtasks** toggle) ## References
Browse features
[Tasks](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/tasks/) [Appearance & AI Models](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/appearance/)
","excerpt":"Configure which tasks and subtasks are visible to users across boards, saved views, tables, and AI Chat.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1792923244,"updated_at":1794840447,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/board-visibility/"}

{"id":"docs-features-boards","title":"Boards & Sections","slug":"docs-features-boards","content":"## Board access, invites, and permissions ### Board invites and access Security fix Sharing access to a board now respects team boundaries. A board invite: - Only adds the signed-in person to the board that generated the invite. - Is refused when no login is provided. - Is refused if the invite target board differs from the invite source board. - Can only be resended by the board's owner and current members. **Behavior before this fix:** An invite could be successfully resent and used to create tickets on a different board, potentially exposing cross-team data. **After this fix:** Each board's access is gated strictly. Invites can only be resent and used within their intended context. Users outside the board's membership cannot leverage invites to access or create tickets on other boards. This change ensures invites are a scoped, safe method to grant board-level access without exposing cross-team boundaries. ### Adding columns and sections Security fix Adding columns to a board is now restricted to board members only. A signed-in person who is not a member of the board's membership will be refused when attempting to add a column. **Behavior before this fix:** An unauthorized user could add columns to a board they were not part of, potentially affecting multiple team areas. **After this fix:** Only board members (including board owners, members, and invited participants with valid access) can add columns. This restriction aligns with the board-wide access model and ensures that board structure changes are controlled within the intended team context. ### "Board unavailable" error screen handling Fix The "Return to previous board" button now safely handles the "This board or ticket is unavailable" error screen. **Before this fix:** Clicking the "Return to previous board" button while encountering an unavailable board would trigger an immediate server request that caused the browser to crash. **After this fix:** The button gracefully handles the unavailable state without crashing. Users can safely return to their previous board or navigate to another area of Hypertask without encountering errors. ## Creating a board ## Quick add with N Use quick add when you only need a task title. It works in both board and table views. 1. Open your board and point at the column where you want to add work. Focus a column or select a task in it if you prefer. 2. Press **N**. A small title box opens in the column under your pointer. Move the pointer off the board and it uses the focused column, then the selected task's column, then the first column. In table view, it uses the selected row's section or the first section. 3. Type a title and press **Enter** to create the task. 4. Press **Escape** to close the box without creating another task. You can also open quick add with a column's **+** button. Press **C** to open the full task editor instead. **Shift+C** no longer opens quick add. The shortcuts do not run while you are typing in a field or while a dialog or command palette is open. ## Select cards on your phone On a phone, hold a card for about a second and let go without moving your finger. The card gets a tick and the selection bar opens at the bottom, with archive, assign, labels, move and more actions. - While cards are selected, tap another card to add it, or tap a ticked card to remove it. - Hold a card and drag it to move it, as before. Dragging never selects a card. - When no card is selected, a tap opens the card as usual. ## Archive every ticket in one column 1. Open your board, then open Commands (**Ctrl+K**). 2. Choose **Archive all tickets in a column**. 3. Pick a column. Check its exact ticket count. 4. Choose **Archive tickets**, or **Cancel**. The count includes tickets hidden by view filters. Other columns stay unchanged. Nothing is permanently deleted. Tickets moved since confirmation stay unchanged, too. Individual refusals do not stop the other tickets. Use the result's **Undo** to restore successful archives. ## Find tickets waiting on you Every board includes **Blocked by me**. Open the view from the board's view tabs on desktop, or the view picker on your phone. The view shows tickets where you are marked as the blocker. Tickets blocked by someone else, tickets without a blocker, and task dependencies alone stay out. Clearing or changing the blocker updates the view. Each person sees their own tickets, so there is no filter to create or save. ## Mark the comment that explains a block A ticket can name the person who blocks it, and one comment can carry the reason. That comment is the blocker comment. 1. Hover the comment, then click the **More** button (three dots) that appears at its right end. The command menu opens for that comment. 2. Choose **Mark as blocker**. 3. The comment gets a red frame. Choose **Unmark as blocker** to take it away. Only a real comment can carry the frame; activity rows cannot. One ticket has at most one blocker comment. Marking a second comment moves the frame. Agents use the same marker from the command line. The blocker comment and the blocking person are separate, so one can be set without the other: ```bash hypertask task blocker-comment HTPR-123 --comment-id 456 hypertask task waiting-on HTPR-123 --user 6 ``` An agent that clears a blocker records why it did, so the ticket keeps a note of who cleared it. ## Find tickets created by an agent 1. Open your board's filters with **Shift+F**. 2. Choose **Created by**, then an agent. 3. Save the view to keep this filter. Only tickets created by that agent appear. Choosing a person excludes their agents' tickets. Combine filters using **Match ANY** or **Match ALL**. This also works in the board's table layout. Calendar and My Tasks keep existing creator choices.","excerpt":"Organize work with Kanban-style boards, customizable sections, and multiple views.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840452,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/boards/"}

{"id":"docs-features-byok","title":"Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)","slug":"docs-features-byok","content":"BYOK lets you bring your own API keys and providers directly into Hypertask. Add keys from providers like Vercel, add custom endpoints, and manage provider keys across your workspace.

## Add a Provider Key

Add a key from any supported provider directly in your workspace:

1. Open the **Board** menu (···K or click the board icon)
2. Select **Board settings** or go to **Settings > Keys & providers**
3. Click **Add provider** and choose from the available options, or paste a provider URL for custom endpoints

## Supported Providers

Hypertask supports the following provider types:

- **Vercel** — Gateway keys for deployments and integrations
- **GitHub** — Token-based authentication for repository access
- **Custom endpoints** — Self-hosted or third-party services via HTTPS

Provider access is tied to your project-level permissions. Only owners and admins can add or remove keys for a project.

## Provider interchangeability

Agents can use interchangeable provider implementations for AI operations. The current overriding provider must be defined per-run by specifying an absolute provider URL. This may be a built-in (e.g., https://claude.com or https://codex.com) or a custom endpoint. Valid URLs are validated on input and persisted where applicable.

After providing a URL and verifying it, the provider becomes active for that run. Agent workflows using MCP tools or external schedulers can reference this provider URL to guarantee consistent model selection and access control across runs—no manual command-line environment variable overwrite is required when a provider URL is configured.

## GDPR-safe mode

Enable GDPR-safe mode to remove all China-hosted providers from your configuration across the platform. This toggle removes providers from settings and selectors and rejects BYOK keys that list China-hosted endpoints. The setting applies globally to your team workspace and persists across devices.

### How GDPR-safe mode works

When you enable GDPR-safe mode:

- **China-hosted providers are rejected:** Keys and custom endpoints pointing to providers hosted in China (e.g., Alibaba Cloud regions, Tencent Cloud regions) are removed from your saved configuration and cannot be used.
- **Settings and selectors are cleaned:** China-hosted entries are removed from settings, preference selectors, and validation flows.
- **BYOK validation:** By adding a new key with a China-hosted endpoint, the validation endpoint rejects it and surfaces a clear error.
- **System-wide impact:** Features like Gateway fallback and backend latency optimization climb back to non-China endpoints when available.

### Enabling GDPR-safe mode

To enable, go to **Settings > Privacy** and toggle **GDPR-safe mode** on. The change takes effect immediately and persists for your team.

GDPR-safe mode does not affect regions outside of China. It specifically targets providers and endpoints hosted within mainland China.

## Managing Your Keys

After adding a key, each provider row displays:

| Control | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Test button** | Verify the key works with the provider before saving |
| **Edit** | Update key details or change provider configuration |
| **Remove** | Delete the key (requires confirmation) |

### Test Provider Keys

Use the **Test button** next to any provider key to verify connectivity and authentication:

1. Click **Test** on the provider row
2. The system sends a quick validation request to confirm access
3. View the result—**success** confirms the key works, **error** shows configuration issues

Re-test after changing keys, switching domains, or updating provider credentials.

## Vercel Gateway Keys

Add Vercel gateway keys for deployments, edge functions, and related services:

1. Select **Vercel** from the provider list in Settings
2. Paste your Vercel **Personal Access Token** or specific project token
3. Click **Test** to verify the key's scopes
4. Save to add the key to your provider configuration

Vercel keys function similar to other provider keys—they're used for API access and integration with Vercel-powered features.

## Custom Endpoints

Bring key-based providers or self-hosted services into Hypertask by adding a custom endpoint:

1. Choose **Custom endpoint** as the provider type
2. Enter the endpoint URL (HTTPS only)
3. Provide any required headers, API keys, or bearer tokens
4. Click **Test** to confirm the endpoint is accessible
5. Save the configuration for reuse across your projects

Custom endpoints are stored securely and tied to your account and project access levels.

## Ephemeral per-turn provider home

During agent agent runs that connect to a provider home, each turn creates an ephemeral directory for that turn. The provider home is scoped to the current turn and doesn't persist across turns. Before each turn starts:

- Every path in the provider home is scanned
- Paths matching the resumable allowlist are preserved (these are expected, safe files such as state resumed from a previous turn)
- All other paths are deleted immediately (including any provider-created cache files that may have been written to the home)

By wiping the provider home outside the allowlist at run start, Hypertask ensures that stale cache files and provider-specific junk do not accumulate. Provider favorites that need to be preserved for resume already belong to the resumable allowlist; other files are cleared out to keep the environment clean.

This behavior aligns with how you'd set up a provider home manually on your system: prepare the directory for a specific run and clean up loose files afterwards, without keeping things around across unrelated work.

If you see unexpected cache files being cleaned up, check the resumable allowlist—anything else in the provider home that is not explicitly expected for resume will be removed at each run start.

## Key Security and Access

BYOK keys in Hypertask are managed with these principles:

- **Server-side storage** — Keys are stored on Hypertask infrastructure and never exposed to third-party providers beyond what's needed for authentication
- **Per-project scoping** — Providers and keys are tied to specific projects, limiting cross-project key sharing
- **Access controls** — Only owners and admins can view, add, or remove provider keys
- **No cross-board leakage** — Keys from one project/board are not visible or accessible from another

Never share keys between projects. If a team needs access to a provider key, have an admin add it directly rather than copying the token across accounts.

## Using Provider Keys

Once configured, provider keys are used automatically:

- **AI agents** — Available when making provider-specific API calls
- **Workflows** — Integrated into agent runs that require provider authentication
- **CLI tools** — References provider keys from your account when making authenticated requests

You don't need to manually invoke provider keys. They're selected automatically based on your current context and permissions.

Stakeholders — please review and reply with corrections or missing context.","excerpt":"Add and manage your own API keys and providers directly in Hypertask.","category":"Collaboration & billing","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840457,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/byok/"}

{"id":"docs-features-calendar","title":"Calendar","slug":"docs-features-calendar","content":"The calendar at `/calendar` shows every task with a due date across your boards. Filter which boards and people are included from the boards panel, and save any combination as a reusable view.

You can enshrine your preferred weekday start and weekend visibility by saving a preset, or rely on the default behavior for a fresh calendar.

## Default behavior

When you open a calendar without a saved preference:

- **Week starts on Monday** (Day and Week views show Monday through Friday; weekends are not shown). If you prefer Sunday as the starting day or want to show weekend rows, change your preference in Settings.
- **Weekend days are hidden in Week view** (you still see Monday through Friday). If you prefer to see the full week including Saturday and Sunday, adjust your preference in Settings.

To change your default weekday start or weekend visibility, go to Settings and set your preferred options. Controls are surfaced via <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> commands (if configured).

## Managing calendar views

Default views include Day, Week, Month, My Tasks, Overdue, Blocked, and Agents. All default views are ordinary orderable views: you can drag them anywhere in the view cluster, including up to an earlier row. You can also show each default view in Manage views (drag + hide) and reorder it alongside saved custom views.

From **Manage calendar views**, you can rename any calendar view that you own. Owned views show a settings affordance that lets you edit the name. Teammate-owned views are locked and cannot be renamed. The modal includes a clear close/back control for safe, deliberate switching between saved and owned views.

## Views

Switch views from the dropdown at the top left (or press <kbd>W</kbd> for week, <kbd>M</kbd> for month):

- **Day**: full-width table layout with tasks as rows. Use <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>D</kbd> to switch to day view. On desktop, Day view now includes a weekday-selector strip above the calendar. To jump to a specific weekday, click any weekday label in the strip. Keyboards actions <kbd>U</kbd> and <kbd>I</kbd> move to previous/next day; <kbd>T</kbd> jumps to today; <kbd>Tab</kbd> and <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> move focus; <kbd>Shift</kbd>+arrows reschedule the focused task.
- **Week**: five columns with hidden weekends (by default), or seven columns if you show weekends.
- **Month**: the classic grid.

## Shareable links

The calendar URL always encodes what you are looking at:

```
https://app.hypertask.ai/calendar?view=day&date=2026-07-31
```

- `view` is `day`, `week`, or `month`.
- `date` is the anchor day in `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Copy a link at any time to share exactly the same view and date. Open a shared link to land on that day's specific view, regardless of the recipient's own last-used calendar state. Links with invalid dates fall back to the recipient's own calendar.

For agents: construct these URLs directly when pointing a person at a specific day or week, e.g. `https://app.hypertask.ai/calendar?view=week&date=2026-08-03`.

## Week strip month expander

In the Week view, a month expander lets you quickly jump to any month. When you change days or weeks using arrows or navigation controls, the picker now stays in sync with your current view instead of remembering the month it opened with.

## Rendering reliability

The calendar renders reliably in production even when a persisted user state is null. Server-side identity-dependent calendar filters use the validated account ID passed from the server boundary, preventing SSR crashes on boards with missing user configurations.

## Legacy image support

If your board has historical images stored with an old S3 host configuration, the calendar no longer crashes when loading those images. Hypertask now accepts legacy bucket hosts in `next.config` remotePatterns, so old images load without bringing down the entire page. Requesting an official image migration, which will rewrite stored URLs to `files.hypertask.app`, remains a separate data cleanup effort. The calendar now works smoothly even when some images are still on an old host.

## Blocked tasks

Blocked tasks now stand out in Calendar. Month, week, and day views show the same red left edge as the board, making it easy to spot bottlenecks at a glance without switching to your board view.

On mobile agenda cards, blocked tasks now show the person blocking them with a red chip. This chip appears on both blocked and unblocked calendar agenda rows, so you can always see who's holding up work at a glance.

---","excerpt":"Day, week, and month views, keyboard navigation, and shareable calendar links.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840462,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/calendar/"}

{"id":"docs-features-chat-board-filter","title":"AI Chat Board Filter","slug":"docs-features-chat-board-filter","content":"Use the board filter in AI Chat to quickly focus on chats from one board, or view all chats across your boards. Set a default to start side by side.

## Docked AI chat scope

Use the scope menu in the docked AI chat to choose what the conversation is about:

- **Current board** — the default scope; focuses on the board you are viewing.
- **Current ticket** — available on a ticket page; focuses on that ticket's title, description, and comments. The scope stays on **Current board** until you choose **Current ticket**, and switches back to **Current board** when you leave the ticket.
- **Pinned boards** — choose a pinned board as the scope.
- **All boards** — includes all your accessible boards.

**Current ticket** is only available in the docked chat on a ticket page. The full-screen chat page is unchanged.

## When AI chat opens

The docked AI chat no longer opens by itself. It opens when you open it, and it stays where you left it as you move between tickets, boards, My Tasks and the inbox, on desktop and on your phone.

A closed chat stays closed when you create a task; an open one stays open. If you close it, a reload keeps it closed, and a tab where you left it open keeps it open.

**Settings > General > Task Page** no longer offers the three auto-open switches, because nothing opens on its own. The older **Keep AI chat closed always** and **Open AI chat by default** choices are gone with them.

## Board filter behavior

- **All boards** — shows every chat across all your accessible boards.
- **One board** — shows only chats from that board.
- Default is **All boards**, so all your chats appear by default when you open the chat.

Run /chat or switch to the Chat view to start a conversation. Then use the board filter above the chat list to switch between "All boards" and a specific board.

## Agent Chat sidebar status

When you open an agent chat with an agent that supports status visibility, the chat sidebar displays real-time per-agent status instead of a static green dot.

### Available status indicators

- **Active** — the agent is currently processing a task or message.
- **Idle** — the agent is idle but available, with an optional duration indicating how long it has been idle.
- **Idle with duration** — same as Idle, but explicitly shows the elapsed time (in minutes) since the last activity.
- **Out of tokens** — the agent has exhausted its token budget and cannot process further requests until refreshed.
- **Inactive** — the agent has been turned off or has no recent activity; it is not responding.

### How status changes are shown

- The status is computed server-side at request time and shown as text immediately next to the agent name.
- Changing from one status to another updates in real time without needing to refresh the page.
- If an agent is explicitly turned off, it always shows Inactive until you restore the agent or the chat session closes.

## Agent Chat auto-scroll behavior

Agent Chat automatically scrolls to the most recent messages as new content arrives, including queued and typing indicators, so you never miss updates during active conversations.

### Scrolling behavior

- When you are already at the bottom of the chat list and new messages arrive or queued statuses appear, the window follows them.
- If you scroll up to view earlier messages and new messages arrive, the scroll position stays where you left it until you scroll back down.
- When a new message appears while at the bottom, Chat immediately follows to keep the latest message in view.

This behavior applies across all supported channels and helps you stay aligned with agent progress without manually paging through the thread.","excerpt":"Choose a ticket or board scope for docked AI Chat, and filter chat history by board.","category":"AI & Productivity","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840467,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/chat-board-filter/"}

{"id":"docs-features-collaboration","title":"Collaboration","slug":"docs-features-collaboration","content":"Hypertask is built for teams — whether that’s two founders, a 50-person engineering org, or a mix of humans and AI agents. Every feature is designed around the idea that project management is inherently collaborative.

## Team workspaces
Workspaces are the top-level container in Hypertask. Each workspace groups related projects together and manages team membership.

A workspace might represent your company, a department, or a client engagement. You can belong to multiple workspaces.

## Project members
### Inviting people
Invite team members to a project by generating an **invite link**. Invite links support several controls:

| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Expiration** | Set when the link stops working (e.g. 7 days, 30 days, never) |
| **Usage limit** | Cap how many people can join via this link |
| **Domain restriction** | Limit invites to specific email domains (e.g. `@yourcompany.com`) |

Domain restrictions are useful when you want to share an invite link broadly (in Slack, for example) but limit access to people within your organization.

### Roles and access

A board has an owner. The owner can set each other person to **Admin** or **Member**. Those are the only two roles you can assign, and the owner’s own role cannot be changed.

There is no Viewer role and no read-only role. Someone who only needs to look at a board still joins as an Admin or a Member.

Manage the people on a board in **Settings > Board > Members**. That list is for the board you have open.

To let a client see a single board, invite them to that board only. People see a board when they own it or are a member of it, so a client invited to one board does not see your other boards.

Billing is under **Settings > Team > Billing**. The team owner can view billing and update the payment method. The team owner, the board owner, or a board Admin can view billing details and change the billing email.

### BYOK and API keys
API key management is available to **BYOK (Bring Your Own Key)** teams. BYOK teams see and manage API keys directly in the **Settings → Team** navigation. For non-BYOK teams, the API Keys entry is hidden from this section.

## AI Agents
AI agents can be added to boards just like human team members. When you add an agent to a board, it gains access to that board’s tasks and can be assigned work, @mentioned in comments, and participate in the project workflow.

### Adding agents to boards

1. Open the board’s settings or invite panel.
2. Look for the **invite modal** — it shows both team members and any agents you’ve created.
3. Select the agent you want to add to the board.
4. The agent appears in the board’s member list and can be assigned tasks.

Agents added to a board are treated as members of that board. This means:
- Agents appear in the assignee dropdown for tasks on that board
- Agents can be @mentioned in comments and will receive notifications
- Agents can read and update tasks on that board via MCP

Agents do not count as team seats toward your subscription limit. You can add as many agents as you need without affecting your seat count.

### Agent access scope
When you create an agent, it inherits access to all boards in projects where you’re a member. Use the board-level invite modal to **restrict which boards an agent can access** — boards not on the list treat the agent as if it doesn’t exist.

This is useful when:
- You work across multiple clients or teams and don’t want a given agent active everywhere
- You want to limit an agent to only the boards where it has relevant context
- You have specialized agents for different workflows and need to keep them scoped

## Feedback
Give feedback directly from the app with a prominent call-to-action. The feedback button is always available at the bottom of the app shell rail and opens a fully-featured real feedback modal with:
- Fast-track submission fields for quick suggestions
- Rich text support so you can include screenshots, drafts, or detailed feature requests
- Clear category selection to route your feedback to the right teams
- Direct posting to the Feedback board with auto-assignment

Use the feedback button to share ideas, report bugs, or suggest improvements. Your input shapes future releases and directly affects the UX improvements we ship.

## @mentions
Type `@` in any comment to mention a team member. Mentions do two things:
1. **Send a notification** — the mentioned person receives an inbox notification immediately.
2. **Add as follower** — the mentioned person is automatically added as a follower on the task, so they receive future updates.

Mentions work in comments and task descriptions, and support native and external agents:

If you receive a mention that looks suspicious, report it to your workspace owner.

### Agent @mentions

Agent owners are not notified of their own agent’s comments.

@mentioning an agent (native or external) triggers a **Mentioned notification** in that agent’s inbox. External agents with scoped tokens receive notifications via their `agent_notifications` array and can poll it with `hypertask_inbox` (`action: "list"`) to pick up mentions.

This means you can @mention external agents in comments and task descriptions to trigger automation; the agent’s inbox receives a Mentioned notification, and it can respond via MCP comments with proper HTML markup.

If an external agent isn’t receiving @mentions, verify that it has board-level access.

## Emoji reactions
React to tasks and comments with emoji. Reactions serve as lightweight feedback — a quick thumbs-up to acknowledge work, a flag to signal concern, or a celebration when something ships.

### Fast like button
For the most common reaction — a simple thumbs-up — Hypertask provides a **fast like button** that appears directly on task cards and comment rows. No need to open the full emoji picker:

- **Mouse users:** hover over a task card or comment row to reveal the like button, which shows a tooltip with a "[L]" hint; click it to toggle your reaction on or off.
- **Mobile users:** tap the like button that appears inline alongside the comment or task actions.

The like button is a shortcut for the thumbs-up reaction. It appears in the full reactions list alongside any other emoji your teammates have added, and it triggers the same notification to the author as any other reaction.

### Mobile emoji picker
On mobile devices, emoji reactions are organized into a docked picker that mimics popular messaging apps:
- Picker appears docked at the bottom of the screen, aligned with the keyboard input area
- A search bar on the Emoji tab lets you quickly find emojis by name
- Selecting an emoji immediately applies it as a reaction, with the picker closing automatically

### Comment display
Comments can be starred (saved) or pinned, and the visual indicators update based on comment state:
1. **Pinned + saved** — only the orange pinned dot displays (saved state is suppressed)
2. **Pinned only** — only the orange pinned dot displays
3. **Saved only** — only the yellow saved/starred dot displays

### All reactions icon
Click the activity icon next to a comment to see all reactions. This icon appears when someone has reacted in any way, whether it’s a like or another emoji expression.

## Agent decision requests
Agents can ask you for decisive feedback on tickets. When an agent encounters a decision that impacts work (e.g., "Archive this task," "Move to inactive," etc.), it opens a **decision request** on the ticket with one-tap approve/answer buttons.

### Triggering decision requests
Decision requests appear as inline panels on the ticket:
- **Approve** — Applies the agent’s suggested action with one tap
- **Reject / More options** — Opens a menu with detailed choices or alternative actions

Agents only create decision requests when the suggested action clearly affects board state and benefits from human sign-off. Routine summaries, AI editor outputs, and informational messages do not trigger requests.

### Agent aftermath
Once you respond:
- **Approved decisions** — The agent applies the action to the ticket immediately (e.g., archives the task and adds a reason comment)
- **Rejected or alternative** — The agent stops iterating on that item and moves on, leaving the ticket in its current state

You can review all pending decision requests anytime in the ticket feed — the panel stays visible until resolved.

## Real-time sync
Hypertask keeps every connected client live — no manual refreshes needed. Changes made anywhere in the app (or via the CLI and MCP) appear instantly for everyone who has the same board open.

**What updates in real time:**
- Tasks appearing, disappearing, or moving between sections when created, archived, or moved
- Task title, status, priority, and assignee changes
- New comments and reactions
- Board and section changes

Creating a task from the CLI and watching it appear on an open board with no page reload is a first-class workflow — useful for monitoring agents running in your terminal or CI pipeline.

### Real-time collaborative text editing
Multiple people can edit the same rich-text field at the same time, with changes merged automatically.

This applies to:
- Task descriptions
- Comments (while drafting)
- Any rich text field in the app

There are no save buttons — changes persist as you type.

Real-time sync means AI agents editing task descriptions via MCP won’t overwrite human edits. Changes are merged automatically.

## Managing comments
You can manage comments on any task — including comments left by other team members or agents. This is useful when:
- Cleaning up outdated or irrelevant comments
- Removing agent-generated comments that are no longer needed
- Tidying up task threads for better readability

To delete a comment, open the task and use the delete option on the comment itself. Comment management is available to all project members — trust within the team is assumed for collaborative housekeeping.

### Comment hover panel
The comment hover panel in table views and card lists is streamlined for faster access to actions:
- **Reply** — standard reply action
- **React** — add or remove a reaction (thumbs-up, favorite, flag, etc.)
- **Three-dot menu** — click the three-dot to reveal remaining options

Press and hold <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> (or the three-dot itself) to access the full menu with all comment commands pinned at the top:
- **Edit** — modify the comment
- **Summarize** — generate an AI summary of the comment thread
- **Fast like** — quickly add a thumbs-up reaction

For the most common reaction, just hover and click the like button directly on the comment row. No need to open the full emoji picker.

### Mobile long press to actions
On a phone, press and hold a comment to open the Command Center with that comment's actions at the top. **Edit comment** is first when you wrote the comment. Swiping a comment is off so it does not fight the task swipe that already moves you to the next or previous ticket.

### Mobile comment actions menu
When you open a comment's Command Center on mobile, the first actions are the comment ones:
- **Edit**: open the comment composer (shown first when you wrote the comment)
- **Delete**: remove the comment from the thread
- **Star or turn off star**: save or unsave the comment
- **Pin or turn off pin**: pin the comment to the top of the feed

### URL auto-linkification
Bare URLs in comments are automatically converted into clickable links at render time, regardless of how the comment was created. This applies to comments posted via the web UI, CLI, MCP, or any API client — so a deploy URL pasted by a CLI script or an agent's status update with a link will always be clickable for your teammates.

Links open in a new tab. URLs that are already formatted as hyperlinks or embedded inside images are left unchanged.

### Quoted replies
When you reply to a comment, Hypertask inserts a placeholder for the quoted message.

### GIFs and emoji in comments
The comment composer includes a built-in **Emoji & GIFs picker** with two tabs, giving you Slack-style expressiveness in task discussions.

#### Slash commands
Type a slash command at the start of your comment to open the picker instantly:

| Command | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `/emoji` | Opens the picker on the **Emoji** tab |
| `/giphy` | Opens the picker on the **GIFs** tab |

#### Emoji tab
Browse and search a full emoji library. Click any emoji to insert it into your comment at the cursor position.

#### GIFs tab
The GIFs tab is powered by **Giphy** and offers two modes:
- **Trending** — shows popular GIFs by default when you open the tab.
- **Search** — type any query to find a GIF that fits the moment.

Click a GIF to insert it into your comment. Inserted GIFs render as **resizable media** — drag the corner handles to adjust the size, and the chosen dimensions are preserved when the comment is posted.

GIF search requires a Giphy API key configured on the Hypertask deployment. If GIFs are not loading, contact your workspace admin.

## Comment edit mode
Edit a comment to refine your thoughts or fix mistakes. The editor includes keyboard shortcuts to help you work efficiently:

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| **ESC** | Leave edit mode without sending (clears unsaved edits) |
| **Ctrl+Enter** | Send the edited comment |

### Exiting edit mode
When you’re in edit mode and want to abandon your changes:
- **Mouse:** click the trash can icon in the edit-mode footer
- **Keyboard:** press **ESC**

Both options exit edit mode without posting the comment and without polluting the conversation with draft text.

## Activity logs
Every change in Hypertask is recorded in the activity log — a full audit trail of who did what, and when.

Tracked actions include:
- Task creation, updates, and deletion
- Section moves
- Assignment and priority changes
- Comments and reactions
- Member joins and leaves
- Board and section modifications

Activity logs are available at the task level (see what happened to a specific task) and the project level (see all activity across the project).

### Comments-only view (default)
The task feed defaults to **comments only** — history events such as field changes, assignments, and status moves are hidden to reduce noise. This keeps the conversation readable at a glance, especially on busy tickets.

To reveal history events:
- Click the **Show history** pill at the top of the feed, or
- Press **`Ctrl+Shift+H`**

Both controls toggle history events on and off. You can also access **Show/Hide history** and **Expand/Collapse all comments** from the command palette (`Ctrl+K`).

If you need a full audit trail of every change on a task, use **Show history** (`Ctrl+Shift+H`) to surface all activity events inline with the comment thread.","excerpt":"Share a board with Admins and Members. There is no Viewer role. Invite a client to one board, and see who manages billing.","category":"Collaboration & billing","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840473,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/collaboration/"}

{"id":"docs-features-custom-fields","title":"Custom Fields","slug":"docs-features-custom-fields","content":"## Overview

Custom fields let you attach structured data to every task on a board, beyond the built-in properties like priority, size, and due date. Each board defines its own set of fields, and every task on that board gets a value slot for each one.

Five field types are supported:

| Type | Use for |
|------|---------|
| **Number** | Ratings, scores, estimates — anything you sort numerically |
| **Text** | Free-form notes that need their own column |
| **Select** | A fixed list of options |
| **Date** | A date separate from due date |
| **Checkbox** | A yes/no flag |

The flagship use case is an **ICE rating** (a Number field for Impact/Confidence/Ease scoring) used to rank a backlog. The [ICE ranking recipe](#ice-ranking-recipe) below walks through setting one up end to end.

## Creating a field

1. Press `<kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>` and search for "Create custom field".
2. Enter a name for the field.
3. Pick a type: Number, Text, Select, Date, or Checkbox.
4. Press `<kbd>Enter</kbd>` to create it.

The field is created on the current board and is visible by default — no separate step to turn it on.

## Setting values

Open a task and the field appears as a property row in the right rail, alongside priority, size, and due date. Click it, type or pick a value, and press `<kbd>Enter</kbd>` to save.

When you create a ticket with the [AI Task Writer](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/ai-features/#how-it-works-today), it can fill Number, Select, Text, Date, and Checkbox fields from the board's saved instructions or past tickets. For example, a score field can match a score in the title. Values that do not fit the field are skipped. This applies to Ctrl+J compose, AI chat ticket creation, and the CLI/MCP task writer.

## Table view: columns and sorting

Every custom field on a board shows up as a column in [table view](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/table-view/):

- **Sorting:** click a custom field's column header to sort by it. Number and Date fields sort numerically/chronologically; empty values always sort to the bottom regardless of sort direction.
- **Columns picker:** open "Configure table columns" to toggle any custom field's visibility or drag it to reorder, the same as built-in columns. "Reset to default" restores the original set.

## Views
