A [saved view](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/favorites/) captures the table's current sort, so a view sorted by a custom field stays sorted every time it's opened. This is what makes an ICE ranking view sharable: save it once, and everyone who opens the view sees the backlog in ICE order.

## ICE ranking recipe

1. Create a Number field named `ICE` on the board (see [Creating a field](#creating-a-field) above).
2. Open each task and set its ICE score in the right rail.
3. Switch to table view, add the ICE column if it's hidden, and click the header to sort descending.
4. Save the sorted table as a view named "ICE ranking".

Anyone who opens the "ICE ranking" view sees the board pre-sorted by score, no re-sorting required.

## For agents & API

Custom fields are managed through the same `Bearer htk_...` REST API used elsewhere in Hypertask ([authentication](https://docs.hypertask.ai/api/rest-api/#authentication)). Task detail responses include a `customFieldValues` array for every task on a board with custom fields defined.

### Create a field

**Endpoint:** `POST /api/mcp/custom-fields`

Creating a field is idempotent on `name` — calling create again with a name that already exists on the board returns the existing field instead of erroring.

```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_id": 123, "name": "ICE", "type": "number"}' \
  "https://app.hypertask.ai/api/mcp/custom-fields"
```

**Response example:**

```json
{
  "fieldId": 789,
  "name": "ICE",
  "type": "number"
}
```

### Set a value

**Endpoint:** `POST /api/mcp/custom-fields/value`

Accepts either `field_id` or `field_name`. The recommended surface is to first create the field via `POST /api/mcp/custom-fields`, obtaining `field_id`, then assign values. Values are strictly validated against the field's type — for example, a non-numeric value sent to a Number field is rejected with a `400` response.

**Set value by field_id**

```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"task_id": 789, "field_id": 789, "value": 42}' \
  "https://app.hypertask.ai/api/mcp/custom-fields/value"
```

**Switch to field_name (auto-creates the field first)**

```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"task_id": 789, "field_name": "ICE", "value": 42}' \
  "https://app.hypertask.ai/api/mcp/custom-fields/value"
```

**Tips:**

- Use `field_id` in named endpoints after retrieval for clarity.
- Typed values must match the field's declared type.
- Empty or unset values are represented as `null` unless overridden.

### Delete a field

**Endpoint:** `DELETE /api/mcp/custom-fields/{fieldId}`

```bash
curl -s -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HT_API_KEY" \
  "https://app.hypertask.ai/api/mcp/custom-fields/456"
```

Deleting a field removes every task's value for it. This can't be undone.

A board can have up to **50 custom fields**, and field names are capped at **64 characters**. Requests past either limit are rejected.","excerpt":"Add per-board fields like Number, Text, Select, Date, and Checkbox to tasks, sort by them in table view, and manage them from agents via the API.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840477,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/custom-fields/"}

{"id":"docs-features-favorites","title":"Favorites","slug":"docs-features-favorites","content":"# Favorites

Keep your most important boards within arm's reach by pinning them to the favorites bar. Quickly jump between core workspaces without hunting through lists or filters.

## Pin Boards

1. Open any board's menu (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> or click the board icon next to its title).
2. Toggle **Pin to favorites**. The board will appear in the favorites bar at the left rail.

## Drag to Reorder

- Grab a favorite by its drag handle (⋮⋮).
- Drag it to a new position and release.
- The sidebar reflects the new order immediately.

The favorites bar uses dependable viewport breakpoints for desktop spacing, matching other layout surfaces for consistency and clarity.

## Remove Favorites

- In the favorites bar, **Remove** a pinned board via the context menu (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> or click the three dots).
- The board disappears from your favorites but remains accessible in the board list.

## System Behavior

The favorites bar persists across sessions. When you reconfigure your sidebar layout, your pinned favorites stay visible under the rail. Access management and sharing settings are not affected by pinning.","excerpt":"Pin important boards to your favorites bar and drag to reorder them.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840481,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/favorites/"}

{"id":"docs-features-images","title":"Images and Attachments","slug":"docs-features-images","content":"We treat HEIC and HEIF images like any other file: they render consistently across thumbnails, inline previews, galleries, and lightbox views. If a preview isn't suitable, exclude the format from previews or use a low-res fallback. ## Supported formats | Format | Default behavior | |--------|------------------| | HEIC/HEIF | Keep the original for download; the system generates a JPEG copy for previews | | JPEG/PNG/WebP | Render at full quality | ## Viewing HEIC/HEIF 1. Attach a photo from an iPhone or Mac. 2. The platform creates a browser-compatible JPEG copy for previews, while the original HEIC/HEIF is preserved for download. 3. See it in the same places as regular images: - **Attachment thumbnails** below comments and email bubbles - **Inline embed** inside a comment or task description - **Board gallery** or gallery views that show attachments - **Task detail lightbox** with a thumbnail strip at the bottom ## Downloading HEIC/HEIF HEIC and HEIF photos uploaded to tasks and comments retain their original file format in the download. When you click **Download** on an attachment: - The original HEIC/HEIF file is downloaded, preserving the full image quality - Previews across the platform use the generated JPEG copy for faster rendering and broader compatibility This ensures you can access the highest-quality version of your photos while maintaining fast, consistent previews everywhere else. ## Who can download attachments New Only people who can see the parent ticket can download its attachments. Access follows board membership: people who are not the owner, an Admin, or a Member of that board cannot reach downloads. ### How it works - When opening a task or viewing the task detail lightbox, the system checks that you own the board or are an Admin or Member before exposing download URLs. - If you are not on the board, downloads come back as not found. - The board owner, Admins, and Members who can see the ticket can download files. Agents on that board can download too. - This change prevents unauthorized downloads for attachments that originated on private or board-limited tasks. ### What this protects - Attachments stored on private tickets are not reachable by users who should not see that context. - AI-generated task previews now respect the same access gate, ensuring draft images on private tickets are not exposed outside the intended scope. - Regular downloads continue to work as before for anyone with proper ticket visibility. ### When it applies - The board owner, Admins, Members, and AI agents on the board can download its attachments. - People who are not the board owner, an Admin, or a Member cannot reach downloads. A public share link can show the board, and it does not let them download. ## Excluding previews To prevent HEIC/HEIF from generating previews (e.g., if the file is too large for preview generation): 1. Open the attachment's context menu (three dots). 2. Select **Excluded from previews** to disable automatic preview generation. 3. Uploaders still receive the file; observers only see the original format and a download link. ## Lightbox image strip In the task detail lightbox, the thumbnail strip shows all attachments in that task. Supported formats and non-preview status appear consistently across all attachments. ## Handling malformed previews in the lightbox strip If the lightbox shows a broken image icon for a non-decodable file: - A file icon now appears instead of a broken icon, making it clear the image content could not be decoded. ## Warnings for unexpected content If a file exhibits preview or display issues (broken icons, no thumbnail, or an unexpected format shown), check: - The file is flagged as excluded from previews (if the goal was to prevent preview). - The file is a HEIC/HEIF image under preview logic (historically, some browsers rendered these as named files before conversion completed). ## Upload tips - **Keep resolution manageable:** Very large HEIC images can lead to longer preview conversion times. - **Review lightbox strip:** If a thumbnail seems wrong after a HEIC upload, the browser might still be loading a placeholder until conversion finishes. ## Paste support You can paste photos directly into comments and task descriptions. The system handles both HEIC/HEIF files and regular image formats in the same paste handler: - HEIC/HEIF: Preserves the original and generates a JPEG preview - JPEG/PNG/WebP: Downloads as-is This gives you a single paste workflow whether you're uploading from Photos via copy-paste or dragging and dropping files. [Learn more about keyboard shortcuts for superhuman-style snippets in the Superhuman-Style Snippets documentation.](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/superhuman-snippets/) ## Handling blocked image hosts New If your network or a firewall blocks the image server domain, attachments now retry through the app domain and display instead of staying broken. ### How it works - Images usually load directly from `files.hypertask.app`. - When a request to `files.hypertask.app` fails (for example, due to network restrictions or a firewall), the app retries once through `app.hypertask.ai`. - On successful retry, the image displays in comments, task descriptions, attachments, and the task detail lightbox. - This happens automatically; no configuration is required on your side. - Normal networks that can reach `files.hypertask.app` continue to load images straight from the image server, so performance is unchanged. ### When this helps This change helps users on restrictive networks (including some corporate Wi-Fi and VPNs) where: - The image host is blocked, resulting in broken images or connection errors. - You cannot easily unblock the domain. - You don't have control over network policy. Example scenario: A comment includes an image attachment, but your network blocks `files.hypertask.app`. Previously the image would appear broken. Now the app retries through `app.hypertask.ai`, and the image loads as expected. ### Reloading for browsers that blocked images before If you saw broken images on a previous visit and still use a network that blocks the image server: - Refresh the ticket page and the attachments with retry behavior will load properly. - After the initial load, the images are cached by your browser, so you should not need to re-enter restrictive network conditions to see them. [Learn more about keyboard shortcuts in the Keyboard Shortcuts documentation.](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/keyboard-shortcuts/) ## Resizing images on pages and ticket descriptions You can manually adjust image size on pages and in ticket descriptions. ### Auto-fit vs manual resize - Auto-fit: Images without a saved size automatically adjust to fit the context (mobile, desktop layout, and container width). - Manual resize: Drag the handle on any image to set a custom width. When you type text nearby and the edit is saved, the new size is persisted. ### Persisted size - After you drag an image's resize handle and see "Saved," the image's width is saved to that page or ticket description. - Reloading the page or ticket keeps the image at the custom size instead of reverting to auto-fit. - Using multiple sizes on the same page works as expected: each one stays where you set it. ### Mobile experience - On mobile, resized images still respect screen width and remain readable. - Auto-fit images respond to pinch-to-zoom; resized images follow the set width. ### Common use cases - Bulleted lists with images: Size images consistently (e.g., 50% width) so they look uniform in lists. - Diagrams on pages: Grow or shrink diagrams on a page to finer steps. - Ticket descriptions: Include screenshots at a consistent scale along with typed text. [Learn more about creating pages in the Pages documentation.](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/pages/) Fix When uploading a file and immediately saving before the preview appears (for example with keyboard shortcuts or Save & new), the attachment now persists on the task instead of dropping.","excerpt":"Send HEIC/HEIF photos, view them everywhere (thumbnails, inline, galleries, lightboxes), force or exempt from preview, and resize images on pages.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1792923251,"updated_at":1794840487,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/images/"}

{"id":"docs-features-inbox","title":"Inbox & Notifications","slug":"docs-features-inbox","content":"The **Inbox** gathers all notifications (mentions, assignments, and more) into a single feed, letting you process them efficiently. Use keyboard shortcuts for quick actions and keep important work at the top of your queue. ## Viewing the inbox Press Ctrl + K to open the command palette and search for **"Inbox"**, or go to the Inbox page from the sidebar. The inbox shows: - **Unread notifications** from mentions, assignments, reactions, and follow updates - **Actionable items** like tasks, notifications with dismiss options (undo, dismiss all, undo all), and confirmed operations (invites, feedback) - **Important tasks**: rows marked with the **Important** label appear first, in priority order and timeline-sorted (newest first) ### Replying to notification emails Reply directly to a task notification email to add your response as a comment on the task. Send the reply from the same email address as your Hypertask account so Hypertask can verify it and post it under your name. The inbox can be grouped into multiple views: Use Ctrl + F from the Inbox to search across all notifications. This is scoped across boards for board-agnostic filtering. ### Bulk archive Select multiple notifications with mouse clicks or keyboard navigation. When you select rows, the selection count appears next to the archive and remind icons, and the archive action archives all selected notifications in one step: | Action | Shortcut | Description | |--------|----------|-------------| | **Select all** | Ctrl + A | Select all visible rows in the current view, mirroring page behavior | | **Archive selected** | Shift + E | Archive all selected notifications | | **Archive all** | Ctrl + E | Archive all notifications (opens confirmation if many) | Ctrl + A selects all visible rows rather than every row in the inbox due to index limits - select specific subsets when the list is long. ### Triage with AI chat Press Ctrl + K (Cmd + K on Mac). Choose **Triage inbox**. This starts a new AI chat. Ask AI chat to read your inbox. It reads up to 500 messages per page and can continue through the remaining pages without asking for confirmation. Before archiving a batch, chat previews every affected ticket, including other messages it would clear on those tickets. Confirm once for that batch. If the batch changes, chat shows a fresh preview and asks again. Its reply names the tickets it cleared. ### Inbox views | View | Shortcut | Purpose | |------|----------|---------| | **Inbox** | Default | All notifications | | **Search** | Search icon | Text-based search across all boards | | **Notifications** | Notification icon | List of all notification types | ### Inbox filtering scope New users in a board see notifications for private tasks, while users removed from a board no longer receive those notifications in their Inbox. To prevent a stale notification from reappearing, you can reply to it (or tap Undo) to remove it from your queue. Cleaning up unsubscribed notifications helps keep the Inbox focused and relevant. ## Decisions Tickets waiting on your decision show in two places. In the **Inbox**, open the **Decisions** split. A ticket is listed there when someone @mentions you in a comment that has a line starting with **Question:**, and you have not answered yet. A later comment you write yourself removes that ticket. A comment posted by an agent does not. Clearing the blocker on that ticket also removes it. An ordinary mention does not appear in Decisions. Open the ticket from this split and Hypertask jumps to the question. On a board, open the **Decisions** view from the view tabs on desktop, or the view picker on your phone. It shows tickets in the **UX Sign-off** column, and in a column titled with your name followed by **review** (for example, **Alex review**). Empty columns stay hidden. Each person sees their own review column. ## Agent chatter in the inbox Improvement Agent messages from the AI now stay out of the personal inbox. Agent-only comments (FYI messages) and agent chatter no longer appear as notifications for human users. Instead: - **Agent chatter ignored** – Pure agent commentary without a human @mention does not reach its owner's inbox. - **FYI mentions visible** – An agent FYI comment with a human @mention does appear in the inbox, making it clear the human is being included in the loop, but it stays out of the Important section. - **Only open questions land in Important** – When an agent poses a question that requires a human response, the message lands in the Important section so you can act on it first. This applies to all agents using Hypertask's AI integration and keeps your inbox focused on questions and actions directly tied to your own work. ## Numbered pins in the mobile inbox On mobile, each inbox row shows a numbered indicator next to the sender name. This creates a visual order that matches the date you received the notification, making it easier to scan recent items: - **Numbered pins** appear on desktop and mobile inbox rows - The numbers correspond to timeline order (newest first) - This keeps your attention on the most recent important items without relying solely on the top position The numbered pins complement the timeline-sorted order for returning visits, giving you a quick visual guide to your recent notifications. ## Invite link validation across pages Improved Pages that generate or use invite links now validate board context. **My Tasks** and **Inbox** no longer send invite-link requests without a board, which previously caused console errors. Requesting an invite link without a board now shows a clear message instead of a server error, keeping the console clean and providing explicit feedback when a board is required. This change applies across most pages that send invite links, ensuring any invalid requests surface a user-friendly message rather than an unhandled error. ## Shortcuts tip visibility Improved When using the archive keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl + E or Shift + E), the tip that shows which shortcut to press (for example, "press E to archive") now appears and stays visible. The tip is tied to the bottom shortcut bar ("Ctrl+K for Command center, J to go down..."). Before this fix, repeatedly archiving would close the bottom shortcut bar or clear the inbox, causing the tip to disappear and making it hard to see which key shortcut to use. The tip is automatically disabled when the shortcut bar is hidden for the session, so navigating to the Inbox or re-opening the shortcut bar restores visibility. ## Board chip in the new task box When you use Ctrl+J to create a new task from the inbox, the new task box shows a board chip indicating the intended destination: - **Always visible**: The chip appears as soon as the box opens, so you always see the target board. - **Same everywhere**: On a board or a ticket detail page, it shows that page's board. - **Editable**: Click the chip to choose a different board before saving the task. Ctrl+J uses the same board selection logic as the AI chat box: the focused ticket's board if there is one, otherwise the open board split, and finally the last used board for All or Important views.","excerpt":"Manage your incoming notifications, Snooze, Important, and Decisions.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840491,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/inbox/"}

{"id":"docs-features-integrations","title":"Integrations","slug":"docs-features-integrations","content":"Hypertask works with Cursor and Codex. Both connect through MCP, the same way as any other MCP client.

## Works today

These are in **Settings**, then **Connect**:

- **[MCP](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/overview/).** Works with any MCP client, such as Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.
- **[CLI](https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/reference/).** The `hypertask` command.
- **[REST API](https://docs.hypertask.ai/api/rest-api/).**
- **[Webhooks](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/agent-webhooks/).** Signed requests to a URL you control.

**Figma** is under **Settings**, then **Profile**, then **Accounts**. Connect a Figma account there. Hypertask uses that connection when a task includes a Figma link.

**ChatGPT** uses an OpenAPI action. The steps are on [MCP Integration](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/overview/#client-configuration), under the ChatGPT tab.

## Not available yet

- **Slack app.** Not available yet.
- **GitHub per board.** Connecting GitHub to a board is not available yet.
- **Google Calendar sync.** Not available yet. Due dates still appear on the Hypertask [calendar](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/calendar/).
- **Other importers.** There is no Jira, Trello, or Asana sync, and no other native importer.","excerpt":"What Hypertask connects to today, including Cursor and Codex, and what is not available yet.","category":"Collaboration & billing","created_at":1792962811,"updated_at":1794840495,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/integrations/"}

## Command Palette

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Open command palette | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> |
| Search commands | Type to filter | Type to filter |
| Execute command | <kbd>Enter</kbd> | <kbd>Enter</kbd> |
| Navigate through filtered commands | <kbd>Arrow keys</kbd> | <kbd>Arrow keys</kbd> |

The Command Palette lists board and section actions, including "Hide column", "Show columns", "Archive board", "Delete board", and more. Use <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> and type keywords like "hide", "show", "archive", "delete" to quickly access relevant actions.

### Board settings from Ctrl+K
When you search for **"Board settings"** in the Command Palette using <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd>, the board picker now preselects the board you came from. This works whether you're on a ticket page, board page, or another view - even if you previously had a different team open in settings. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to cancel and restore your previous state.

Try it: open any ticket, press <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>, type "board", pick **"Board settings"**. The board picker shows that ticket's board and preselects the right team.

## Hiding and Showing Columns
To hide a column using the Command Palette:

1. Open the Command Palette: <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>
2. Type "hide" to find the "Hide column" action
3. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to hide the active (hovered/last-clicked) column directly
4. The Command Palette closes automatically after execution

To show previously hidden columns:

1. Open the Command Palette: <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>
2. Type "show" to find the "Show columns" action
3. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to reveal all hidden sections

"Hide column" now targets the last clicked or currently hovered section rather than cycling through sections, making it easier to hide the specific column you're working with. The "Empty columns" command also reads the current state and filters both the Kanban view groups and the table view groups, showing "Show empty columns" when they're hidden and "Hide empty columns" when they're visible.

An empty view keeps its visible columns on screen, even when empty columns are hidden. Your saved setting does not change. Add a ticket and the other empty columns hide again. Columns you hid individually stay hidden.

## Board palette
Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> (Windows/Linux) or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> (Mac) to show the board palette overlay. On the left rail, the board palette displays your user account row with:
- **Email or handle** - Click to open the account switcher dialog
- **Avatar** - Click to open Account & Profile settings

This provides quick access to switching workspaces or reviewing your account configuration without leaving the current board.

The board palette joins <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> as a non-intrusive way to access workspace settings while staying in context.

## Open Latest Updates
Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> (Windows/Linux) or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> (Mac) then search for **"Latest Updates"** in the board palette or command palette to open the Latest Updates panel from any route in the app. This provides quick access to see recent activity across your boards without leaving your current view.

## Global Alt+Number board shortcuts
**Before:** On the table view or any board view, <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>1-7</kbd> shortcuts did nothing even when the app-shell rail was supposed to be active, causing them to behave as no-ops.

**After:** When the rail is enabled, <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>2-7</kbd> now correctly switch to their corresponding surfaces (Board = 2, Table = 3, Calendar = 4, AI Chat dock = 5, and Search = 6) from any view. On Mac, the global board switcher uses <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>2-7</kbd> instead of <kbd>Cmd</kbd> to avoid interfering with tab switching.

The app-shell rail and global Alt+Number shortcuts were designed to provide tactile, one-hand navigation across main surfaces. Enabling the rail (via account menu or command palette) unlocks these skips so they work reliably everywhere, not only on the rail itself.

## Time reports quick-log
Quick-log time directly from the board or a task card using <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>:

- **On a board or task card** - Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> to open the quick-log dialog preconfigured for the selected card.
- **On an open ticket** - Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> to instantly jump to the per-ticket time log modal, skipping the intermediate step of selecting the ticket from the board list.

The quick-log interface supports Hours and Minutes fields, board and user filters per entry, and works across time zones with per-entry local-noon timestamps for accurate log association with the logged day.

**Keyboard shortcuts**:

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Quick-log time on a selected board card | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> |

## Timer shortcuts
Time tracking shortcuts are available when time tracking is enabled for your board or task:
- **App shell rail** - Press <kbd>7</kbd> on the rail to open the running-timers view
- **Task detail** - Press <kbd>Option</kbd> + <kbd>T</kbd> or <kbd>Alt+T</kbd> to start or stop the open task timer

The timer indicator appears in the task card and task detail, showing whether a timer is running for that task.

See the <a href="https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/time-tracking/">Time Tracking</a> page for full details.

## System-theme prediction
When you open the Command Palette with <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> (or <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd> on Mac), theme-related options now display context-appropriate labels to make system-theme mode predictable. Retired numeric theme modes (1-5) redirect safely to the Appearance settings with your in-session command state preserved.

Theme options in the command palette now adapt to your system theme and gracefully redirect legacy theme choices to Appearance settings.

## Copy current page URL
When you open the Command Palette with <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd>, the action **"Copy current page URL"** copies the complete browser address, including the board, view, task, filters, and section. The action is available everywhere <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> opens, including task detail, calendar, and inbox views.

The action is available to everyone.

## Use everywhere, including Settings
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> (Windows/Linux) or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> (Mac) now opens the Command Palette on every signed-in page. This includes:
- Boards, tickets, inbox, and search (existing behavior)
- My Tasks view
- All settings pages, such as Settings & General, Board general, and Appearance

On Mac, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> also works in addition to <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>.

Public/sign-in pages, including the sign-in page, still ignore this shortcut.

Escape behavior in Settings:
- First <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the command menu and keeps you in Settings
- A second <kbd>Esc</kbd> exits Settings as usual

This makes the command palette consistently available for board actions, views, and shortcuts throughout the app.

## Mobile in-app gestures
- On mobile, press and hold a comment to open the Command Center with comment actions at the top. Edit comment is first when you wrote the comment.
- Dictation remains the primary input method on mobile; Tap *Improve with AI* to refine your comments without leaving the input flow

## Mobile page exit gesture
On mobile, pressing **<kbd>Esc</kbd>** in the full-screen Pages view now exits via the back action - just like other views in the app. With text typed but unsaved, <kbd>Esc</kbd> clears the unsaved draft. Without text, a single <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the page and stays on the task.

## Ctrl+J board chip
When you press <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd>, the new task box shows which board the task will land on, using the same board chip UI as the AI chat box. The chip appears as soon as the box opens, on every page: a board, a ticket, the inbox and views that mix boards. On a board or ticket page it shows that page's board.

**Board selection logic:**

- **Focused ticket's board:** If a ticket is visible and focused in the inbox, <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd> places the new task on that ticket's board.
- **Open board split:** If there's no focused ticket, the task goes on the open board split.
- **All or Important:** If no board is in context, <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd> uses All or Important as a default board.

Click the chip before saving to change the board.

From the inbox, <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd> is the fastest way to start a new task on a specific board without exiting the feed.

## Sending from the Ctrl+J new task box
The new task box sends with the same shortcut as comments and descriptions, so Enter is free for paragraphs.

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Send the new task | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Enter</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Enter</kbd> |
| Start a new paragraph | <kbd>Enter</kbd> | <kbd>Enter</kbd> |

The hint under the box names the shortcut. One press creates one task with everything you typed, and your note stays in the box if the task fails.
### New Task board shortcut hint

Hover over the board chip in **New Task** to see its keyboard shortcut:
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> on Windows and Linux,
or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> on Mac.
The same shortcut appears below the task box. Click the chip or use that
shortcut to choose a board. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to cancel without losing
your draft.","excerpt":"Complete keyboard shortcut reference for Windows, Linux, and Mac.","category":"Keyboard Shortcuts","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840499,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/keyboard-shortcuts/"}

{"id":"docs-features-pages","title":"Pages","slug":"docs-features-pages","content":"Pages keep research and notes on your boards. A page can stand alone or link tickets. Open **Pages** below **Table** in the sidebar. You can also use **Commands → Go to Pages**. ## What is a Page? A page belongs to a board. Linking a ticket does not grant access. Pages follow their board’s existing permissions. Pages are: - **Board-owned:** Stand alone or link multiple tickets. - **Markdown-first:** Write in markdown; the editor renders rich HTML with TipTap. - **Agent-friendly:** Created, appended, updated, and archived programmatically via CLI, MCP, REST, and AI Chat. - **RAG-indexed:** Every write is indexed so the AI can search, summarize, and reason over page content. - **Versioned:** Every change is captured with history and restore capabilities. - **Conflict-safe:** Optimistic-lock guards return a 409 conflict if multiple agents try to write at once. ## Create and find pages 1. Open **Pages** from the sidebar or Commands. 2. Choose **This board** or **All boards**. 3. Search by page title or content. 4. Choose **New page** to start a document. 5. Choose its board when prompted. Your title and content save automatically. **Archived pages** lists documents removed from active lists. ## Search finds a page from different words Improvement Pages were already sent to the search index, but page search only matched the exact words you typed. Page search now reads that index, the same way ticket search does, so a page written as "view tab count includes cards in hidden columns" is found by "tab counter includes cards that the view hides". What changed for you: - **The Pages screen** returns the right page for a question written in your own words, up to 50 results per search. - **Agents** get the same behaviour through the page search tool in REST, MCP and AI Chat. - **Exact words still work**, and exact matches stay first in the list. - **Board access is unchanged.** A page is only returned when the current page still passes the same board, project, archive and link checks, so better ranking never shows a page you could not open. - **No search, no change.** The unfiltered page list behaves exactly as before. ## Link tickets and pages On a page, choose **+ Link ticket**. Pick an existing ticket from the search window. **Linked tickets** shows the page’s visible ticket links. Choose **Unlink** to remove a link. Unlinking keeps the page and ticket. On a ticket, open **Commands → Link page**. Pick an existing page from the list. The page appears in that ticket’s **Pages**. Existing page lists also offer **+ Link page**. Commands also includes **Link page** and **Link ticket**. Pages without visible tickets show **Back to Pages**. --- ## Agent permissions for page operations What an agent may do with pages depends on its access mode: - **Normal (read/write):** Can create, change, archive, and restore task pages. - **Read-only:** Can only read pages. Creating, changing, archiving, or restoring is refused. ## Publishing a long report from a file New The CLI can read page content from a file, so a long report does not have to fit in one command-line string. Linux caps a single argument near 128KB, which used to force agents to paste a report in pieces. ```bash hypertask pages create --task HTPR-123 --title "QA report" --html-file report.html hypertask pages update 456 --content-file report.html --canvas hypertask pages append 456 --content-file notes.md ``` - `--content-file ` reads the content from a file and keeps the page's current type on update and append. - `--html-file ` reads the content and marks the page type `html`. - Add `--canvas` to store the file exactly as written, styles and inline images included. This is the way to publish a self-contained HTML report.","excerpt":"Create board documents, link tickets, and find pages.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840504,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/pages/"}

{"id":"docs-features-reports","title":"Reports","slug":"docs-features-reports","content":"The **Reports hub** (`/report`) lists saved reports and board velocity reports for boards you can access. ## Review board velocity Open **Reports**, then choose a board under **Velocity**. You can also open the command palette from a board and choose **Board velocity report**. Choose **Today**, **7 days**, **14 days**, **30 days**, **3 months**, **6 months**, or **12 months**. The default is **30 days**. The report shows: - Median time to finish a task and tasks finished per week - Finished work and comments by board member - Created versus finished tasks - Open and stale tasks by column ## Create a saved report Ask AI chat or an agent to create a report for a board. You can also save HTML with the CLI or MCP. Saved reports appear under **Reports** in the hub, with their board, author, and last update time. ### CLI Use a short slug, the board's numeric ID, a title, and an HTML file: ```bash hypertask report create weekly-summary \ --project 15 \ --title "Weekly summary" \ --html-file ./weekly-summary.html ``` Use `--body` instead of `--html-file` to pass HTML directly. Add `--description` for a short summary. The CLI also supports `report list`, `report get`, `report update`, and `report delete`. Every command needs `--project`; every command except `list` also needs a slug. Deleting a report requires `--confirm`. ### MCP Call `hypertask_reports` with the `create` action: ```json { "action": "create", "input": { "project_id": 15, "slug": "weekly-summary", "title": "Weekly summary", "body_html": "

Weekly summary

Three tasks completed this week.

" } } ``` Use `list`, `get`, `update`, or `delete` to manage saved reports. Open the URL returned by the tool to view the report. A saved report is a snapshot, not a live query. Include all data in its HTML. Inline styles and scripts work, but network requests and external script libraries do not. Update the report when its data changes. ## Status updates A **status update** is an AI-written summary of what has happened on a board, saved as a report. **To generate one:** from the board, press Ctrl+K and run **Generate status update**. It opens when ready. The update has four parts: - **Headline** - one sentence on where the board stands - **Shipped** - work that reached a done column or was archived - **In flight** - work moving through the other columns - **Risks and blockers** - tickets sitting still or otherwise worth attention It is written from the same board data the velocity report uses - ticket movement over the window, per-column counts, staleness thresholds - so the figures it quotes are computed rather than generated. Ticket titles are passed to the model as data, not instructions, so a task title cannot steer what the summary claims. Each board keeps **one** status update, at a fixed address: ``` /report/project-/status-update ``` Regenerating rewrites that page rather than creating a new one, so a link to it always shows the current state. The default window is the last 7 days. The slug `status-update` is reserved for this feature on every board. A report you create manually with that slug will be overwritten the next time an update is generated. ## Best practices - Give reports clear titles and short slugs. - Include the reporting period in the content. - Update an existing report to keep the same link. - Use inline SVG or CSS for charts.","excerpt":"Review board velocity and manage saved reports created by AI, CLI, or MCP.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840509,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/reports/"}

{"id":"docs-features-scheduling","title":"Scheduling","slug":"docs-features-scheduling","content":"# Scheduling Plan when work starts, set up recurring tasks, or reuse common task structures. Scheduling features help you align work with deadlines, keep deliverables on track, and streamline repetitive project workflows. ## Due dates Set when a task should be completed: - **Pick a date**: Click the due date field on a task or in the New task form, then choose from the calendar. - **Predictive phrases**: Enter phrases like "tomorrow," "next week," or "in 3 days" to set relative dates. - **Remove a due date**: Click today's date or select "No due date" to clear it. ### Snoozed tasks in My Tasks To temporarily hide a task from your My Tasks list, set a snooze until a specific date: - Open the task and use the snooze option in the edit panel, or - Use the command palette (Ctrl + K) and search for "Snooze this task" - The task will no longer appear in My Tasks until that date passes - The snooze date sets a calendar reminder so you can resurface the task later A snooze is per task and independent of other views. Tasks remain otherwise accessible from boards, calendars, and saved views. ### Grouping by due time My Tasks lists tasks by due time by default: - **Overdue**: Due dates in the past, always at the top - **Today**: Due date is today - **This week**: Due date is within the next 7 days - **Later**: Due date is any time in the future - **No due date**: Tasks without a set due date Use the **Group** toggle or saved view settings to show board groups instead. ## My Tasks planning view The **My Tasks** view gives you a personal planning dashboard for work assigned to you: - Groups by due time (Overdue, Today, This week, Later, No due date) - Full Kanban board filters available across all time groups - Custom columns you've defined on your boards are preserved in My Tasks - Real-time live updates: rows refresh automatically when changes happen from other tabs, the CLI, or agents, without reloading the page - Quick-add at the top: type a task title and press Enter to create a task on the view's default board, assigned to you ### Saved views Save custom filters, sorting, board selection, and hidden columns to create personalized My Tasks views: - **Full filtering**: Filter by title, assignee, priority, due date, labels, and more - **Sorting**: Sort by any of the same fields, with priority as the primary sort key - **Board selection**: Show tasks from one board or across multiple boards - **Done columns hidden by default**: Keep focused on active work Behavior change Saved views now use the same save, reset, and Ctrl+K picker flows that you use on the Kanban board for deep controls. The Scope button (including Involvement, Detail, and Group scope) and its corresponding command now open the consistent board picker panel you see throughout the app, with search and standard keyboard navigation for "up to scope" actions. This keeps your palette familiar across inbox and board surfaces. > **Tip**: Create a My Tasks saved view to align on active priorities; at any time you can reorder the view's filters, sorting, or board selection without losing them. Saved views persist at the account level and can be reused or deleted from the view toolbar. ## Repeating tasks Configure a task to repeat on a schedule: - Set a due date and enable repeat - Choose a frequency (daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly) - Specify repeat until (date or count) When a repeat task is marked complete, a new instance appears with the next due date. ## Task templates Task templates save task structures for reuse: - Create a template from a completed task's fields, due date, and subtasks - Apply templates to new tasks to keep formatting consistent - Manage templates from the Board Settings or task detail "Templates" section ## Start dates A start date records when work is *meant to begin*, separately from the due date that records when it must *finished*. **To set one:** open a task, press Ctrl+K, run **Set start date**. The field accepts natural language — `today`, `tomorrow`, `next week monday`, `in 3 days` — or pick from the presets. Choose **Reset** to clear it. The task detail shows a **Start date** row only once the field is set; a task without one looks exactly as it did before. A start date on its own never makes a task overdue. Only a missed *due date* does that. A task that started last week but has no deadline is current work, not late work, and **My tasks** files it accordingly. ### API ```http POST /api/tasks/setStartDate Content-Type: application/json { "taskId": 1234, "startDate": "2026-08-10T09:00:00.000Z" } ``` Pass `"startDate": null` to clear it. Returns the updated task. Requires membership of the task's board. ## Repeating tasks A repeating task recreates itself when you finish it. **To set a repeat:** open a task, press Ctrl+K, run **Repeat task**, and choose a cadence: | Cadence | Meaning | |---|---| | `Daily` | Every day | | `Weekdays` | Every weekday, Monday to Friday | | `Weekly` | Every 7 days | | `Biweekly` | Every 14 days | | `Monthly` | Same day each month, clamped to the last day of shorter months (31 Jan → 28 Feb) | Choose **Don't repeat** to stop a task repeating. The option only appears when a rule is already set. A repeating task shows a **Repeats** row in the task detail. ### What "finishing" means The next occurrence is created when you **move the task into a done column**, or **archive it yourself**. It carries over the title, description, priority, size, labels and assignees, with the date advanced by one period. Two cases deliberately do *not* create a new occurrence: - **Auto-archive.** A board's auto-archive sweep fires because nobody touched a task, which is abandonment rather than completion. Repeating there would regenerate neglected tasks indefinitely. - **Moving the task to another board**, including into that board's done column. Relocating work is not completing it. Finishing a repeating task late never produces an already-overdue copy: the next date is rolled forward until it is genuinely in the future, keeping the original time of day and, for weekly rules, the original weekday. If a board has no column that counts as "not done", the task does not repeat — the new occurrence would otherwise be created directly into a done column, where it would read as finished work the moment it appeared. ### API ```http POST /api/tasks/setRecurrence Content-Type: application/json { "taskId": 1234, "recurrence": "Weekly" } ``` Valid values: `Daily`, `Weekdays`, `Weekly`, `Biweekly`, `Monthly`, or `null` to stop repeating. Requires membership of the board. ## Task templates A template stores the shape of a task so you can create the same kind of work repeatedly without retyping it. Templates are per board, and capture the **title**, **description**, **priority**, **size** and **labels**. **To save one:** open a task you want to reuse, press Ctrl+K, run **Save task as template**. The template is named after the task title. **To use one:** from the board, press Ctrl+K, run **New task from template**, and pick from the list. The new task is created in the board's first non-done column and opens immediately. Labels that were deleted after the template was saved are skipped rather than failing the creation. ### API ```http GET /api/task-templates?projectId=15 # list a board's templates POST /api/task-templates # { "taskId": 1234, "name": "Weekly review" } DELETE /api/task-templates # { "templateId": 7 } POST /api/task-templates/apply # { "templateId": 7 } ``` `name` is optional on create and defaults to the task's title. All four require membership of the board. ## My tasks **My tasks** answers "what am I working on today" across every board you belong to. The inbox remains the place to triage what arrived; this is the place to plan. **To open it:** G then M, or Ctrl+K and **Go to my tasks**, or visit `/my-tasks`. It shows every open task assigned to you as a **table**, the same table the board uses. By default the sections are due-time groups: **Overdue**, **Today**, **This week**, **Later**, and **No due date**. Overdue stays first. Use **Group** to switch to one section per board. Saved My Tasks views remember that choice. **Ordering puts urgent work first.** In time groups, Overdue is the first section. In board groups, boards that contain overdue tasks sort above boards that do not. Inside a group, overdue tasks lead, then the rest by due date, with undated tasks last. **Cross-board priority sorting.** In any table column, click the column header to sort by that column. Sorts are applied across each board's section, so you can see the highest-priority tasks at the top of the list, ordered by the board's default priority level. **Priority levels.** Tasks across all boards are sorted using the board's real priority levels: No Priority, Urgent, High, Medium, and Low. The sort uses these levels consistently regardless of the board's visual cues. **The split pills filter by board.** They still work inside a time group. "All" shows every board; picking a board narrows the table to that board alone. Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through them, exactly as on the inbox and board surfaces. **Sorting keeps the grouping.** Clicking a column header sorts within each time or board section rather than flattening everything into one list. Navigation matches the inbox and scheduled views: J and K (or the arrow keys) to move, Enter to open, Esc to go back. My tasks is a planning surface across every board you belong to. Use the quick-add row at the top to create a task on the view's default board (My Tasks asks once if none is set), or create from a board, the inbox, or Ctrl+K. ## Agent scheduling and provider selection","excerpt":"Start dates, repeating tasks, task templates, and the My tasks planning view.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840513,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/scheduling/"}

{"id":"docs-features-search","title":"Search","slug":"docs-features-search","content":"# Search Search across your board to find tasks fast. Type to filter by people, boards, labels, statuses, dates, and more, with autocomplete that suggests operators and values as you type. ## Search filters Use operators to filter tasks by specific fields: - **from:** Restrict to tasks created by a specific person. - **assignee:** Restrict to tasks assigned to a specific person. - **commenter:** Restrict to tasks commented on by a specific person. - **in:** Restrict to tasks in a board, section, or column; `board:` also filters by board. - **label:** Restrict to tasks with a specific label. - **Board-scoped label suggestions (Owner + QA preview):** - When a board is picked with an `in:` or `board:` chip, `label:` only suggests labels from that board. - Each label shows the number of search results on the right (open and done, not archived). - Labels with zero results appear at the bottom, greyed out. - Without a board selected, all your labels appear (same-name labels merged into one row). - **is:** Narrow by type; for example, `is:card` to show only standard cards. - **priority:** Filter by task priority: `priority:urgent`, `priority:high`, `priority:medium`, or `priority:low`. - **type:** Filter by result type: `type:ticket` for tickets or `type:comment` for comments. - **dates:** Show tasks matching a date condition. - `dates:2026-10-03` Tasks with this exact due date. - `dates:<2026-10-03` Tasks due before. - `dates:>2026-10-03` Tasks due after. - `dates:in-range 2026-10-01..2026-10-07` Tasks within a date range. - `dates:overdue` Overdue tasks. - `dates:today` Tasks due today. - `dates:this-week` Tasks due in the current week. - `dates:later` Tasks due beyond the current week. - `dates:todays` Tasks due today or yesterday. - **has:** Show tasks that have a value in a field. - `has:due-date` Tasks with a due date. - `has:attachment` Tasks with at least one attachment. - `has:comment` Tasks with at least one comment. - **"exact phrase":** Match an exact phrase, for example `"bug report"`. - **-word:** Exclude results containing a word, for example `-blocked`. These operators work together; combine them, for example `from:alice label:urgent dates:>2026-10-03` to find urgent tasks created by Alice after a specific date. Quoted phrases and `-word` exclusions stay plain text in the search box, rather than becoming coloured operator chips. ## Autocomplete As you type, Hypertask suggests: - **Filter names**: Type `la`, `fr`, or `is` to reveal `label:`, `from:`, and `is:` with ghost text. Press Tab or Enter to accept. - **Filter values**: After typing `from:` or `label:`, a dropdown shows people or labels. After typing `is:`, a dropdown shows states like `open`, `done`, and `archived`. - `priority:` suggests `urgent`, `high`, `medium`, and `low`. - `type:` suggests `ticket` and `comment`. - `has:` shows `attachment`, `comment`, and `due-date` options. - `dates:` shows presets: `today`, `this-week`, `last 7 days`, plus a date picker. - **Filter types have unique colours**: `from:`/`@`, `assignee:`, and `commenter:` are purple; `in:`/`#` and `board:` are blue; `label:` is rose; `is:` and `priority:` are green; dates are amber; `has:` and `type:` are cyan. Slack-style operators autocomplete with the same colours as the other operators. ## Person name matching behavior **Owner and QA preview:** - **Typed person filters**: When you type a name for `from:`, `assignee:`, and currently `commenter:`, it matches every person you can see whose name or email contains that text, ignoring case and accents. For example, `from:valentin` finds Valentin Yeo and any account named valentinyeo; `assignee:yc` finds Yusuf C. and any name containing "yc" in the email. Using `-from:valentin` excludes all those matches. - **People from the picker**: A person you select from the autocomplete list is matched exactly, so `from: Valentin Yeo` narrows to just that person. - **Without the flag**: If fuzzy person matching is off, typed person filters require the exact full name and case-sensitive search. ## Tips panel When the search bar is empty or focused, a tips panel lists every operator with an example and plain meaning. Tips include `priority:high`, `type:ticket`, `"exact phrase"`, and `-word`. Click any tip to insert it. Saved searches and recent searches also appear inside the tips panel. ## Keyboard navigation in search - **Navigate suggestions**: Use ↓ (or j) and ↑ (or k) to move through values and tips without typing. - In empty search, j/k moves through tips. - In a typed query, j/k move through results while you type. - **Accept a suggestion**: Tab or Enter inserts the pending value. - **Escape**: Closes suggestions and drops focus from the search bar. - On search results, Esc returns you to your previous search term and its results, or to recent searches and tips when there is no previous search. - Esc never leaves you on a blank results page. - **Open a result**: Put focus on a result row with arrows, then press Enter to open the task. ## Results while typing Results appear while you type via debounced search. No need to press Enter to see matching tasks. ## Chips After applying filters, clickable chips appear in the search bar. Click a chip's X to remove it. Clearing text keeps filter chips until you press Backspace one extra time. **Board chips** now display the board icon and name (e.g., `board:inne`), with no extra `#` prefix. When you type a filter operator such as `from:` or `assignee:` and select a person from the dropdown, the operator character is now absorbed into the chip itself. For example, selecting a person after typing `from valentin` results in a `from: Valentin Yeo` chip instead of leaving `from` and the person both visible. **Board tabs behavior**: When the board-tab flags are enabled and all search results come from the same board, either because you filtered to one board or because results naturally returned from a single board, the row of board tabs is hidden to keep your attention focused on that board. If the search returns tasks from multiple boards, the tabs remain visible so you can switch between them from search results. ## People and board pickers - **@ people picker**: Start typing `@` to select or create people. - **# board picker**: Start typing `#` to select or create boards. Pickers appear when typing a people or board-related operator such as `from:`, `assignee:`, or `in:`. ## New tasks appear immediately in search Tasks created through the API now appear in search results right away without needing to update their title. Previously, when you created tickets via the API without a title update, the search index would not reflect the new entries. Now, Hypertask updates the search index immediately after task creation, so the new tasks show up when you search. To verify it’s live: - Create a new task using the API or CLI with just a description. - Switch to the search screen and use a keyword from the description to see the new task appear in results. - No additional steps like editing the title are required. This change applies to all API surfaces, including the MCP tools and REST endpoints, and makes search results consistent across all task creation flows. Also fixed slow AI calls that were stalling due to fresh server startup. Slow calls now finish in half the time or less. Long pages and comments are now indexed for search. Previously very long or empty pages and comments were rejected by the AI service that generates search copies, and would not appear in results.","excerpt":"Search across tasks with operator autocomplete, filter suggestions, and a rich tips panel.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1792923257,"updated_at":1794840521,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/search/"}

{"id":"docs-features-search-screen","title":"Search Screen","slug":"docs-features-search-screen","content":"# Search Screen The search screen provides a focused, keyboard-first way to find tasks across your board. It adopts a Superhuman-inspired design: a single aligned list of recent searches and tips, grey value completions (operator and values), and keyboard-driven workflows while deferring results until selection or Enter. ## Enhanced search preview: Owner+QA only This enhanced search screen is a strict preview available to the Owner and QA roles. It is not a general release and does not require any minimum activity threshold. If you see the normal search UI, ensure you are on a checked board and the search preview flag is enabled for your account or team. ## Layout and structure Top-level search shows a consistent list: - **Recent searches**: A single list of your most recent searches. - **Tips**: Helpful hints below recent searches (operator shortcuts, example queries). - **AI panel**: Fixed on the right side, leaving the core search interface on the left. No floating boxes. The suggestions list is full-width and aligned with the search box on desktop and mobile. - **Mobile board tabs**: Under the search box, board tabs sit clearly above the bottom navigation, tapable with ample spacing and swipe-friendly when many boards exist. - **Desktop**: Board tabs follow the same layout, for the same filter behavior across devices. ## Empty and loaded states - **Empty search**: Recent searches (or none, if you have none) appear once, then tips below them. The AI panel stays fixed on the right side; the left side is free for search only. - **Loaded search**: After selecting a suggestion or pressing Enter, aligned results appear under the suggestions list. Results do not start loading until you accept a suggestion or press Enter. ## Grey inline value completion As you type, the inline suggestions box shows: - **Top suggestion**: Completed in grey inside the list. Accept with Tab. - **Operators**: Hinted inline (e.g., el: hints label:). - **Values**: Top value preview in grey (e.g., from:mal shows Malcolm Stern). This applies to common value types: people (names + emails), labels, boards. Results do not trigger while you type; they load only after you pick a suggestion or press Enter. **Example**: Type from:val; the top suggestion Valentin Yeo appears in grey; select it with Tab to trigger a board fetch and show results. ## Tips panel Under recent searches, tips explain operators the first time you open search: - Ctrl+K / Cmd+K — open command palette. - from:, assignee:, in:, label:, is:, dates:, has:, priority: — field modifiers. - "quoted phrase" — exact phrase match. - -word — exclude tasks with a word or phrase. - Press Tab on an inline value to accept it; choose Ask AI, operators, people, labels, or boards. ## Keyboard shortcuts (search UI) - Ctrl+K / Cmd+K — open command palette. - Enter — apply selected suggestion and load results. - Tab — accept and grey the top inline suggestion and load results. - Shift+Tab — previous suggestion. - Esc — clear or dismiss panels. ## Sample workflows 1. Click the search box or press /. Empty state: recent searches and tips appear. 2. Type a partial term or operator (e.g., from:mal). Inline completion shows the top value in grey. Results do not load yet. 3. Select a suggestion with Tab (or hover & click). Results load under the suggestions list. 4. Press Esc to clear and return to the recents/tips layout; results are removed. ## Status notes - This new search screen replaces the live results from the previous iconic live-results approach and works behind the existing search flags. - Verified live for Owner and QA; full release plan to widen the flag is out of scope for this documentation.","excerpt":"Superhuman-style aligned search result list with tips, grey value completions, and keyboard shortcuts. Owner+QA preview.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1792958979,"updated_at":1794840517,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/search-screen/"}

{"id":"docs-features-skills","title":"Skills","slug":"docs-features-skills","content":"Skills let you cluster related tasks, projects, and workflows around shared expertise. A skill can be anything: a domain, a technology, or a role. You can assign skills to people, filter any task list by skill, or use skills as metadata in saved views.

Use skills to surface specialized work: "React", "Schema Design", "Customer Research", or "Onboarding". Assign a skill to a person, and watch it surface in searches, assignments, and saved views.

## Save a workflow from AI chat

Ask chat to create a skill:

> Turn this session into a skill.

Or describe a workflow you want saved.
Review its name, slug, trigger, instructions and scope.
Choose personal scope or the current board.
Confirm the draft to save it.
Or request edits or reject the draft.
Edits need another preview before saving.
Nothing saves until you confirm the draft.
If the slug exists, approve an update instead.

Use `/slug` in chat, comments, or Task Writer.
Ctrl+J also supports saved skills.

## Create & assign skills

Skills are scoped to: personal (for you), project (for a board), or team (for all members of that team). When you assign a skill to a person, the assignment is also scoped to the skill’s scope, so a team-level skill appears in each project’s skill list.

1. **Open Skill management**
   - Use the **Ctrl+K** command palette and search for **"Skills"**, or go to the **Settings > Skills** page.

2. **Create a skill**
   - Click **New Skill**.
   - Give it a name (e.g., "Python" or "Design System").
   - Optionally add a description.
   - Choose the scope:
     - **Personal** — skill available only to you.
     - **Project** — skill available on a specific board/project.
     - **Team** — skill available to all members of your team, regardless of project.

3. **Assign a person**
   - On the skill card, click **Assign People**.
   - Search for a team member and add them.
   - Assignments are scoped: a personal skill assignment is only visible to you; a project assignment is only visible on that project’s board.

4. **Backlog/assign tasks by skill**
   - Filter a task list by skill using the skill picker.
   - Or assign a skill to a task to tag it for later filtering or reporting.
   - Saved views can also explicitly filter by skill.

## Run a skill from a ticket comment

Start writing a comment on any ticket. Type `/`, then choose an available skill. Use Enter or click to choose the skill.

The AI chat sidebar opens with its answer. The skill reads the ticket and your draft. Your comment stays editable and unposted.

### /prototype skill

You can now create a **/prototype** skill to define a shared prototype format across agents and collaboration tools. When someone inserts a prototype with this skill:

- The prototype becomes clickable in comments and AI chat.
- The default action is to open and display the prototype in the same context.
- The prototype’s slug is inserted into comments and prompts, making it easy to reference and reuse.
- If the prototype has its own action URL, the UI presents standard context‑appropriate actions:
  - **Comment composer**: click the prototype card to insert its slug; opening the prototype works the same way as other skills.
  - **AI chat**: pick /prototype from the command menu, then engage with the prototype in the same way you would any other skill.

Use the /prototype skill to streamline reference workflows: embed consistent embed URLs and referenceable slugs for MP4s, PNGs, and hosted prototypes. Agents and collaborators can open, inspect, and reference them without leaving their current flow.

### Use a skill when writing a new task

Press **Ctrl+J**, start your note with the skill's slug (for example `/deeper`), and send it. The AI writes the task using that skill, then opens the task with the AI chat.

As soon as you type `/`, a skill picker opens under your cursor, the same one the AI task writer shows. Keep typing to filter it, use the arrow keys to move, and press **Enter** or **Tab** to insert the skill. **Escape** closes only the picker, so your note stays open.

The chat's first message tells you which skill shaped the task and what changed compared with your note. It then lists concerns, ideas and follow-up questions for this task. Click a suggested question below the message to ask it in the same chat.

If no skill was used, or the skill was edited or removed after the task was written, the chat shows the usual short intro instead.

### Example agent use case

An agent that manages design reviews might:

- Use the /prototype skill to indicate designs under review.
- In a comment, insert the prototype slug to surface the linked prototype card.
- Ready the prototype for quick, context‑appropriate opening by teammates.

### Keyboard workflow

Quickly assign or filter by skill using your keyboard:

- **Ctrl+K** — Command palette; start typing **"Skill"** to find:
  - **Skills** — Open Skill management.
  - **Filter tasks by skill** — Pop up the skill selector.

- Use the skill picker in a board or task detail to click or navigate with arrow keys to select skills.

### Data model (for integrators)

- **Scope** — `personal` | `project` | `team`.
- A skill on a board applies only when that board is opened.
- A project skill applies across all boards in that project.
- A team skill applies automatically to all boards that your team owns.

[Keyboard Shortcuts](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/keyboard-shortcuts/)

    Use keyboard workflows to surf tasks and filter by skill.

[CLI Reference](https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/reference/)

    Manage skills from the terminal with full CRUD and import.

[Agent Workflows](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/workflows/)

    Patterned ways agents can pick up and complete work scoped by skill.","excerpt":"Create, manage, and import skills to organize your team's expertise and filter by them in queries and saved views.","category":"Features & How-To","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840525,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/skills/"}
