{"id":"docs-features-tasks","title":"Tasks","slug":"docs-features-tasks","content":"# Tasks A task represents a unit of work that can be assigned, progressed, and tracked. It supports rich fields, priority levels, relationships, and subtasks. ## My Tasks **My Tasks** is your personal task list across boards. By default it shows tasks assigned to you. The list groups by due time: **Overdue**, **Today**, **This week**, **Later**, and **No due date**. Overdue stays at the top. Use **Group** to switch back to board groups. Saved My Tasks views remember the choice. One row of tabs sits on top, your saved views. Use **Scope** to narrow the list to some boards, and **Group: Board** to see one section per board with its count. ### Scope in My Tasks Improvement The **Scope** button in My Tasks and the standard **Scope** command in Ctrl+K now open the same board picker list. The panel has been redesigned to match the board picker you use throughout the app, with search and standard keyboard navigation for quick filtering and selection. The previous, custom implementation has been replaced with the consistent board picker experience. ### Bulk selection and actions on My Tasks You can select multiple tasks in the **My Tasks** view using the keyboard shortcut **G**, followed by **M**, to enter multi-select mode. This mirrors the selection behavior from the Kanban board for a consistent workflow. Once in multi-select mode: - **Verify your selection**: Each task you want to act on is checked. If viewing a filtered list, only tasks that are both checked and visible are included in the action. - **Apply bulk actions**: The following actions are available at the bottom of the list: - Archive - Assign - Label - Move to column - Delete - **Unselect**: Press **G** again or press **U** to exit multi-select mode. Selected rows persist until you commit an action, so you can review the working set before bulk-actioning multiple tasks. > **Tip**: The selection model matches the way you select tasks in Kanban, so if you are comfortable bulk-archiving or moving tasks on a board, the pattern transfers directly to My Tasks. ### Tasks you're snoozed on To temporarily hide tasks from your My Tasks view, set a **snooze**. When you snooze until a date: - The task no longer appears in My Tasks until that date passes - The snooze date sets a calendar reminder so you can resurface the task later A snooze is per task and independent of other views. Tasks remain otherwise accessible from boards, calendars, and saved views. ### Saved views You can create and manage saved views on My Tasks to customize what you see. These views support: - **Full filtering**: Filter by title, assignee, priority, due date, labels, and more. Filter options match the Kanban board filter menu, so you can use familiar screen-level controls directly on My Tasks. - **Sorting**: Sort by any of the same fields, with priority as the primary sort key. - **Board selection**: Show tasks from one board or across multiple boards. - **Done columns hidden by default**: Done columns are hidden within each view to focus on active work. Saved views persist at the account level and can be used as templates for board filter setups. ### How it works When you toggle a filter, sort order, or board, your selection is saved with the view. The next time you open that view, the settings are applied automatically. You can create multiple views for example, one for active prioritized tasks, one for a specific project, or any combination that matches your workflow. To create a saved view, open My Tasks and use the view toolbar to pick filters and sorting options, then select **Save view**. The view appears in the saved views list alongside system views like **Involvement** and **All tasks**. ### Excluding tasks you don't need To hide distracting or temporary tasks: - Use **View filters** to show or hide assignments, priorities, or tags that don't match your current focus. - Create and pin a custom view with the exact criteria you want to see. - Review tasks by tag or priority and archive or move them away when no longer relevant. > **Note:** Saved views are scoped to the current team. Cross-board filters and sorting are supported, so you can see, for example, all high-priority inbox tasks across all boards in a single custom view. ### All Tasks view The **All Tasks** view provides an at-a-glance overview of every active task across the board. It builds split views for each board section (To Do, In Progress, Done, etc.) from a single source of truth. To access this view, navigate to the board and select **All Tasks** from the view toolbar. ### How All Tasks works All Tasks uses a single fetch pass that loads rows once and builds board splits from those rows. As a result: - Each board sees its own split of the task list. - Quiet boards do not lose splits in favor of busy boards. - The view is stable and deterministic across sessions. ### Drawing from multiple streams Since All Tasks is board-wide, it aggregates tasks from all active columns and sections, making it useful for a quick health check or high-level tracking when you need to see everything that matters—not just what's pinned or currently in one section. **Note:** Unlike **My Tasks** saved views, All Tasks does not automatically filter out onboarding, demo, template, and staging content, so those tasks may appear in the list. For visibility filtering, see [Board & Subtask Visibility](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/board-visibility/). ### Search filters When searching within a board or in saved views, you can now narrow results using search operators on fields: - **from:** Restrict to tasks created by a specific user. - **assignee:** Restrict to tasks assigned to a specific person. - **in:** Restrict to tasks in a board, section, or column. - **label:** Restrict to tasks with a specific label. - **is:** Narrow by task type; for example, `is:card` to show only standard cards. - **dates:** Show tasks with dates matching a condition (by default, **by due**), or filter by due date ranges. - `dates:2026-09-30` For tasks with that exact due date. - `dates:<2026-09-30` For tasks due before. - `dates:>2026-09-30` For tasks due after. - `dates:in-range 2026-09-01..2026-09-30` For tasks due within the range. - `dates:overdue` For tasks marked overdue. - `dates:today` For tasks due today. - `dates:this-week` For tasks due within the current week. - `dates:later` For tasks due later than the current week. - `dates:todays` For tasks due on today and the day prior. - **has:** Show tasks that have a value in a field; for example, `has:due-date` for tasks that have a due date (including empty values) or `has:assignee` for tasks that have someone assigned. - Combining multiple operators is supported—for example, `from:alice label:urgent dates:>2026-09-30` to find urgent tasks created by Alice after a certain date. To apply search filters: 1. Open **Kanban** or **Table View**. 2. On the board header (or in the saved view toolbar), select **Filter**. 3. Choose a field and an operator, then enter a value or pick from the options. 4. Repeat for additional filters to narrow the list. Search filters apply at the board level in Kanban and in saved views. The available operators depend on the board's configuration. ### Chips in the search bar New The search bar includes: - **Chips**: Select or refine filters after your search, then click to apply chips. Click the × on a chip to remove it. - @ people picker: Start typing the @ symbol to select or create people. - # board picker: Start typing # to select or create boards. ## My Tasks toolbar Behavior change The My Tasks toolbar now uses icon-only controls with tooltips for Involvement, Columns, Scope, Filters, Sort, and Group. Active controls turn blue like Kanban, and Group shows its current choice. Overdue tooltips on red counts now appear over each overdue item. The toolbar also uses the same Save view and Reset controls as Kanban board views. From the **Ctrl+K** command palette, you can still use **Save view as** to create a saved view, and **Reset view** to revert My Tasks to its default set of built-in filters. Keyboard shortcuts like **Ctrl+S** and **Ctrl+R** no longer open popovers on the board; they now open the Save view and Reset dialogs respectively. This change makes view management across My Tasks and other board views more consistent, and ensures My Tasks mirrors the primary board interface. ## Creating a task From a board or inbox, click **New task** (or use the keyboard shortcut **Ctrl+N** / Cmd+N). This opens the task creator with the following top-level sections: - **Title**: The name or headline of the work. - **Description**: Optional text explaining what to do. - **Assignees**: One or more members to get notified and held accountable. - **Sections & Columns**: Drag the task to a section or use the section picker dropdown. - **Due date**: Pick a date or use predictive phrases like "tomorrow," "next week," or relative periods. - **Priority**: Choose Low, Medium, or High. - **Estimated time**: Optionally specify hours or a low-high range if needed. Use **Write with AI** (**Ctrl+K** / Cmd+K, or the command palette) in the description area to turn a brief task idea into a fleshed-out task. ### New Task creator New The task creator window (formerly the "Compose" button) can be opened from any view with **Ctrl+J** / Cmd+J and is now live for everyone. The window behaves like a task creator with Search and New Task tabs, Ctrl+K and Ctrl+J tooltips, and Tab/Shift+Tab switching. It retains your old window size and grows as you type, and the New Task button is renamed to **New Task**. On desktop, click the primary **New Task** plus button in the left sidebar to open the same window. Expand the sidebar to see its label. Hover shows **Ctrl+J**, or **Cmd+J** on Mac. Mobile keeps its existing new-task button. ### Edit a task with AI New Click **Edit with AI** under a task's description to open the AI chat in the sidebar on that task. It asks "How do you want to edit this task?" and offers ready-made requests: **Rewrite in plain words**, **Shorten the title**, **Add acceptance criteria**, **Split into sub-tasks**, and **Turn the error log into steps to reproduce**. Pick one or type your own, and the chat updates the task in place. The AI button in the description and comment editor opens the same chat. On an open task, **Ctrl+J** / Cmd+J still opens the New Task window. ### AI writer failure reasons Fix When the AI writer fails to generate a task, the **Ctrl+J New Task** box and the AI Task Writer now show the real failure reason instead of hiding it; your note is still saved as a task. If AI generation is not available, the text you entered appears without modification. This applies to task creation from boards, the inbox, and description editing in task details. ## Field validation Some fields are type-checked before submission. For example, the **ranking** parameter must be a string; passing a number will fail with an error. ## OAuth connection flow When Hypertask connects to a board from an external site or app, Hypertask now shows an **approve screen** first. The screen names the connector and the exact site that will receive access, letting you confirm before any access is granted. This prevents a signed-in user from inadvertently granting external sites access to their entire board without prior approval. ## Managing task details Open a task to view and edit all its fields. Unsupported columns or fields may be hidden based on your team's board configuration. ### Priorities Assign a clear priority (Low, Medium, or High) to reflect the task's importance and replacement cost. Higher priorities should be shown ahead of lower ones in lists, table view, and filters. ### Assignees - Added assignees trigger notifications to the task's assignees. If no assignee is specified, the task is unassigned. - Workers can have their own assignee field, tracked separately from human assignees. Workers appear in the Relationships section under the *Workers* relation type. ### Due dates Click a date to pick another date or remove it. The date affects due date pickers and filter views. Predictive phrases like "tomorrow," "next week," and relative periods also persist. ### Estimated time Type hours or a low-high range for time-tracking integration. ### Section & column Drag tasks between sections to change their column. This can trigger auto-assign rules if configured. In Table view, you can also drag any row onto another section's card; the row is the drag handle, the section card is the drop target, and the change surfaces immediately in both views (Column sort must be off for this to work; on /my-tasks, rows are grouped by time or board, so dragging doesn't target a section directly). ### Description edition UX To edit the task description: - On desktop: Click or tap the description area, then edit. - Mobile: Double-tap the description to open the editor; a single tap remains in read mode. If you are the **Task Reporter** (see below), you can edit the description directly. Only the Task Reporter can edit the description. ### Task Reporter With the **Task Reporter**, anyone on the task can update the task description directly. The Task Reporter indicator visually appears alongside comment headers, making it clear who has opened the description for editing just like comments. ### Permissions - **Task Reporter** is available to any human assignee or worker on a task. The feature is not available for closed tasks. - When you open the description in edit mode, you become the **Task Reporter** for that task. - Only the Task Reporter can edit the description. This prevents concurrent edits and restores the semantic meaning of "owner of the description field". - If you close the description without saving any changes, the status clears and the next person to open it becomes the Task Reporter. This model ensures a clear ownership of the description field, similar to comment ownership, which helps teams coordinate around tasks without stepping on each other's work. Note: While you are the Task Reporter, you cannot switch to another task description edit until the current edit state closes, preserving a single active description edit at a time. ### Saved attachments - To remove an attachment, open the description in edit mode, click the attachment you want to remove, and save. Only the items you deselect will be removed; remaining attachments are preserved as one copy each. Fix A previous bug caused the wrong attachment files to be saved when removing items from a description. When you had two or more description files attached, removing one would incorrectly save a duplicate of the other file. This is now fixed so that always only one copy of each remaining attachment is saved. Fix Deleting a task no longer creates an invalid undoable state. Undo is now always possible when restoring from deletion, ensuring tasks can be fully recovered and the undo system behaves consistently. Fix Undo functionality has been consolidated under a single restoring rule. This ensures that restoring tasks after deletion behaves the same whether you use the Undo button or Ctrl+Z, with consistent behavior tracked through the board's undo history. ### Agent lease interactions When you make manual changes to a task—"moving, assigning, unassigning, archiving, or deleting"—Hypertask cancels any active agent lease on that task and persists the change. Human modifications take priority over agent tasks, but agent-versus-agent collision protection remains in place. This ensures your task updates are never blocked by an agent while you're working. ## Task detail view Open a task to see: - Header with title, status section, assignees, workers, priority, and due date. - Description area with optional attachments. - Sections: Comments, Relations, Subtasks, Times, and Pages. - Task Reporter indicator marking who can edit the description. - **Top bar** with instant navigation and actions: - ← **Back to task** — Settings-style back button for navigation. On mobile, the back control matches the app's mobile back style with normal side spacing, making it easy to tap and fully visible up to 390px wide. - **Save** — Only right-aligned action remaining in the top bar; **Delete** is now moved to the **Undo** action in the Actions section. ### Linked pull requests Tasks can link to GitHub pull requests. The pull request section displays each linked PR with its status: - **Open, Merged, Closed**: Show the current status as reported by GitHub. - **Last observed**: The last-known status before the page loads. - **Fetching...**: Indicates a background refresh is in progress. Improvement Tasks with linked PRs now show any saved PR status immediately—Open, Merged, or Closed—without waiting for GitHub to respond. Queries to GitHub run in parallel in the background and update the panel once the fetch completes, keeping the page fast and responsive. If you navigate away and come back, the PR panel refreshes again to stay current. This change eliminates wait times for tasks with linked PRs and provides an instant-open experience even when GitHub fetches are slower than usual. Security Hypertask now verifies that incoming PR updates come from known GitHub accounts before accepting them. By default, this restriction applies only to board 15. Except for board 15, an updated PR can link to any public repository, and the update is accepted as long as it originates from a trusted GitHub account. For board 15, only PR updates from three specified accounts are permitted: Valentin Yeo and two others configured by the board team. This prevents unauthorized actors from creating, moving, or commenting on tasks in board 15 via external PRs. ### Comments The comment thread shows all comments on the task. By default, when you open a task with comments, the newest comment remains expanded so you can see the latest conversation. Link handling Plain web addresses in ticket descriptions and comments (http:// or https://) are automatically transformed into clickable links. Detects addresses based on recognized URL patterns, ensuring links in work notes and teammate discussions remain navigable on both desktop and mobile. Performance improvement When you open a task, comments now load once instead of twice. The initial SSR data used as the starting point, with React Query configured to skip a second fetch if the data is fresh. This eliminates redundant data handling and speeds up task loads: repeat visits are now approximately 0.6 seconds faster. New and edited comments still appear automatically without a reload, and realtime invalidation, reconnect reconciliation, and window-focus refresh continue to work as expected. Improvement Long task pages and comment threads now send their initial snapshot only once, reducing data copies and decoding passes. Repeat visit times drop from roughly 2.2 seconds to about 0.6 seconds. The change applies to tasks with many comments or long descriptions and focuses on the initial load speed, preserving all existing behavior for navigation, real-time updates, and comment handling. Fix The comment box on ticket pages is now positioned immediately below the last comment instead of appearing in the middle of the task. It previously moved under the task description, causing the interface to split the comment content unnaturally. The comment section now renders after other content and before the top bar, keeping comments at the bottom of the page as expected. Fix A shared comment link now opens on that comment instead of the ticket top, with the comment visible on screen on both desktop and mobile. The link scrolls directly to the referenced comment when you open it—for example, from Slack or email—making it easier to reference specific points in a conversation. This fix improves navigation for long threads with hundreds of comments and helps ticket descriptions stay readable even on narrow phones. ### Actions Common actions include: - **Back**: Navigate back to the board using the ← Back to task button. - **Move**: Relocate the task to a different section, board, or project. - **Duplicate**: Create a copy with the same fields. When duplicating a task, the new task includes the full description and can be copied to another board in one step (see board-level Duplicate in the [Boards & Sections](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/boards/) docs). - **Archive**: Hide the task from current views while keeping it in the archive. - **Delete**: Permanently remove the task. Undo appears on the notification after deletion, clicking **Undo** restores the task to its previous column and keeps it available for future edits. For bulk deletions, undo restores all affected tasks together and still works with Ctrl / Cmd+Z. Fix Opening a ticket now downloads its details once, and board cards stay up to date. Before this fix, opening a task from the board or by its link would trigger 2 to 3 redundant data fetches. Fix On mobile, tapping a board card no longer loads the task page twice. The board now shows the task without redundant data fetches, eliminating a flash or stutter that previously occurred. This fix applies across all boards and resizes, keeping the board-tap experience smooth. Security Tasks can link to GitHub pull requests. Board 15 now accepts automatic PR updates only from three known GitHub accounts: Valentin Yeo and two others configured by the board team, preventing outsiders from creating tasks, moving them to review, or commenting via PRs. Security A person who is not on a board can no longer add labels to it or modify label assignments on tasks. Outsiders now receive a Forbidden error, while board members continue to manage labels as before. Security A team-only share link no longer exposes task content to outsiders. Before, the page sent the whole task and comments to unauthenticated users who only saw blurred content. Now an outsider sees an empty page with a Sign in or Login bar and cannot see task details or comments. Security When you attempt to move or nest a task under another task on an inaccessible board, the operation is refused and nothing is saved. Hypertask validates board boundaries before allowing parent-child relationships across unrelated teams, preventing accidental exposure of foreign task titles or context. ## Relations between tasks Create relationships between tasks to surface context without leaving tasks: - **Block**: Mark a task as blocking another task. - **Blocked by**: Identify what indirectly holds a task back. - **Duplicate**: Link to other tasks that represent the same work item. - **Workers**: Associate an agent or intelligent agent with the task for scheduling and coordination. See a task's relations in the **Relations** section of the task detail view. ## Subtasks Break down a task into smaller units. Subtasks appear in the task detail under the **Subtasks** section. Mark them complete to show progress toward the parent task. Add one from the parent task's **Subtasks** section. The window lists tasks you can link as a sub-task, and the **New sub-task** button under the search box opens the normal create window with the parent already attached. Typing a name that matches nothing still creates a new sub-task when you press Enter. ## Task property rail The task detail sidebar includes a rail of properties (title, priority, assignees, labels, etc.). The rail now occupies the full remaining dynamic viewport height, so it uses all available space rather than a fixed maximum and leaves no unused viewport space. **Task properties no longer scroll with the task thread**, keeping them pinned to the sidebar for easy access while browsing comments and history. When another browser, the CLI, or an agent changes a task, its open detail page refreshes the title, assignees, labels, priority, dates, status, attachments, and linked pull requests without a reload. If the live connection is unavailable, the page checks for changes every 10 seconds. ## Time tracking Track work hours on tasks via the **Times** section: - **B** opens the time entry modal from the task, or use the command palette ("Log time"). - Manual per-day rows let you log time for any calendar day without a timer. - Export time logs as CSV for payroll or reporting. See the [Time Tracking](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/time-tracking/) guide for full details. ## AI Task Writer The AI Task Writer is a prompt-based task creation flow that generates complete, shippable tickets from paste inputs. ### How it works today The Task Writer writes tasks in your team's style. It uses board-aware prompts, pulls task templates from boards, and uses search to find related tickets instead of inventing them. ### Using the Task Writer - From a board: **Ctrl+J** / Cmd+J and select **Create with AI** — **Task Writer**. - From the command palette: **Ctrl+K** — search for "Task Write" and select it. - From a task: Click the AI icon in the task header and select **Task Writer**. After the Task Writer generates a draft, you can refine it just like any other AI-generated comment or description. ### Board task templates Save a representative ticket through **Ctrl+K → Save as template**. Open **Settings → Board → Task templates** to edit its name, title pattern, and description structure. Use names such as **Bug** or **A/B test** so the writer can match your request to the right template. Simple descriptions support headings written with `##` and plain paragraphs. Rich descriptions remain read-only here to preserve their formatting; you can still change their names and title patterns. If someone else saves first, reload before saving your changes. When you explicitly request ideas, the writer fills them in one pass using board tickets, documents, memory, and custom instructions. For example, “Write an A/B test with five headlines” produces five finished headlines, not placeholders. A matched template's title pattern and headings stay in place. Required ICE scores include the component scores and mark estimates. Ordinary editing requests still preserve your source instead of inventing copy. ## Instant ticket opening New Tickets now load instantly from cached board data, with no spinner, no "Loading..." text, and no placeholder animation. The entire opening experience is fast and lag-free across desktop and mobile. ### What you see - **Click to open**: When you tap or click a task, it appears in about 0.15 to 0.3 seconds on both desktop and mobile. - **No loading animation**: No full-screen spinner, no pulsing grey bars, no brief placeholder state. - **Suggested questions right away**: If the AI panel is open, suggested questions appear immediately—not waiting for the API response. ### Browser history The browser back and forward buttons now behave consistently with the app: - Press **Back** to return to the board. The board remains loaded and you can stay there. - Press **Forward** to re-open the last ticket you viewed. This lets you browse through tasks inside the app while the rest of your session stays tight and fast. ### Performance details - Median open times are ~0.15 seconds on desktop and ~0.17 seconds on mobile. - The first open after a board loads takes about 0.25 to 0.33 seconds; subsequent opens are closer to 0.13 to 0.18 seconds. - The first open after a board loads now paints its cached title and description before expensive editing property controls, so the title and description appear instantly while controls like assignees, status, and priority still warm. This tighter paint-first sequence reduces the first-open delta to about 0.10 seconds—considerably faster than before. ### Visual smoothness Fix Ticket pages no longer shift or jitter after opening. Visual elements that previously filled in after the initial paint now appear instantly as part of the cached board data, keeping the title, description, and controls in place across desktop and mobile for all test accounts. ### Keyboard shortcuts We recommend using keyboard shortcuts to navigate: - **Ctrl+J** / Cmd+J to jump to a task or open it with the Task Writer. - **Ctrl+O** / Cmd+O to jump to a task or link from within the task detail. These shortcuts preserve the instant-open feel and keep you moving without page spins or wait states. ### Assignee persistence Improvement When you assign a task from the assign picker, closing the picker or pressing Escape no longer drops the assignment. The human assignee name stays on the task and persists across page reloads and subsequent checks. This applies whether you assign from the board card or from a direct task link. ### Faster task opening Improved Pressing **Back** after opening a subtask now shows the parent task immediately instead of the subtask, with no "Loading..." flash, and **Forward** returns you to the subtask if needed. Opening a task directly from cached data shows it reliably within about 0.3 seconds on both desktop and mobile, eliminating previous delays. ### Navigating to previous titles in Inbox Improved Using **J** or the arrow keys to move to the next Inbox item now loads and displays it within about 0.3 seconds on desktop and mobile, removing lag that previously held up the wrong ticket title for up to several seconds. ### No flash of the ticket title after opening a board card Fixed Pressing **Back** right after opening a board card now shows the board immediately, with no flash of the ticket title. In at least 19 of 20 quick Backs (within 0.3 seconds of opening a card), you see only the board, not the ticket, and the board is visible within 1 second. ### Task detail downloads once Fix Opening a ticket now downloads its details once, and board cards stay up to date. Before this fix, opening a task from the board or by its link would trigger 2 to 3 redundant data fetches. ### Board tap loading Fix On mobile, tapping a board card no longer loads the task page twice. The board now shows the task without redundant data fetches, eliminating a flash or stutter that previously occurred. This fix applies across all boards and resizes, keeping the board-tap experience smooth. ### Faster open on cold phone Improved Opening a task on a cold phone with no cached data now shows its title and description sooner (11.8 s vs 14.1 s median, 95th-percentile gap of ~2.3 s). The first load paints the title and description earlier, while controls like assignee and priority still warm up afterward, keeping the experience instant and frictionless. ### Ticket page no longer shifts on mobile Fix The ticket page no longer jumps on first load. The comment box appears once and never moves: 20 of 20 fresh loads on two test accounts, on both desktop and phone. Visual elements that previously filled in after the initial paint now appear immediately as part of the cached board data, keeping the title, description, and controls in place across platforms for all test accounts. ### Comments no longer jump with content Behavior change The comment box and comment thread no longer shift downward as content loads, so the task layout stays consistent across desktop and mobile from open to load. ### Instant board tap New Clicking a board card now initializes the task with a single board interaction instead of triggering redundant rendering. This keeps the opening experience snappy across desktop and mobile, especially after boards have already been reloaded. Loading address-bar updates that occur as part of the navigation are tracked correctly as navigations within the same page rather than distinct page loads. The change applies across all boards and view types—Kanban, table, and card lists—with consistent, performant behavior. ## Invited-in aspects and board validation Improved Pages that use invite links now validate board context before sending requests. **My Tasks** and **Inbox** no longer fire invite-link requests without an associated board, which previously caused console errors for unmatched requests. With this fix, such invalid requests now surface a clear, user-facing message instead of a server error, keeping the console clean and providing explicit feedback when a board context is required.","excerpt":"Create, assign, and manage tasks with rich fields, priorities, relations, and subtasks.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840549,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/tasks/"}

{"id":"docs-features-time-tracking","title":"Time Tracking","slug":"docs-features-time-tracking","content":"### Start a timer or log time manually Use **/time** from the command palette to open the time tracking interface: - **Timer mode**: Select a task on a board or table, or open its detail page, then press W to start or stop its timer - **Per-ticket time log modal**: Press B (or Cmd+K — "Log time") on an open ticket to open an in-place dialog (day-grouped entries with a total and inline add row for any date and duration; total updates in real time as you add rows) Both modes support saving the entry directly from the form. ### Show task totals on boards and tables Enable **Settings → General → Time tracking → Show total time on tasks** to see each task's accumulated time without opening it. - Board cards show the total as quiet text. An active total turns green and advances live. - Table view adds a sortable **Time** column. Use **Configure table columns** to hide, show, or reorder it. - Concurrent timers all contribute to the live total. Paused timers remain frozen. - The setting is board-specific and off by default. Disabling time tracking also hides totals. ### Navigation on the time reports page The **/time** view includes the standard app navigation rail, giving you quick access to Board, Calendar, Inbox, AI, and Search from anywhere on the time reports page. ### React to the per-ticket time log modal The per-ticket time log modal in the task detail view links to the broader **/time** view. Click **See all time entries** (or use the link in the modal header) to open `/time?board=&task=` in a new tab. The /time view then: - Loads the board and task parameters from the URL - Shows the time log for that specific task instead of a filtered list - Includes an add/edit entry form with full Hours/Minutes, date, and note fields - Displays all existing time entries grouped by date for the selected task This makes it easy to navigate from a quick check of tracked time on a ticket into a detailed log with bulk actions (add rows, edit, delete). ### Time reports in Light Mode Time reports render correctly across Light and Dark themes: - Reports display with clear borders to distinguish rows and columns. - Light mode backdrops use the container background color (white for Light theme) rather than transparent or missing borders, ensuring legibility on typical white backgrounds. - Fields like duration, assignee, and note remain fully visible and accessible; related labels and totals are legible without cross-out or missing content. ### Use filters to view reports The **/time** view aggregates time across your workspace. Board owners and admins can report on everyone’s entries for boards they manage. Regular board members see only their own history. | Filter | Description | |--------|-------------| | **Team** | Boards you can access in a team | | **Board** | Specific board or project scope | | **User** | Individual user, available when you own or administer a board in the selected scope | | **Range** | Last 7 days, month-to-date, or custom date picker | | **Group** | By task, board, user, or date | Filters are saved per prompt so you can quickly reapply the same view. ### Time report date presets Select a date range from the start of the report: | Preset | Description | |--------|-------------| | **Yesterday** | Entries from the previous calendar day | | **Last week** | Entries from the last full 7-day period | | **Last month** | Entries from the previous full month | | **Custom** | Open a date picker with From and To fields | ### Time report interaction For any filter view that shows a duration: - **Click a duration** to open an in-depth time log modal for that row, with the full entry history and ability to add or edit entries - This modal is basically the same view opened from the per-ticket time log on a ticket ### Time report entry form UI When adding or editing time entries, the time report entry form includes: - **Duration input**: Accept HH:MM format, integer minutes, or split hours/minutes. A dedicated Hours and Minutes field makes selecting exact durations easier than combining them. - **High-precision duration support**: Use h:mm:ss format for exact precision (e.g., `0:45:30` for 45 minutes and 30 seconds). The system stores durations at the second level for accurate reporting. - **Date picker field**: Fully clickable date field that opens the calendar popover for quick selection - **Multi-select filters per entry**: Board and User checkboxes toggle per entry; rows can be bulk selected with checkboxes, deleted in bulk, or exported to CSV - **Entry-level local timestamps**: Each manual entry is stored as local-noon timestamps so logs are correctly associated with the logged day, even across time zones This UX appears in both the per-ticket time log modal and the broader time report when adding rows. Each entry stays on a single line; the person's name truncates instead of every field wrapping on its own row. ### Time log filters The time log modal also supports quick filters: | Filter | Description | |--------|-------------| | **Assignee** | Filter entries by who logged them; real assignee filter helps surface who actually worked on a task rather than who merely received it | | **All dates** | Show all time entries regardless of date | | **Today / This week** | Quick-finishing filters for common work periods | ### View and export CSV reports After applying filters, click **Export** to download a comma-separated values (CSV) file: - Formatted for Excel and Google Sheets with decimal hours - No injected formulas or formatting artifacts - Includes task number, description, user, duration, date, and note CSV export supports the same range and group filters as the time report. ### Prompt shortcuts Use these prompt patterns when entering time tracking queries:
!time today
Entries for the current day
!time task = T-123
Entries on task T-123
!time board = Marketing
Entries on the Marketing board
!time me last week
Your entries from the previous week
### Quiet rows mode Toggle **Quiet rows** in the view toolbar to hide the time cell for less verbose views. This keeps the table compact while preserving edit/delete access to each entry. ### Save a "what is running now" view **Has a running timer** is a filter like any other, so a saved view can hold it permanently instead of relying on the temporary board toggle. It works in table layout as well as on the board. The filter needs time tracking enabled on the board; with it off, or with nothing running, it matches nothing rather than everything. ### Pause and resume a timer On the running-timers overview, **Pause** freezes a timer in place and **Resume** continues the same total. The row stays listed while paused, showing **Paused** where the end time would be, and its elapsed count stops moving everywhere it appears: the overview, the task-detail indicator, and the board card badge. **A paused gap is never billed.** Stopping a timer while it is paused ends it at the moment you paused, not at the moment you pressed stop, so a timer left paused overnight charges the work rather than the night. Starting a paused timer again resumes it instead of leaving it frozen. Pause and resume are available in the app and via the MCP API endpoints `/api/time/pause` and `/api/time/resume`. The CLI and MCP surfaces can start, stop, and log time, and their payloads report whether a timer is paused, but they cannot pause or resume one yet. ### Timer indicators - **Running timer badge**: Appears in the Kanban header (Ctrl+K view) showing the number of active timers on the board - **Per-board persistence**: Timer state is scoped per board — starting a timer on one board doesn't affect timers on other boards - **Rail timer icon**: When time tracking is enabled, the App shell rail shows a **Timer** icon that opens the running-timers view #### Start a timer 1. Select a task on the board or table, or open its detail page 2. Press W — the timer starts automatically 3. Press W again to stop and save the entry #### Log time on an open ticket 1. On an open ticket, press B (or Cmd+K — "Log time") 2. Day-grouped time entries appear with rows for each calendar day and a total at the top 3. Click **Add row** to create a new entry for any date; type a duration in HH:MM or minutes (e.g., `1:30` or `90m`) 4. Enter separate **Hours** and **Minutes** values for precise durations (e.g., 1 hour 30 minutes) 5. Adjust the date, duration, and optional note per row; the Board and User fields are multi-select checkboxes per entry 6. Total updates in real time; click **Save** or press Return to commit all entries #### See detailed entries for a task 1. Click the time cell on a board card to open the per-ticket time log modal 2. Click **See all time entries** in the modal header to open `/time?board=&task=` 3. The /time view shows the full time log, edit/add forms, and filters for that specific task 4. Add additional entries directly from the /time view using Hours/Minutes or minutes #### Refine filter views 1. Open `/time` from the command palette 2. Select filters from the Dropdown panel: - **Team**, **Board**, **User**, **Range**, **Group** 3. Click **Save filters** to prompt-saved states 4. Quickly re-open saved filters from the left panel #### Export data 1. Apply filters you want to export 2. Click **Export CSV** 3. Open in Excel or Google Sheets — times display as decimal hours ready for calculations ### Keyboard shortcut summary
W on a board, table, or task detail page
Starts/stops a timer on the selected task
B on a ticket (open ticket only)
Opens the per-ticket time log modal (in-place dialog; fires only outside text inputs)
Cmd+K — "Log time"
Time log modal on any open ticket via the command palette
7 on the App shell rail (when time tracking is enabled)
Opens the running-timers overview
Option+T or Alt+T on an open task
Starts/stops the open task timer in the task detail
Technical notes - The `/time` interface includes an integrated header with no floating back button (consistent with settings-style pages) - Report API supports query parameters: `?board=&task=&user=me&running` - Manual entries use integer and decimal hours for duration (you can enter an integer like `3` or HH:MM format like `2h 30m`), then the system converts to decimal hours (e.g., `2h 30m = 2.5h`) - Timer state is stored as `startTime` and `endTime` timestamps relative to the board scope - Per-ticket time log entries live under the ticket's time tracking row and are grouped by day with a running total - Time report now includes date presets (Yesterday, Last week, Last month, Custom), clickable durations, and split Hours/Minutes fields - The time log modal and /time entry form support Hours, Minutes, h:mm:ss precision, and per-date local-noon storage with multi-select filters per entry - The `/time` view now includes the standard app navigation rail - Fixed recurrence date logic: long-abandoned fixed-period recurrences are fast-forwarded instead of stopping at 400 steps, preventing occurrences from spawning in the past
[Inbox & Notifications](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/inbox/) Stay on top of assignments, mentions, and task updates with a unified inbox.","excerpt":"Track time on tasks with W, log time manually from the command palette, review reports, and export CSV.","category":"Boards & tickets","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840553,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/time-tracking/"}

{"id":"docs-getting-started-apps","title":"Mobile and desktop apps","slug":"docs-getting-started-apps","content":"Hypertask on a phone is the web app at [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai), installed on the device. On a computer, use that same site in a browser, or install it from the browser.

## Is there a mobile app?

### Android

The official Android app is a Trusted Web Activity wrapper of [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai). It opens the web app with its own launcher icon, splash screen, and push notifications. The project README says to download the APK from the [Android releases page](https://github.com/hypertask-ai/android/releases).

That releases page is the download location. If no APK is listed there yet, install the web app with Add to Home Screen until a release is published.

### iPhone and other phones

Install the web app with **Add to Home Screen**.

On an iPhone, open [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai) in Safari, tap **Share**, then **Add to Home Screen**. On other phones, use the browser's **Add to Home Screen** or **Install** command.

The site publishes a web app manifest named Hypertask with `display` set to `standalone`, so the home-screen icon opens Hypertask without the browser toolbar. The live manifest is [app.hypertask.ai/manifest.webmanifest](https://app.hypertask.ai/manifest.webmanifest).

## Is there a desktop app for Windows or Mac?

Use the web app in a browser. Chrome and Edge can also install [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai) as an app from the address bar. That installed window is the same web app.

Hypertask does not publish a signed desktop installer for Windows or Mac.

[hypertask-desktop](https://github.com/hypertask-ai/hypertask-desktop) is an early-pilot native client written in Rust with GPUI. It covers Inbox, Board, and Task detail, and you build it from source. The repository has no GitHub release and no signed download.","excerpt":"How to use Hypertask on Android and iPhone, and what to use on Windows and Mac.","category":"Getting Started","created_at":1792962844,"updated_at":1794840557,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/apps/"}

{"id":"docs-getting-started-concepts","title":"Core Concepts","slug":"docs-getting-started-concepts","content":"This page covers every core concept in Hypertask. Use it as a reference when building integrations or configuring your workspace.

## Projects

A project is the top-level container for work. Think of it as a board — a single workspace where your team organizes tasks into sections.

Each project has:

- **Name and description** — What the project is about.
- **Prefix** — A short code (e.g., `HT`, `API`) used to generate ticket numbers like `HT-42`.
- **Unique ID** — A numeric identifier used in the MCP API.
- **Members** — The people (and AI agents) who have access.
- **Sections** — The columns that define your workflow.
- **Views** — Saved filter/sort configurations.
- **Labels** — Custom tags for categorizing tasks.

Projects map 1:1 with boards in the UI. When an MCP tool refers to a `board_id`, it means the project ID.

## Sections

Sections are the columns on a project board. They represent stages in your workflow.

**Default sections** when you create a project:

| Section | Typical use |
|---------|-------------|
| Todo | Work that's defined and ready to start |
| Doing | Actively in progress |
| Done | Completed and verified |

You can add, rename, reorder, or remove sections at any time. Common additions include **Review**, **Build**, **Backlog**, or **Blocked**.

Each section has:

- **Name** — Displayed as the column header.
- **Visibility** — Sections can be hidden without deleting them.
- **Rank** — Controls left-to-right ordering on the board.
- **Section ID** — Used by MCP tools to move tasks between sections.

Use `hypertask_projects` with `action: "manifest"` to find the section ID, then `hypertask_tasks` with `action: "update"` and `input.section_id` to move a task into that section.

## Tasks

Tasks are the core unit of work. Every task belongs to exactly one section within one project.

### Properties

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| **Title** | Short, actionable summary of the work |
| **Description** | Rich HTML content with full context, acceptance criteria, and links |
| **Ticket number** | Auto-generated sequential ID scoped to the project (e.g., `PROJ-123`) |
| **Priority** | `Urgent`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, or `None` |
| **Estimate** | T-shirt sizing: `XS`, `S`, `M`, `L`, `XL`, `XXL`, `XXXL` |
| **Due date** | Optional deadline |
| **Status** | `Normal`, `Archive`, or `Deleted` |
| **Section** | Current column on the board |
| **Assignees** | One or more team members responsible for the work |
| **Followers** | Users who receive notifications (auto-added via @mentions) |
| **Labels** | Custom tags for categorization |
| **Subtasks** | Nested tasks for breaking down work |

### Subtasks

Any task can have subtasks — smaller units of work nested under a parent. Subtasks are full tasks themselves, with their own title, assignee, priority, and status. Use them to break complex work into trackable steps.

### Task relations

Tasks can be linked to each other with typed relationships:

| Relation | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `RelatedTo` | General association between two tasks |
| `BlockedBy` | This task cannot proceed until the linked task is done |
| `BlockedTo` | This task is blocking another task from proceeding |

Relations are bidirectional — creating a `BlockedBy` link on Task A to Task B automatically creates a `BlockedTo` link from Task B to Task A.

## Assignees and followers

### Assignees

A task can have **multiple assignees**. All assignees:

- See the task in their inbox
- Receive notifications when the task is updated or commented on
- Are responsible for completing the work

Use the `hypertask_tasks` (`action: "assign"`) MCP tool to add or remove assignees programmatically.

### Followers

Followers are users who receive notifications about a task without being responsible for it. Users become followers when:

- They are **@mentioned** in a comment or description
- They **manually follow** the task through the UI
- They **create** the task (the creator auto-follows)

## Comments

Comments are threaded discussions attached to a task. They serve as the primary communication channel for async collaboration.

Each comment supports:

- **HTML formatting** — Bold, italic, code blocks, links, lists, and more. All comments use HTML, not Markdown.
- **@mentions** — Reference team members by name. Mentioned users are auto-added as followers and receive inbox notifications.
- **Reactions** — Emoji reactions on any comment for lightweight feedback.
- **Attachments** — Files attached to comments for sharing screenshots, documents, or other artifacts.

When an AI agent completes a task, best practice is to post a comment summarizing what was done, what changed, and any relevant file paths or URLs. This creates an audit trail that teammates can review async.

## Labels

Labels are custom tags you define at the project level. Use them to categorize tasks by type, area, or any dimension that matters to your team.

Examples:

- `bug`, `feature`, `chore`
- `frontend`, `backend`, `infra`
- `quick-win`, `tech-debt`

Tasks can have multiple labels. Labels are filterable in views.

## Views

Views are saved filter and sort configurations for a project. They let you slice the board in different ways without changing the underlying data.

A view can filter by:

- Section
- Assignee
- Priority
- Label
- Due date

And sort by:

- Priority
- Due date
- Created date
- Ticket number

Each project can have multiple saved views. They're useful for creating focused perspectives like "My tasks", "Urgent items", or "Overdue work".

A label filter can also leave tasks out. Open the tags filter, pick your labels, then set the toggle to **Hide tags**. The view drops every task carrying one of those labels and keeps the rest. Saved views remember it, and asking AI Chat for everything except those labels sets it up for you.

## Inbox

The inbox is a unified notification center for each user. It surfaces work that needs your attention.

You receive inbox notifications when:

| Event | Notification |
|-------|-------------|
| **Assigned to a task** | Task appears in your inbox |
| **Comment on your task** | New comment notification |
| **@mentioned in a comment** | Mention notification |
| **Task due date approaching** | Due date reminder |
| **Task overdue** | Overdue warning |

Inbox items can be **archived** once handled. Use `hypertask_inbox` (`action: "list"`) to check notifications and `hypertask_inbox` (`action: "archive"`) to clear them via MCP.

AI agents should check their inbox at the start of each session to pick up newly assigned work. This is the recommended pattern for agent-driven task execution.

## Teams

Teams are organization-level containers that group projects and members under a shared billing account.

Key aspects:

- **Seat-based billing** — Each team member (human or AI agent account) occupies a seat.
- **Member roles** — Control who can create projects, manage billing, or invite new members.
- **Shared projects** — All projects within a team are accessible to team members based on their role.

A user can belong to multiple teams, each with its own projects, billing, and member roster.","excerpt":"Reference for all key concepts in Hypertask.","category":"Getting Started","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840561,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/concepts/"}

{"id":"docs-getting-started-contact-support","title":"Get help","slug":"docs-getting-started-contact-support","content":"Start at the [AI help chat](https://help.hypertask.ai). It answers from these docs, and it can hand the conversation to the team in the same chat when it cannot solve something.

- Ask there first, including when you want to talk to a person.
- You can email [help@hypertask.ai](mailto:help@hypertask.ai). The [contact page](https://hypertask.ai/contact/) uses that address for support, partnership, and press.
- Signed in, open **Settings → Help → Send feedback**. That screen says it goes straight to the team. Mark it Bug, Idea, Question, or Praise.
- Free and BYOK list email support. Pro lists priority support.
- For privacy questions, the [privacy policy](https://hypertask.ai/privacy/) names Hypertask Lab Ltd. and links to the same contact page.","excerpt":"How to contact support. Start with the AI help chat, which can hand off to the team in the same chat.","category":"Getting Started","created_at":1792966925,"updated_at":1794840565,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/contact-support/"}

{"id":"docs-getting-started-introduction","title":"What is Hypertask?","slug":"docs-getting-started-introduction","content":"# What is Hypertask? **AI-native collaboration** Built with agents first. Hypertask comes with an intelligent co-worker that can read your board, create tasks, and respond to comments—all via Chat, CLI, MCP, or REST. **Full control, no lock-in** Use built-in or programmatic auth. The CLI, MCP and REST APIs cover every piece of your workflow, so you own the experience. **Workspace-ready** Multi-tenant workspaces with optional boards per workspace, team invites, role-based permissions, and real-time collaboration for many teams. **Modern UX** Clean Kanban boards, calendar views, a unified Inbox for mentions and updates, and a Theme picker supporting Light, Dark, AMOLED, and custom Paper theme. ## Setup options Whether you prefer a browser UI, the command line, or integrating via code, there's a path that fits your workflow. ### Browser Sign in with email on app.hypertask.ai to start collaborating immediately. Invite your team and start adding tasks, boards, and workflows. ### CLI Manage and create tasks from the terminal with the hypertask CLI. Install via your package manager, login, and start creating. 1. Install the CLI via npm or homebrew. 2. Run hypertask login and follow the on-screen prompts. 3. Use commands like hypertask task create, hypertask task list, and hypertask comment add from your shell. ### MCP Connect Hypertask to your AI agents via the Model Context Protocol. The MCP server exposes tools for tasks, boards, chat, and more. 1. Add the Hypertask MCP endpoint to your LM Studio, Claude Desktop, or another MCP-compatible client. 2. Authenticate with a Bearer token or session cookie. 3. Use hypertask_tasks for task creation and assignment, and hypertask_comments for replies. ### REST API Use our REST API to build integration or mobile apps. Seeds, boards, views, tasks, comments, and more are all reachable via simple HTTP requests. 1. Get an API key from the Settings sidebar in the app. 2. Add Authorization: Bearer <key> headers to your requests. 3. Use endpoints like GET /boards, POST /tasks, POST /messages/chat, and more. ## Core concepts Here's a quick overview of the key concepts you'll use in Hypertask. | Concept | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Workspace** | The top-level container for your organization. Board owners can choose whether a board belongs to one workspace or automatically inherits from the owner. | | **Board** | A flexible surface for organizing work: Kanban columns, tables, lists, or calendars. Boards contain sections, views, and tasks. | | **Section** | A column on a Kanban board with tasks that share a common state or trigger. Sections support drag-to-reorder. | | **View** | A custom perspective on a board—filtering, sorting, grouping, or hiding tasks. Views can be pinned, hidden, or deleted as needed. | | **Task** | A unit of work with a title, description, assignee, tags, subtasks, and relations with other tasks and issues. | | **Chat** | An in-app AI assistant that understands your context—tasks, boards, messages, and more. You can create and edit saved GPTs, speed up writing, and control agents and time tracking. | | **Inbox** | A unified feed of mentions, important items, reactions, and updates across your boards. Unread items are highlighted and accessible via keyboard navigation. | | **Agents** | Autonomous AI agents that can pull context from your board, create and update tasks, respond to comments, run schedules, and interact with your workspace via tools. | It's Email-native, but not Firebase-dependent. Hypertask uses Better Auth and your own SMTP for signing in, with Firebase kept exclusively for push notifications. You can also integrate via CLI, MCP, or REST without going through the app UI at all. ## Getting started 1. Create an account or sign in with email/app password at app.hypertask.ai. 2. Request a new sign-in link if your browser session expires or is shared; links are single-use, so each click gives you a fresh sign-in. 3. Request a new verification link when creating a new account; never reuse old verification emails. 4. Set your preferred theme using the Ctrl+K command palette or the Theme picker in Settings (Light, Dark, System, AMOLED, Paper). 5. For email signups: You land directly on a board and receive a welcome email containing install steps for Claude Code / Cursor MCP along with a link to your board. 6. Invite teammates to your workspace and create your first board (Kanban, Table, List, or Calendar). 7. Start adding tasks, tagging them for organization, and assigning them. 8. Use Ctrl+K to access the command palette for quick navigation and actions. 9. Chat with the AI assistant to create tasks, summarize boards, or brainstorm without leaving the page. 10. Optional: install the CLI or set up an MCP agent for programmatic control over your tasks. ## Keyboard shortcuts Hypertask has a rich set of keyboard shortcuts across surfaces. Press Ctrl+K to open the command palette and search for shortcuts by name. Depending on your OS, Ctrl is Control on Windows/Linux and ⌘ on macOS. Ctrl+K — Open command palette for shortcuts and actions. Ctrl+G — Navigate surfaces (Inbox → Boards → My Tasks → Chat), as needed. ### Live shortcuts The command palette shows all shortcuts relevant to your current context, such as boards, tasks, inbox, and chat. Hover over a shortcut to see its location (modal, board surface, or button). ### Keyboard hints in the UI The header's **Login** button shows a "Press L to log in" tooltip when you hover over it or focus it with the keyboard. This hint highlights the visual keycap style for improved discoverability and accessibility. ## Onboarding First-time users see an Onboarding Tour when they sign in. You can replay it at any time by pressing Ctrl+K, searching for "Onboarding tour", and selecting the replay option. The tour walks you through connecting AI, creating your first board, and using key features. Invited teammates see a trimmed version that skips heavy setup but still introduces essential workflows. ## Security, auth, and permissions Hypertask uses server-side authentication and ensures that other users' data never leaks into your boards or views. Here are some key principles: - Email sign-in & Better Auth: Sign in is handled server-side. Email login takes you directly to your board; magic-links and sign-out remain functional. - Firebase for push only: Firebase Auth is not used for login or signup. Firebase is strictly for FCM push notifications. - Route cleanup: Dead authentication routes that no longer exist (e.g. old signup or password reset paths) return 404, and CORS carve-outs are removed for production security. - Session integrity via signed ht_session cookies: API routes validate signed ht_session cookies alongside nookies_user, ensuring that forging cookies cannot be used for cookie spoofing. - PostHog cross-domain visitor identity: Signin and load attribution between hypertask.ai and app.hypertask.ai use signed ht_session cookies, avoiding client-side cookie dependency. - Strict account linking: Linking a Google login to an unverified local account is blocked, ensuring verified local accounts are not orphaned. - Multi-tenant isolation: By design, boards, views, and tasks belong to the user. Archive and other features show only your data unless explicitly shared. - Single-use login and verification links: When you request a new sign-in link or account verification email, the link is valid for one use only. Attempting to reuse a link shows an "invalid or expired" message and does not grant a session. - Board-level access for files: Only people who can see a ticket can download its attachments. Access is scoped to the task: observers outside the ticket cannot reach files and previews, even if they can view the board. For finer-grained security, you can use the REST API to enforce claims, tokens, and additional checks for your integrations. ## Frequently asked questions
Is Hypertask free? The Free plan includes unlimited members and unlimited open tickets. You can own up to 3 boards. Archived boards are not counted. A paid or comped plan has no board limit. See [Billing & Seat Management](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/billing/) for details.
Can I export my tasks? Yes. Export options include CSV, JSON, and integrations with IDEs, build tools, and CI/CD pipelines using the CLI and REST API.
Is there a mobile app? Yes. Android has an official app, and iPhone and other phones install the web app with Add to Home Screen. See [Mobile and desktop apps](https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/apps/).
Is there a desktop app for Windows or Mac? Use the web app in a browser, or install it as an app. There is no signed desktop download. See [Mobile and desktop apps](https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/apps/).

{"id":"docs-getting-started-quickstart","title":"Quick Start","slug":"docs-getting-started-quickstart","content":"## For humans 1. **Sign up** at [hypertask.ai](https://hypertask.ai) using email or Google. 2. **Get onboarded.** Visitors landing at [hypertask.ai/demo](https://hypertask.ai/demo) immediately see a guest board seeded with sample content and a setup wizard. On desktop, the AI Task Writer opens by default; press Ctrl + K and select "Create board" to open the Board creation assistant, which walks you through naming, adding columns, and inviting people. 3. **Create a project** from the dashboard. Give it a name and a short prefix (e.g. `HT` for "Hypertask") - this prefix is used for ticket numbers like `HT-1`, `HT-2`. 4. **Set up sections.** Every new project starts with default sections. A typical workflow uses: | Section | Purpose | |---------|---------| | Todo | Work that's ready to be picked up | | Doing | Actively in progress | | Review | Completed, awaiting review | | Done | Shipped and verified | You can rename, reorder, add, or remove sections at any time from the project settings. 5. **Create your first task.** Click the "+" button in any section, or use the AI Task Writer to generate a task from a natural language description. Fill in: - **Title** - Keep it short and actionable (e.g. "Add password reset flow") - **Description** - Rich HTML content with context, acceptance criteria, links - **Priority** - Urgent, High, Medium, Low, or None - **Estimate** - XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL, XXXL Email sign-in links are single-use. Once you click a sign-in or verification link in your email, the link expires and can't be clicked again. If you miss it or accidentally open it in a browser, requesting a fresh link sends you another valid, single-use link. ## For AI agents (MCP) Hypertask exposes an MCP server over Streamable HTTP. Connect any MCP-compatible client to let your AI agent manage tasks programmatically. ### Get your API key 1. Open [app.hypertask.ai](https://hypertask.ai) and go to **Settings**. 2. Navigate to the **API Keys** section. 3. Click **Generate API Key** and copy the token. Treat your API key like a password. It grants full access to your projects and tasks. Never commit it to version control. ### Connect your client Add the Hypertask MCP server to your client's configuration: ### Claude Code Add to your Claude Code MCP settings (`.claude/settings.json` or project-level `.mcp.json`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "hypertasks": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" } } } } ``` ### Claude Desktop Open **Settings > Developer > Edit Config** and add to `claude_desktop_config.json`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "hypertasks": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" } } } } ``` Restart Claude Desktop after saving. ### Cursor Open **Settings > MCP Servers > Add Server** and configure: ```json { "mcpServers": { "hypertasks": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" } } } } ``` Replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with the token from the previous step. ### Verify the connection Ask your client to call `hypertask_user_context` with the `hello` action: ```json { "action": "hello", "input": {} } ``` This returns your user details and accessible boards. Authentication comes from the bearer token in your client configuration, not from a connection tool. Next, ask: ```text List all my Hypertask projects. ``` The agent calls `hypertask_projects` with `action: "list"`. If you see your boards, the connection is working. Use the current resource tools and pass action-specific fields in `input`. ## Your first task workflow Here's a typical task lifecycle - whether you're working through the UI or via an AI agent: 1. **Create a task** in the Todo section. Give it a clear title and description. 2. **Assign it** to a team member or AI agent. The assignee receives an inbox notification. 3. **Move to Doing** when work begins. This signals to the team that someone is actively working on it. 4. **Post comments** as work progresses. Use HTML formatting for code snippets, links, or structured updates. 5. **Move to Review** when the work is complete. Add a comment summarizing what was done. 6. **Move to Done** after review passes. The task is archived and the ticket number remains for reference. AI agents follow this same workflow. A well-configured agent will check its inbox, pick up assigned tasks, move them to Doing, do the work, post a summary comment, and move the task to Review - all without human intervention. ## Next steps [Core Concepts](https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/concepts/) Understand projects, sections, tasks, and the full data model. [MCP Integration](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/overview/) Learn how MCP tools let agents work with Hypertask. [MCP Tools Reference](https://docs.hypertask.ai/api/tools-reference/) Complete API reference for every MCP tool with parameters and examples.","excerpt":"Get up and running with Hypertask in under 5 minutes.","category":"Getting Started","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840574,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/quickstart/"}

{"id":"docs-getting-started-security-and-privacy","title":"Security and privacy","slug":"docs-getting-started-security-and-privacy","content":"## Do you support SSO or SAML login?

No. Hypertask does not offer SSO, SAML, or SCIM.

You can sign in with Google, with email, or with a passkey. Email sign-in sends a temporary login link and a verification code. The login page shows **Sign in with a passkey** when the browser supports passkeys. Add or remove a passkey in **Settings → Profile → Accounts**.

A signed-in session lasts 30 days. Using Hypertask refreshes that session about once a day, which starts the 30 days again.

## Is Hypertask GDPR compliant, and where is my data stored?

The [privacy policy](https://hypertask.ai/privacy) is from Hypertask Lab Ltd. in London. It describes your right to request access to the personal information Hypertask holds, and to ask for a correction when that information is inaccurate, incomplete, or out of date. Third parties named in the policy include Google Analytics, Gmail, and Stripe. Google Calendar is included only if you connect it.

These docs do not state a data hosting region, and they do not include a data processing agreement. For data-processing questions, [contact support](https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/contact-support/).

## Can I delete my account?

Yes. Open **Settings → Profile → General**. Under **Danger zone**, choose **Delete account**.

The screen says this wipes your boards and data, and that your email can sign up again from scratch. Confirming shows that this cannot be undone and that everything you own is wiped. Hypertask then signs you out.

Cancel your subscription before you delete the account. If a subscription is still active, deletion is refused, and the screen says it could not delete your account.

## Can I export my data?

There is no data export in the app. You can read tasks with the [REST API](https://docs.hypertask.ai/api/rest-api/) and the [CLI](https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/reference/) (`hypertask task list`).","excerpt":"Sign-in methods, session length, account deletion, and where to read the privacy policy.","category":"Getting Started","created_at":1794036459,"updated_at":1794840578,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/security-and-privacy/"}

{"id":"docs-getting-started-settings-profile","title":"Profile & Settings","slug":"docs-getting-started-settings-profile","content":"Your Profile page in Hypertask is split into three dedicated sections: **General**, **Appearance**, and **Task page**. Each has its own navigation point and can be accessed directly from anywhere in the app via `Ctrl+K`.

---

## General

The **General** tab contains your identity settings:

- **Avatar** — Upload or change your profile picture.
- **Display name** — The name shown to others in tasks, comments, and activity feeds.
- **Email** — Your primary email address; used for notifications and logins.
- **Bio** (optional) — A short description shown in your profile card.

Use these fields to manage how you appear across the platform.

## Session settings

Hypertask uses Better Auth server-side authentication with configurable login session duration:

- **Session length** — Choose between 7 days and 30 days when signing in. This controls how long your session stays active before requiring re-authentication.
- **Persistent sign-in links** — Access a persistent sign-in link that doesn't expire until used.
- **Clean sign-out** — All flows support immediate session invalidation and cookie clearing.

## Privacy & cookies

Hypertask respects your right to control how your data is collected. By default, tracking is disabled until you make an explicit choice:

- **No tracking until consent** — Tracking cookies and IP lookups are not stored or performed until you select an option.
- **Consent banner** — Every visitor sees a cookie banner on login, signup, and when you open a signed-in board.
- **Shared consent choice** — Your tracking preferences on hypertask.ai are shared across all Hypertask products and tracked behavior follows your choice.

This ensures your data is not collected without your knowledge or agreement.

---

## Appearance

The **Appearance** tab controls the visual look of your interface:

- **Theme** — Choose between Light, Dark, or System theme (automatically follows your OS preference).
- **Font size** — Adjust text size across the app for better readability.
- **Reduced motion** — Reduce animations for a calmer environment.

## Task page

The **Task page** tab configures behavior specific to how tasks display:

- **Show task scroll** (on/off) — When enabled, Hypertask automatically scrolls to the full task description and details when opening a task.
- **Subtask depth** — Control how many levels of subtasks are visible by default.
- **Expand inline details** — Show fields like due date, assignee, and labels inline on the task card.

These settings apply to the task detail view and the task editor across all boards.

## AI settings

The **AI Settings** tab in the Task page section allows you to configure how the AI assistant behaves across your tasks and comments:

- **Custom instructions** — Provide board-level instructions that the AI follows when helping with tasks on that board. Enter your instructions directly into the text box, which fills the page to give you maximum writing space and easy visibility of full context.

These instructions are applied automatically when the AI drafts responses, edits descriptions, or proposes next steps in chat or comments.

## Ask the AI to change a setting

On any Settings page you can ask the AI chat, in plain words, for a change on that page:

- Say what you want: "switch me to the dark theme", "turn off email notifications for comments", or "make Anna an admin on this board".
- The reply carries one **Setting change** card showing the setting, its current value and the new value. Nothing changes until you press **Apply**; press **Cancel** and nothing happens.
- Once a change lands, the card offers **Undo**, which puts the previous value back.
- The card also shows **Open setting**, so you can go to the control yourself.

The AI uses your own rights, exactly as if you clicked. A board member cannot change what only the board owner may change, and access and people changes always go through the same card. If a change is not something it can make, it tells you where the setting lives and opens that page.

## User profile caching

On authenticated startup, Hypertask reuses a fresh account-scoped user profile cached at the app shell layer. The cached profile remains valid for about 5 minutes, reducing repeated `/api/users/getById` refetches and improving cold start performance. The cache is automatically invalidated and refreshed as needed.

## Preferences via signed login

Preferences now load and save correctly with a signed login alone, without requiring the older profile cookie. As long as your session is signed in, the Preferences page can read and write settings such as Play GIFs, text size, and theme, and changes persist across reloads.

```bash
# Signed in with your session only
# Navigate to Settings → Task page
# Toggle Play GIFs or adjust a setting
# The change is saved immediately and survives navigation
```

This simplifies session handling so a single authentication flow serves all content and settings across the app.

## Management keys

Management keys let API, CLI, MCP, and AI chat clients manage agents and credentials. Create them under **Settings → Connect → Management keys**, next to MCP, CLI, and REST API.

1. Open [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai) and sign in.
2. Open **Settings**, then **Connect**, then **Management keys**.
3. Enter a name, choose a scope, and choose an expiry.
4. Choose **Create key**. Copy the key immediately. It is shown once.

**Scope** is **Management**, **Usage**, or **Full access**. Full access stays on the whole account. Usage reads team AI usage and spend. Management manages agents and keys.

**Expiry** is **Never**, **30 days**, **90 days**, or **365 days**. A new management key starts on **Never**. The list shows **Expires** and a date, or **Never**.

When team-scoped keys are available, Management and Usage can be limited to one team. Full access cannot. A team key stops working if you lose access to that team.

REST API keys are on the same **Connect** screen, under **Developer access**. They use the same four expiry choices, and a new REST API key starts on **90 days**.

If a client is refused after a key's date, see [MCP troubleshooting](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/troubleshooting/).

## Common Actions

### Change your avatar or name

1. Open your Profile page in the app.
2. Switch to the **General** tab.
3. Upload a new image or edit your name under the Avatar or Display name fields.
4. Click **Save** to apply changes.

See [Keyboard Shortcuts](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/keyboard-shortcuts/) for cmd-k access to Profile and General.

## Keyboard Shortcuts

For quick navigation within Profile:

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| `Ctrl+K` then type "Profile" | Open the full Profile page |
| `Ctrl+K` then type "General" | Jump to General tab |
| `Ctrl+K` then type "Appearance" | Jump to Appearance tab |
| `Ctrl+K` then type "Task" | Jump to Task page tab |

### Related Topics

[Keyboard Shortcuts](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/keyboard-shortcuts/)

Complete list of keyboard shortcuts for navigation and actions across Hypertask.","excerpt":"Manage your identity, appearance, and preferences in Hypertask.","category":"Getting Started","created_at":1785877232,"updated_at":1794840582,"url":"https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/settings-profile/"}

{"id":"docs-getting-started-switching","title":"Switching from Trello, Jira, or Asana","slug":"docs-getting-started-switching","content":"Switching from Trello, Jira, or Asana usually starts with two questions: whether existing tasks can move over, and how Hypertask differs from Linear or Jira.

## Importing tasks

Hypertask has no task import. There is no one-click import from Trello, Jira, Asana, or Linear. The import routes in the product import [AI skills](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/skills/), not tasks.

Export a CSV from the old tool. Connect an agent over [MCP](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/overview/) or the [CLI](https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/reference/), and ask it to create the tasks from that file.

- CLI: [`hypertask task create`](https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/commands/#hypertask-task-create) creates one task. It needs a project id and a title.
- MCP: [`hypertask_tasks`](https://docs.hypertask.ai/api/tools-reference/#hypertask_tasks) with action `create` creates one task the same way.

[Agent workflows](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/workflows/) describe how an agent lists board work and creates tasks.

## How Hypertask differs
