{"id":"10895347","title":"How to Create a Kanban Board in Hypertask","slug":"how-to-create-a-kanban-board-in-hypertasks","content":"

Steps to Create a Kanban Board

  1. Open the Hypertask Command Center (HTC)

    • Press Ctrl + K (Windows) or Cmd + K (Mac) to open the HTC

  2. Create a New Board

    • Type \"create board\" in the HTC

    • Select the \"Create new board\" option

  3. Name Your Board

    • Enter a name for your new board

    • Press Enter to confirm

  4. Set Up Columns

    • Your new board will have default columns (e.g., To Do, In Progress, Done)

    • To add a new column:

      1. Open the HTC (Ctrl + K / Cmd + K)

      2. Type \"Add column\" or search for \"column\"

      3. Enter the column name

      4. The new column will be added to the end of your board

    • To manage columns (rename, delete, or reorder), see our article on \"Managing Columns in Hypertask\"

  5. Add Tasks

    • Press C to add a new task at the top of a column

    • Press Shift + C to add a task at the bottom of a column

  6. Customize Your Board

    • Use Shift + S to sort tasks

    • Press Shift + F to access filtering options

Keyboard Shortcuts for Board Management

  • Ctrl + B: Switch between boards

  • Alt + 1-9: Quickly switch to favorited boards

Tips for Effective Board Creation

  • Keep your board focused on a specific project or workflow

  • Use clear, descriptive names for your columns

  • Start with essential columns and add more as needed

Remember, you can always access the full list of keyboard shortcuts by pressing ? while on your board.

","excerpt":"Creating a new Kanban board in Hypertask is quick and easy. Follow these simple steps to set up your board and start managing your tasks efficiently.","category":"cat-12128993","created_at":1767701666,"updated_at":1792969767,"url":null}

{"id":"10895348","title":"How to Create Tasks in Hypertask","slug":"how-to-create-tasks-in-hypertasks","content":"

Keyboard Shortcuts for Quick Task Creation

  1. Add a Task to the Top of a Column

    • Navigate to the desired column

    • Press C to create a new task at the top

  2. Add a Task to the Bottom of a Column

    • Navigate to the desired column

    • Press Shift + C to create a new task at the bottom

Mouse-Based Task Creation

  1. Using the Column Header

    • Click the plus sign (+) at the top of any column

    • This opens the task creation dialog

  2. Using the Column Footer

    • Hover your mouse below the last task in a column

    • Click the plus sign (+) that appears

Detailed Task Creation Using the Hypertask Command Center (HTC)

  1. Open the HTC by pressing Ctrl + K (Windows) or Cmd + K (Mac)

  2. Type \"Create ticket\" and select the option

  3. Choose the board where you want to create the task

  4. Enter the ticket title

  5. The task detail page will open, where you can fill in additional information:

    • Description

    • Assignee

    • Due date

    • Priority

    • Size

    • Tags

Editing Tasks

To edit an existing task:

  1. Select the task

  2. Press Enter or double-click to open the task details

  3. Make your changes

  4. Press Ctrl + Enter (Windows) or Cmd + Enter (Mac) to save

Task Management Shortcuts

  • A: Assign a task to a team member

  • P: Set task priority

  • S: Set task size

  • T: Add tags to a task

  • Shift + D: Set due date

Best Practices for Task Creation

  • Keep task titles clear and concise

  • Use the description field for additional details

  • Assign tasks to specific team members when possible

  • Set realistic due dates and priorities

Remember, you can always access the full list of keyboard shortcuts by pressing ? while on your board.

{"id":"10895754","title":"How to Edit Comments in Hypertask","slug":"how-to-edit-comments-in-hypertasks","content":"

Editing Comments with Keyboard Shortcuts

  1. On any task detail page navigate to the comment you want to edit using Tab and Shift + Tab keys. You can also use the ↑ and ↓ cursor keys.

  2. Press Ctrl + Enter (Windows) or Cmd + Enter (Mac) to activate editing mode.

  3. Make your changes to the comment text.

  4. Press Enter to save your changes.

  5. To cancel editing without saving, press Esc.

Editing Comments with Mouse

  1. Hover over the comment you want to edit.

  2. Click the pencil icon (✏️) that appears on the right side of the comment.

  3. The comment will enter edit mode.

  4. Make your changes to the comment text.

  5. Press Enter to save your changes.

  6. To cancel editing without saving, press Esc.

Additional Tips

  • You can @mention team members in your comments to notify them.

  • If you want to quote an existing comment in a new comment, simply press Enter when the comment is selected.

  • Remember, you can always access the full list of keyboard shortcuts by pressing ? while on your board or task detail page.

{"id":"10895747","title":"How to Filter Tasks in Hypertask: Mastering Shift+F","slug":"how-to-filter-tasks-in-hypertasks-mastering-shiftf","content":"

With a simple Shift+F shortcut, you can access a wide range of filtering options. This guide will walk you through the available filters and how to use them efficiently.

Accessing Filters

To access the filter options in Hypertask:

  1. Use the keyboard shortcut: Press Shift + F

  2. Or click the filter icon in the header of your Hypertask interface

Both methods open the Hypertask Command Center (HTC) view of the filter options.

Available Filter Categories

Hypertask provides a range of filters to help you focus on specific aspects of your tasks:

Communication Filters

  • Has unread notifications: Shows tasks with unread updates or comments

  • Present in inbox: Displays tasks currently in your Hypertask inbox

Personal Task Management

  • Tasks assigned to me: Lists tasks assigned to you

  • Priority: Filter tasks by their priority level

  • Task Size: Sort tasks based on their estimated size or complexity

Team Collaboration

  • Assignees: Filter tasks by specific team members

  • Tags: Organize and filter tasks using custom tags

Time Management

  • Due date: Filter tasks by their due date or date range

  • Date updated at: Find recently modified tasks

  • Date created at: Identify new tasks or review older ones

Additional Options

  • Match ANY filters: Shows tasks that meet at least one of your selected criteria

Using Filters

  1. Open the filter options using Shift + F or the filter icon

  2. In the HTC, select the filter categories you want to apply

  3. For each category, choose the specific criteria

  4. Hypertask will update your view to show tasks matching your filters

Tips for Effective Filtering

  • Combine multiple filters for more specific task views

  • Use \"Match ANY filters\" for broader results

  • Regularly clear filters to return to your full task view

  • Experiment with different combinations to find what works best for your workflow

Keyboard Navigation

  • Use arrow keys to navigate through filter options

  • Press Enter to select/deselect a filter option

  • Press Esc to close the filter options without applying changes

By mastering the Shift+F shortcut and these filtering options, you can streamline your task management process, improve project visibility, and enhance team communication within Hypertask.

","excerpt":"Hypertask offers a powerful filtering system to help you manage your tasks more effectively.","category":"cat-12130036","created_at":1767701666,"updated_at":1792969761,"url":null}

{"id":"10895786","title":"How to Reach Inbox Zero with Hypertask","slug":"how-to-reach-inbox-zero-with-hypertasks","content":"

Mastering Inbox Zero with Hypertask: A Keyboard-Driven Approach

Inbox Zero is a productivity method aimed at keeping your inbox empty, or almost empty, at all times. Here's how to achieve this using Hypertask, with a focus on leveraging keyboard shortcuts for maximum efficiency.

Understanding Hypertask Inbox

Hypertask provides a powerful inbox integrated with its Kanban boards. This inbox is your central hub for all project-related communications and tasks. The key to mastering Hypertask and achieving Inbox Zero lies in leveraging keyboard shortcuts for maximum efficiency.

Essential Keyboard Shortcuts

  • G then I: Quickly jump to your inbox from anywhere in Hypertask

  • J and K: Navigate up and down through items

  • ENTER: Open a task

  • E: Archive an item

  • H: Set a reminder for a task

  • CTRL/CMD + K: Open the Hypertask Command Center (HTC)

  • Tab: Cycle through auto-splits

  • CTRL+M: Add a comment to a task

  • A: Assign a task to someone

  • I: View AI-generated summaries

  • /: Access AI writing assistance menu

Mastering Keyboard Shortcuts

  1. Start by memorizing the most frequently used shortcuts (G then I, J, K, ENTER, E, H).

  2. Practice using these shortcuts regularly to build muscle memory.

  3. Gradually incorporate more advanced shortcuts into your workflow.

  4. Remember, speed comes with practice. The more you use shortcuts, the faster you'll become at managing your inbox.

Steps to Achieve Inbox Zero

1. Quick Access

Always use G then I to jump to your inbox, no matter where you are in Hypertask.

2. Set Processing Times

  • Dedicate specific times during your day to process your inbox.

  • Aim for at least twice daily: morning and afternoon.

3. Use Auto-Splits

  • Leverage the auto-split feature to categorize incoming items by project or board.

  • Access different splits using the Tab key.

4. Efficient Processing

  • Navigate items with J and K.

  • Open an item using ENTER.

  • Decide immediately: act, delegate, defer, or archive.

  • Use CTRL+M to add a comment.

  • Use @ to mention other people or tasks in your comment.

  • Use A to assign it to someone else.

  • Use E to archive completed or irrelevant items.

  • Use H to set reminders for tasks you'll address later.

5. Utilize AI Features

  • Use AI-generated summaries (shortcut I) to quickly understand the content of messages.

  • Access AI writing assistance through the forward slash (/) menu for faster responses.

6. Task Management

  • Don't use your inbox as a to-do list.

  • Prioritize and categorize tasks within their current board.

7. Regular Review

  • At the end of each day, aim to process your inbox to zero.

  • Review your 'reminder' items periodically to ensure nothing is overlooked.

Tips for Maintaining Inbox Zero

  • Process in batches: Handle similar items together for efficiency. Auto-splits help tremendously with that.

  • Be decisive: Avoid leaving items in your inbox "just in case". You can always defer with H.

  • Use the Hypertask Command Center (HTC) (CTRL/CMD + K) for quick actions.

  • Customize your workflow: Adjust these steps to fit your specific needs and work style.

  • Keep practicing shortcuts: The more you use them, the faster and more efficient you'll become at managing your inbox.

Remember, the goal is to keep your inbox at or near zero consistently. This practice helps maintain focus, reduce stress, and improve overall productivity in your project management. By mastering keyboard shortcuts, especially the quick navigation to your inbox (G then I), you'll be able to process your tasks and communications more efficiently than ever before.

","excerpt":"Reach Inbox Zero in Hypertask with keyboard shortcuts: jump to your inbox with G then I, move with J and K, and clear items fast.","category":"cat-12130247","created_at":1767701666,"updated_at":1792969759,"url":null}

{"id":"10895350","title":"How to Receive Notifications from Hypertask","slug":"how-to-receive-notifications-from-hypertasks","content":"

Accessing Notification Settings

  1. Open the Settings sidebar:

    • Keyboard: Press \\ (backslash)

    • Mouse: Click the gear icon in the bottom right corner

  2. Navigate to the \"Notifications\" section

For more on using keyboard shortcuts, see our Hypertask Keyboard Shortcuts guide.

Email Notifications

To toggle email notifications:

  1. Find the \"Email Notifications\" option in the Notifications section

  2. Click the toggle switch to turn email notifications on or off

Browser-Based Push Notifications

To enable push notifications on your current device:

  1. Locate the \"Push Notifications on this device\" option

  2. Click the toggle switch to turn push notifications on or off

Note: When enabling push notifications for the first time, your browser will prompt you to allow notifications from Hypertask. You must select \"Allow\" to receive push notifications.

​

How to allow Push Notifications in your Browser

If you see a message saying \"Allow push notifications from browser settings\", you need to allow push notifications in your browser for Hypertask first. Follow the browser-specific instructions in the next section to enable notifications.

If you've previously blocked notifications from Hypertask or need to enable them, you'll need to update your browser settings:

  • Chrome: Click the lock icon in the address bar > Site Settings > Notifications > Allow

  • Firefox: Click the lock icon in the address bar > Clear the \"Block\" setting for Notifications

  • Safari: Preferences > Websites > Notifications > Find Hypertask and select \"Allow\"

  • Edge: Click the lock icon in the address bar > Permissions > Notifications > Allow

Remember, you can always adjust these settings later through the Hypertask sidebar or your browser preferences.

{"id":"10895744","title":"How to Sort Tasks in Hypertask: Using Shift+S","slug":"how-to-sort-tasks-in-hypertasks-using-shifts","content":"

Accessing Sort Options

There are two ways to access the sort options in Hypertask:

  1. Keyboard Shortcut: Press Shift + S

  2. Sort Icon: Click the sort icon located in the header of your Hypertask interface

\n

Both methods will open the Hypertask Command Center (HTC) with the sort options.
​

Available Sorting Options

Hypertask offers the following sorting options:

  1. Manual: Allows you to manually arrange tasks by dragging and dropping

  2. Priority: Sorts tasks based on their assigned priority level

  3. Due Date: Organizes tasks according to their deadlines

  4. Size: Arranges tasks based on their size/complexity estimation

  5. Creation Date: Orders tasks by when they were created

How to Sort Your Tasks

  1. Open your desired board in Hypertask

  2. Press Shift + S or click the sort icon in the header

  3. The HTC will open, displaying the sort options

  4. Use the arrow keys or mouse to select your preferred sorting method

  5. Press Enter or click to confirm your selection

  6. Your board will automatically update to reflect the chosen sorting option

Understanding the Sorting Options

Manual Sorting

  • Gives you full control over task order

  • Ideal for custom workflows or specific project needs

  • Tasks can be rearranged by dragging and dropping

Priority Sorting

  • Automatically organizes tasks based on their assigned priority

  • Helps focus on high-importance tasks first

  • Useful for quickly identifying critical items

Due Date Sorting

  • Orders tasks by their deadline dates

  • Perfect for deadline-driven projects

  • Helps ensure time-sensitive tasks are visible

Size Sorting

  • Arranges tasks based on their estimated size or complexity

  • Useful for planning work capacity

  • Helps in sprint planning and effort estimation

Creation Date Sorting

  • Orders tasks based on when they were created

  • Helpful for chronological review

  • Can identify older tasks that might need attention

Sorting Direction

The Hypertask sorting feature defaults to descending order (highest priority first, earliest due dates first, etc.). You can see the current direction indicator next to the \"Descending\" label.

\n

Tips for Effective Sorting

  • Use priority sorting when you need to focus on urgent or important tasks

  • Switch to due date sorting for deadline-driven projects

  • Use size sorting during sprint planning or resource allocation

  • Try creation date sorting to identify tasks that have been in the backlog for too long

  • Combine sorting with filters (Shift + F) for more precise task management

Keyboard Navigation in HTC

  • Use arrow keys to navigate between sorting options

  • Press Enter to select a sorting option

  • Press Esc to close the HTC without applying changes

By mastering the Shift+S shortcut and understanding these expanded sorting options in the Hypertask Command Center, you can quickly reorganize your tasks, streamline your workflow, and boost productivity within Hypertask.

","excerpt":"This guide will walk you through the process of sorting your tasks in Hypertask using the Shift+S shortcut to access the Hypertask Command Center (HTC).","category":"cat-12130036","created_at":1767701666,"updated_at":1792969762,"url":null}

{"id":"10895737","title":"Navigation and Editing Mode in Hypertask Task Detail Page","slug":"navigation-and-editing-mode-in-hypertasks-task-detail-page","content":"

Navigation Mode

Navigation mode allows you to move around the task detail page, perform quick actions without changing the content, and navigate between tasks.

Entering Navigation Mode

  • When you first open a task, you're in navigation mode by default.

  • If you're in editing mode, press Esc to return to navigation mode.

Key Features of Navigation Mode

  • Use arrow keys to navigate between different sections of the task.

  • Press Enter to activate editing mode for the selected field.

  • Use shortcuts to perform quick actions:

    • A: Assign the task

    • P: Set priority

    • S: Set task size

    • T: Add tags

    • Shift + D: Set due date

    • Ctrl + E (Windows) or Cmd + E (Mac): Archive the task

  • Navigate between tasks:

    • J: Move to the next task

    • K: Move to the previous task

    Note: If you opened the task from the inbox, this will navigate through inbox tasks. If you opened it from a Kanban column, it will navigate through tasks in that column.

Editing Mode

Editing mode allows you to modify the content of the task and access advanced formatting options.

Entering Editing Mode

  • Select a field in navigation mode and press Enter.

  • Double-click on any editable field.

Key Features of Editing Mode

  • Type or modify the content in the selected field.

  • Use Tab to move to the next field.

  • Use Shift + Tab to move to the previous field.

  • Press Ctrl + Enter (Windows) or Cmd + Enter (Mac) to save changes and return to navigation mode.

  • Press Esc to cancel changes and return to navigation mode.

  • Access the forward slash menu for text formatting options by typing /.

  • Use Tiptap shortcuts for quick formatting (see below).

  • All other keyboard shortcuts are deactivated to allow for uninterrupted typing.

Text Formatting with Tiptap Shortcuts

Hypertask uses Tiptap for rich text editing. Here's a comprehensive list of keyboard shortcuts available in editing mode:

Essentials

  • Copy: Control + C (Windows/Linux), Cmd + C (macOS)

  • Cut: Control + X (Windows/Linux), Cmd + X (macOS)

  • Paste: Control + V (Windows/Linux), Cmd + V (macOS)

  • Paste without formatting: Control + Shift + V (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Shift + V (macOS)

  • Undo: Control + Z (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Z (macOS)

  • Redo: Control + Shift + Z (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Shift + Z (macOS)

  • Add a line break: Shift + Enter / Control + Enter (Windows/Linux), Shift + Enter / Cmd + Enter (macOS)

Text Formatting

  • Bold: Control + B (Windows/Linux), Cmd + B (macOS)

  • Italicize: Control + I (Windows/Linux), Cmd + I (macOS)

  • Underline: Control + U (Windows/Linux), Cmd + U (macOS)

  • Strikethrough: Control + Shift + S (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Shift + S (macOS)

  • Highlight: Control + Shift + H (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Shift + H (macOS)

  • Code: Control + E (Windows/Linux), Cmd + E (macOS)

Paragraph Formatting

  • Apply normal text style: Control + Alt + 0 (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Alt + 0 (macOS)

  • Apply heading style 1: Control + Alt + 1 (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Alt + 1 (macOS)

  • Apply heading style 2: Control + Alt + 2 (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Alt + 2 (macOS)

  • Apply heading style 3: Control + Alt + 3 (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Alt + 3 (macOS)

  • Apply heading style 4: Control + Alt + 4 (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Alt + 4 (macOS)

  • Apply heading style 5: Control + Alt + 5 (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Alt + 5 (macOS)

  • Apply heading style 6: Control + Alt + 6 (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Alt + 6 (macOS)

  • Ordered list: Control + Shift + 7 (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Shift + 7 (macOS)

  • Bullet list: Control + Shift + 8 (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Shift + 8 (macOS)

  • Task list: Control + Shift + 9 (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Shift + 9 (macOS)

  • Blockquote: Control + Shift + B (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Shift + B (macOS)

  • Left align: Control + Shift + L (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Shift + L (macOS)

  • Center align: Control + Shift + E (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Shift + E (macOS)

  • Right align: Control + Shift + R (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Shift + R (macOS)

  • Justify: Control + Shift + J (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Shift + J (macOS)

  • Code block: Control + Alt + C (Windows/Linux), Cmd + Alt + C (macOS)

  • Subscript: Control + , (Windows/Linux), Cmd + , (macOS)

  • Superscript: Control + . (Windows/Linux), Cmd + . (macOS)

Text Selection

  • Select all: Control + A (Windows/Linux), Cmd + A (macOS)

  • Extend selection one character to left: Shift + ←

  • Extend selection one character to right: Shift + →

  • Extend selection one line up: Shift + ↑

  • Extend selection one line down: Shift + ↓

Remember, these shortcuts are active only in editing mode. In navigation mode, different shortcuts apply for task management and navigation.

Switching Between Modes

  • To switch from navigation mode to editing mode: Press Enter on the selected field.

  • To switch from editing mode to navigation mode:

    • Press Ctrl + Enter (Windows) or Cmd + Enter (Mac) to save changes.

    • Press Esc to cancel changes.

Best Practices

  1. Use navigation mode to quickly review task details and perform quick actions.

  2. Use J and K to efficiently move between tasks without returning to the board view.

  3. In editing mode, use the forward slash menu and Tiptap shortcuts for efficient text formatting.

  4. Remember that regular keyboard shortcuts are disabled in editing mode to allow for uninterrupted typing.

  5. Always save your changes before exiting editing mode.

","excerpt":"When working with tasks in Hypertask, understanding the difference between navigation mode and editing mode on the task detail page is crucial for efficient task management. This guide will explain both modes and how to use them effectively.","category":"cat-12130036","created_at":1767701666,"updated_at":1792969763,"url":null}

{"id":"pricing-plans","title":"Hypertask pricing, free trial and Free plan limits","slug":"pricing-plans","content":"Hypertask has three plans: **Free**, **BYOK** and **Pro**. The current price list is always on the pricing page: https://hypertask.ai/pricing

## Is Hypertask free?
Yes. The Free plan costs $0 and is free forever. You can use it with your whole team.

## Is there a free trial?
Yes. Paid plans come with a 14-day trial (also asked as "free trial", "trial period", "how long is the trial" or misspelled "trail"). The Free plan itself is free forever, with no trial needed.

## How many people are included in a free team?
There is no member limit on the Free plan. A free team can have unlimited members, so you can invite as many people (users) as you need.

## How many boards and tickets can I have on Free? (board and ticket limits)
On the Free plan you get unlimited members and unlimited open tickets. You can own up to 3 boards. Archived boards are not counted. A paid or trialing plan has no board limit.

## What are the limitations of the Free plan?
Free plan limits (also asked as "freeplan", "free tier", "free version" or "free account" limits, limitations or restrictions): A free team gets unlimited members and unlimited open tickets, and each person can own up to 3 boards (archived boards are not counted). It costs $0, is free forever, and needs no credit card. A paid or trialing plan has no board limit.

What Free does not include, compared with paid plans:
- More than 3 owned boards. Paid and trialing plans have no board limit.
- Free includes a small starter AI allowance on fast budget models. For more AI, Pro includes more AI on Hypertask's managed models, or BYOK runs AI on your own keys.
- Integrations come with Pro.
- Support on Free is email support. Pro gets priority support.
- File uploads: Free includes file uploads and storage. This article does not list file size or total storage limits, so don't promise a storage number or unlimited storage; point to https://hypertask.ai/pricing for current details.

## Do I need a credit card to start?
No. You don't need a credit card to start. Sign up with **Start for free** (https://app.hypertask.ai/login) and choose a paid plan only when you are ready.

## How much does Hypertask cost?
Paid plans are priced per user (per seat). You can pay yearly or monthly.

**Billed yearly**
- BYOK: $8 per user / month ($96 per user / year)
- Pro: $16 per user / month ($192 per user / year)

**Billed monthly**
- BYOK: $10 per user / month
- Pro: $20 per user / month

Free is $0. Paying yearly saves 20%.

## Seats on paid plans
BYOK and Pro are offered for teams of up to 50 seats, billed monthly or yearly. When someone joins a team on a paid plan, the number of seats on the subscription is updated.

The pricing page lists only these monthly and yearly prices, for up to 50 seats. It does not list volume discounts, multi-year plans or paying by invoice, so we can't promise any of those here. To ask about more than 50 seats or other billing needs, email help@hypertask.ai or ask here to talk to a human on the team.

## What each plan includes
**Free**
- Unlimited members and unlimited open tickets
- Own up to 3 boards (archived boards are not counted)
- A small included starter AI allowance on fast budget models
- CLI and MCP access for AI agents
- Email support

**BYOK (bring your own key)**
- All AI features, running on your own API keys from Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter
- Up to 50 team seats
- CLI and MCP access
- Email support

**Pro** (for teams that want more AI, with no keys to manage, plus integrations)
- Everything in BYOK
- More AI included, on Hypertask's managed models, with no API keys to manage
- Integrations
- Priority support

## How much AI is included?
- **Free:** a small included starter allowance of AI on fast budget models.
- **Pro:** more AI included, on Hypertask's managed models. No keys to manage.
- **BYOK:** AI runs on your own Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter keys.

The app shows how much of this month's included AI your team has used: the team owner or a board admin can see it in **Settings → AI Usage**.

## How to upgrade
In the Hypertask app, open **Settings → Plans** (https://app.hypertask.ai/settings/plans), choose BYOK or Pro, then pick monthly or yearly billing.

## Questions about price or billing
See https://hypertask.ai/pricing, email help@hypertask.ai, or ask here to talk to a human on the team.
","excerpt":"Free is $0 forever, with unlimited members, unlimited open tickets and up to 3 owned boards. Paid plans per user per month: BYOK $10 monthly or $8 billed yearly, Pro $20 monthly or $16 billed yearly. Paid plans come with a 14-day trial. Upgrade in Settings > Plans.","category":"cat-12128993","created_at":1773062572,"updated_at":1792969769,"url":null}

{"id":"10895732","title":"Replying to and Quoting Comments in Hypertask","slug":"replying-to-and-quoting-comments-in-hypertasks","content":"

Replying to Comments

Using Keyboard:

  1. Navigate to the comment using the Tab key or arrow keys.

  2. Press Enter to focus on the comment box at the bottom of the page.

  3. Type your response in the comment box.

  4. Press Ctrl + Enter (Windows) or Cmd + Enter (Mac) to post your reply.

Using Mouse:

  1. Scroll to the comment box at the bottom of the page.

  2. Click in the comment box to focus.

  3. Type your response in the comment box.

  4. Click the \"Save\" button to submit your reply.

For more information on keyboard navigation, see our guide on Navigation and Editing Mode in Hypertask Task Detail Page.

Quoting Comments

Quoting comments requires a combination of mouse and keyboard actions:

  1. Navigate to the comment using the Tab key, arrow keys, or mouse.

  2. Use your mouse to highlight the specific part of the comment you want to quote.

  3. Press Enter on your keyboard.

  4. The highlighted text will appear quoted in the comment box at the bottom of the page.

  5. Add your response below the quoted text.

  6. Press Ctrl + Enter (Windows) or Cmd + Enter (Mac), or click the \"Save\" button to post your comment.

Note: There is no way to quote comments using only the keyboard or only the mouse. The process always requires both.

Editing Quoted Text

You can edit the quoted text if needed:

  1. Place your cursor in the quoted section of the comment box.

  2. Make your changes as necessary.

  3. The quoted text will remain in the quote format, distinguishing it from your response.

For more details on editing comments, see our guide on How to Edit Comments in Hypertask.

Tips for Effective Communication

  • Use replies to maintain the context of conversations within tasks.

  • Quote specific parts of comments to address particular points in a discussion.

  • Keep quotes concise to maintain focus in your responses.

  • You can quote multiple parts of comments in a single response by repeating the quoting process.

  • Practice using the combination of mouse selection and keyboard commands for efficient quoting.

  • Utilize the Forward Slash Menu for additional formatting options in your comments.

Remember, you can always access the full list of keyboard shortcuts by pressing ? while on your board or task detail page.

","excerpt":"Hypertask offers efficient ways to reply to comments and quote specific parts of messages, enhancing communication within your tasks. This guide covers how to use these features effectively.","category":"cat-12130036","created_at":1767701666,"updated_at":1792969763,"url":null}

{"id":"11900001","title":"Troubleshooting Email Login (Magic Link)","slug":"troubleshooting-email-login-magic-link","content":"

How Email Login Works

Hypertask uses a passwordless login system. When you choose to log in with your email address:

  1. Enter your email address on the login page

  2. We send you a magic link or one-time code to that email

  3. Click the link or enter the code to log in

There is no password - the email itself serves as your authentication.

Login Methods in Hypertask

Hypertask offers two ways to log in:

  • Email login (Magic Link): Enter your email, receive a link/code, click to log in

  • Google/Workspace login: Click \"Sign in with Google\" to use your Google or Google Workspace account

If you are having login issues, first identify which method you are using.

Not Receiving the Login Email?

If you are not receiving the magic link email, try these steps:

1. Check Your Spam/Junk Folder

The email might have been filtered. Look for an email from notifications@hypertask.ai

2. Corporate Email Filters

If you are using a work email, your company email security system might be blocking our emails. Ask your IT department to whitelist the following email address:

notifications@hypertask.ai

3. Wait a Few Minutes

Sometimes email delivery can be delayed. Wait 2-3 minutes before requesting another login link.

4. Double-Check Your Email Address

Make sure you entered the correct email address with no typos.

5. Try Google Login Instead

If email login continues to fail, you can use Google login as an alternative. Click \"Sign in with Google\" on the login page.

Still Having Issues?

If you have tried all the above steps and still cannot log in, contact our support team. Please let us know:

  • Which login method you are using (email or Google)

  • The email address you are trying to log in with

  • Whether you are using a personal or corporate email

  • Any error messages you see

","excerpt":"Having trouble logging in with email? Learn how Hypertask magic link login works and troubleshoot common issues like missing emails and corporate filters.","category":"cat-12128993","created_at":1768903054,"updated_at":1768903054,"url":null}

{"id":"10895790","title":"Using AI-Powered Auto Summary in Hypertask (Shortcut i)","slug":"using-ai-powered-auto-summary-in-hypertasks-shortcut-i","content":"

What is Auto Summary?

Auto Summary is an AI-powered feature that automatically generates concise summaries of task descriptions, comments, and discussions. It helps you quickly grasp the key points of lengthy content without reading through everything in detail.

How to Access Auto Summary

  1. On the Task Detail Page:

    • Open any task to view its details

    • Look for the "Summary" section at the top of the task description

  2. In Comments:

    • For long comment threads, an auto-generated summary will appear at the top of the comments section

  3. Using Keyboard Shortcuts:

    • Select any task or comment

    • Press I to view the AI-generated summary

  4. Using a Mouse:

    • Simply click on the summary element to open and view the AI-generated summary

  5. On Mobile Devices:

    • Tap on the summary element to view the AI-generated summary

Benefits of Using Auto Summary

  • Time-saving: Quickly understand the essence of tasks and discussions

  • Improved focus: Easily identify key points and action items

  • Enhanced productivity: Spend less time reading and more time doing

  • Better decision-making: Get a clear overview to make informed choices faster

Tips for Effective Use

  1. Use auto summaries for initial task review to decide which tasks need immediate attention

  2. Refer to summaries before team meetings to quickly refresh your memory on discussion topics

  3. Utilize summaries when returning from time off to catch up on project progress efficiently

  4. Combine auto summaries with Hypertask's powerful filtering for even more efficient task management

Customizing Auto Summary

Currently, the auto summary feature is automatically applied to tasks and comments that meet a certain length threshold. Future updates may include options to customize this feature.

Limitations

  • Auto summaries are AI-generated and may occasionally miss nuanced details

  • They're not a replacement for reading important information in full, especially for critical tasks

","excerpt":"Hypertask's AI-powered auto summary feature provides quick, intelligent overviews of tasks and discussions. This guide will explain how to use and benefit from this productivity-enhancing tool.","category":"cat-12130247","created_at":1767701666,"updated_at":1792969758,"url":null}

{"id":"10895796","title":"Using Auto-Splits in Hypertask","slug":"using-auto-splits-in-hypertasks","content":"


What are Auto-Splits?

Auto-Splits are automatically created categories in your Hypertask inbox that sort your messages based on certain criteria. There are two main types of Auto-Splits:

  1. Project-specific Auto-Splits

  2. Global Auto-Splits

Types of Auto-Splits

Project-specific Auto-Splits

For each project or board you have in Hypertask, an automatic split is created. These splits contain messages related to their respective projects.

\n

Global Auto-Splits

There are four global Auto-Splits that apply across all projects:

  1. Updates: Shows tickets that have been moved to other columns.

  2. Reactions: Displays comments that have received emoji reactions.

  3. Important: Lists all direct comments.

  4. All: Shows all messages in your inbox.

How Auto-Splits Work

Auto-Splits appear and disappear dynamically based on the presence of relevant messages. If there are no messages that fit a particular split's criteria, that split will not be visible in your inbox.

\n

Navigating Auto-Splits

To navigate through Auto-Splits:

  • Press 'Tab' to move forward through the splits.

  • Press 'Shift + Tab' to move backward through the splits.

  • Use 'J' and 'K' to move up and down within a split.

  • Press 'Enter' to open a message.

  • Press 'E' to archive a message.

Using Auto-Splits Effectively

  1. Start with Important: Begin by checking the 'Important' split for direct comments that may need immediate attention.

  2. Check Updates: Review the 'Updates' split to see task movements across all projects.

  3. Review Reactions: Look at the 'Reactions' split to see which comments have resonated with your team.

  4. Address Project-Specific Splits: Go through each project-specific split based on your current priorities.

  5. Finish with All: Scan the 'All' split to ensure you haven't missed any messages.

Tips for Using Auto-Splits

  • Process your inbox regularly to prevent message buildup.

  • Use keyboard shortcuts to navigate quickly between and within splits.

  • Remember that splits only appear when they contain messages. If you don't see a split, it means there are no relevant messages at that time.

","excerpt":"Auto-Splits is a feature in Hypertask that automatically organizes your inbox messages into different categories. This guide will explain what Auto-Splits are, how they work, and how to use them effectively.","category":"cat-12130247","created_at":1767701666,"updated_at":1792969758,"url":null}

{"id":"10911082","title":"Using Project Board Views in Hypertask","slug":"using-project-board-views-in-hypertasks","content":"

What Are Project Board Views?

Project Board Views save combinations of:

  • Applied filters

  • Column configurations

  • Sorting preferences

  • Other board customizations

Each view can be personal (only visible to you) or shared with your entire team.

Creating a Project Board View

  1. Set up your board with your preferred filters and layout:

    • Use Shift + F to apply filters

    • Arrange columns as needed

    • Set sorting preferences with Shift + S

  2. Save your configuration:
    ​

    • Press Shift + V to open the save view dialog

    • Enter a descriptive name for your view

    • Choose whether the view is private or shared with the team

    • Click "Save" or press Enter

Switching Between Views

You can switch between your saved views in two ways:
​

Using Keyboard Shortcuts

  1. Press G then V to open the view selector

  2. Use arrow keys to navigate to your desired view

  3. Press Enter to apply the selected view

Using Mouse

  1. Click the Views icon or the board title in the board header

  2. Select your desired view from the dropdown menu

When a custom view is active, a blue view icon will appear in the header to indicate you're not viewing the default board layout.
​

Managing Your Views


To manage existing views:

  1. Press G then V to open the view selector

  2. Click the "Manage Views" option

  3. From here you can:

    • Rename views

    • Delete views

    • Change privacy settings

    • Reorder views

Returning to Default View

To exit a custom view and return to the default board:

  1. Press G then V to open the view selector

  2. Select "Default View" or press Esc

Practical Examples

Here are some useful view configurations to consider:

My Tasks View

  • Filter: Tasks assigned to me

  • Sort: By priority and due date

Upcoming Deadlines View

  • Filter: Tasks with due dates in the next week

  • Sort: By due date

Unread Notifications View

  • Filter: Tasks with unread notifications

  • Sort: By most recent notification

Team Progress View

  • Filter: Tasks in progress

  • Group: By assignee

Tips for Effective View Management

  1. Use descriptive names that clearly indicate the purpose of each view

  2. Consider creating standard views for your team to ensure everyone has access to important perspectives

  3. Regularly review and clean up unused views

  4. Create specific views for different meetings or review sessions

For more information on enhancing your Hypertask experience, check out these related articles:

  • [How to Filter Tasks in Hypertask: Mastering Shift+F](https://help.hypertask.ai/help

","excerpt":"Project Board Views allow you to save and quickly switch between different board layouts, filters, and settings. This feature helps you maintain multiple perspectives of your project without needing to manually adjust filters each time.","category":"cat-12130036","created_at":1767701666,"updated_at":1792969757,"url":null}

{"id":"article-ai-chat-1741567200","title":"Using the AI Chat to Manage Your Board and Inbox","slug":"using-the-ai-chat-to-manage-your-board-and-inbox","content":"

What is the AI Chat?

The AI Chat is your built-in AI assistant that can read and act on your boards, tasks, inbox, and projects — all through natural language. Instead of clicking through menus and task lists, just tell the AI what you need.

It has full access to the same tools as the Hypertask MCP server — meaning it can create tasks, move them between boards, add comments, manage your inbox, and much more.

How to Open the AI Chat

You have two ways to open it:

  • Ctrl+Shift+? (Windows) or Cmd+Shift+? (Mac) — open the AI Chat
  • Ctrl+Shift+O (Windows) or Cmd+Shift+O (Mac) — start a new AI Chat session

The chat opens as a sidebar panel so you can keep working on your board while talking to the AI.

What Can the AI Chat Do?

The AI Chat has full board and inbox access. Here are some examples of what you can ask:

Inbox Management

  • "Triage my inbox — categorize everything and archive the noise"
  • "What’s new in my inbox since yesterday?"
  • "Archive all inbox items older than a week"

Task Management

  • "Find all tasks with no assignee and assign them to me"
  • "Move everything in Backlog that’s marked High priority to In Progress"
  • "What tasks haven’t been updated in 2 weeks? Flag them as stale"
  • "Create a task for the homepage redesign on the Sprint board"

Comments & Updates

  • "Add a comment to every overdue task asking for a status update"
  • "Summarize what happened on this board in the last 7 days"

Board Overview

  • "How many tasks are in each column right now?"
  • "Show me all urgent tasks across all my projects"
  • "Who has the most tasks assigned to them?"

Things that used to take an hour of clicking around — done in seconds.

Tips for Getting the Most Out of AI Chat

  • Be specific — the more context you give, the better the results. Say "on the Marketing board" instead of just "on the board"
  • Chain actions — you can ask for multiple things in one message, like "find all overdue tasks, add a comment asking for status, and move them to a Review column"
  • Start fresh when needed — use Ctrl+Shift+O / Cmd+Shift+O to start a new session if the conversation gets long
  • Use it for reporting — ask for summaries, stats, and overviews to get a quick pulse on your projects

AI Chat vs. MCP Server

Both the AI Chat and the MCP server give AI access to the same set of tools. The difference is where you use them:

  • AI Chat — built right into Hypertask. Open it with a keyboard shortcut and start talking. No setup needed.
  • MCP Server — connects external AI tools (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, etc.) to your Hypertask boards. Requires a one-time token setup.

Use the AI Chat for quick queries and board management. Use MCP when you want your coding AI agent to track and manage tasks as part of your development workflow.

{"id":"10895715","title":"Using the Forward Slash Menu in Task Descriptions and Comments","slug":"using-the-forward-slash-menu-in-task-descriptions-and-comments","content":"

Accessing the Forward Slash Menu

The forward slash menu is only available in edit mode on the task detail page. To access it:

  1. Open a task to view its details

  2. Enter edit mode for the description or a comment

  3. Type / (forward slash) anywhere in the text

  4. The menu will appear, showing various options

For more information on navigation and edit modes, see our guide on Navigation and Editing Modes in Hypertask Task Detail Page.

Menu Options

Text Formatting

  • Task List: Toggle a task list for creating checklists

  • Numbered List: Create a numbered list

  • Text: Switch to plain text (removes formatting)

  • Bold: Apply bold formatting to selected text

  • Italic: Apply italic formatting to selected text

  • Underline: Underline selected text

  • BlockQuote: Create a block quote for emphasizing text

Advanced Formatting

  • File Attachments: Upload and attach files to your task or comment

  • Embed Video: Add a YouTube video embed

  • Heading 1: Create a large heading (Level 1)

  • Heading 2: Create a medium heading (Level 2)

  • Highlight: Toggle highlight for selected text

  • Add Image: Upload and insert an image

AI-Assisted Features (Paid Plans Only)

The following AI-powered features are available exclusively to users on paid plans:

  • AI Fix Spelling & Grammar: Automatically correct spelling and grammar errors

  • AI Simplify: Simplify complex text for better readability

  • AI Summarize: Generate a concise summary of selected text

  • AI Translate to German: Translate selected text to German

  • AI Translate to English: Translate selected text to English from any language

  • AI Shorten: Reduce the length of selected text while maintaining key information

Using the Menu

  1. Navigate through options using arrow keys or mouse

  2. Press Enter or click to select an option

  3. For text formatting, apply the style to selected text or start typing with the new format

  4. For AI features (paid plans only), select the text you want to modify before choosing the option

Tips for Effective Use

  • Use headings to organize longer task descriptions or comments

  • Leverage AI features (if available on your plan) for quick improvements to your writing

  • Combine formatting options for clear, visually appealing content

  • Use task lists for breaking down complex tasks into manageable steps

Remember, you can always access the full list of keyboard shortcuts by pressing ? while on your board or task detail page.

{"id":"10895373","title":"Video Tutorial: A Guide to Keyboard-Driven Productivity","slug":"video-tutorial-a-guide-to-keyboard-driven-productivity","content":"

1. Navigating the Kanban Board

  • Move between tasks: J (down) and K (up)

  • Move task between columns: M

  • Access search: / (in navigation mode)

  • Switch to favorite boards: Alt + 1 to Alt + 9

  • Open HTC: Ctrl + K (Windows) or Cmd + K (Mac)

{"id":"10895425","title":"Why You Should Use Hypertasks as a PWA: Quick Access and Improved Keyboard Experience","slug":"why-you-should-use-hypertasks-as-a-pwa-quick-access-and-improved-keyboard-experience","content":"

Why Use Hypertasks as a PWA?

  1. Quick Access: Install Hypertasks as a PWA to get a dedicated access point at the OS level. This allows you to launch the app quickly and easily, without opening a browser and navigating to the website.

  2. Improved Keyboard Experience: The PWA version reduces browser native UI elements (the browser \"chrome\"), which significantly decreases the risk of shortcut clashes. This is particularly beneficial for Hypertasks, as it relies heavily on keyboard shortcuts for efficient use.

These advantages make the PWA version of Hypertasks the preferred way to use our app, especially for frequent users who value quick access and a seamless keyboard experience.

What is a Progressive Web App (PWA)?

A Progressive Web App is essentially a website that can be installed on your device like a native app. For Hypertasks, this means you get the same features and experience as the website, but with the added benefits of quick access and reduced browser interference.

How to Install Hypertasks as a PWA

For Desktop (Chrome):

  1. Open Hypertasks in Google Chrome.

  2. Look for the install icon (usually a plus sign or computer icon) in the address bar.

  3. Click on the install icon.

  4. In the pop-up window, click \"Install\".

  5. Hypertasks will now be installed as a PWA on your computer.

For Mobile (Android):

  1. Open Hypertasks in Google Chrome.

  2. Tap the three-dot menu in the top right corner.

  3. Select \"Add to Home screen\".

  4. Tap \"Add\" in the popup.

  5. Hypertasks will now appear as an app icon on your home screen.

For iOS:

  1. Install Google Chrome from the App Store if you haven't already.

  2. Open Hypertasks in Chrome.

  3. Tap the three-dot menu in the bottom right corner.

  4. Select \"Add to Home Screen\".

  5. Tap \"Add\" in the popup.

  6. Hypertasks will now appear as an app icon on your home screen.

Additional Benefits of Using Hypertasks as a PWA

  • Dedicated Workspace: The PWA provides a cleaner, more focused environment for managing your tasks and projects.

  • Fewer Distractions: Without browser tabs and UI elements, you can concentrate better on your work in Hypertasks.

  • Optimized for Keyboard Use: With reduced risk of shortcut clashes, you can fully leverage Hypertasks' keyboard-driven interface.

Additional Notes

  • The Hypertasks PWA offers the same features and experience as the website.

  • An internet connection is still required to use Hypertasks.

  • Chrome provides the best support for the Hypertasks PWA, which is why we recommend using it for installation.

By installing Hypertasks as a PWA, you'll have a convenient shortcut to boost your productivity, manage your tasks more efficiently, and enjoy an optimized keyboard experience.

Docked AI chat scope

Use the scope menu in the docked AI chat to choose what the conversation is about:

  • Current board — the default scope; focuses on the board you are viewing.
  • Current ticket — available on a ticket page; focuses on that ticket's title, description, and comments. The scope stays on Current board until you choose Current ticket, and switches back to Current board when you leave the ticket.
  • Pinned boards — choose a pinned board as the scope.
  • All boards — includes all your accessible boards.

Current ticket is only available in the docked chat on a ticket page. The full-screen chat page is unchanged.

When AI chat opens

The docked AI chat no longer opens by itself. It opens when you open it, and it stays where you left it as you move between tickets, boards, My Tasks and the inbox, on desktop and on your phone.

A closed chat stays closed when you create a task; an open one stays open. If you close it, a reload keeps it closed, and a tab where you left it open keeps it open.

Settings > General > Task Page no longer offers the three auto-open switches, because nothing opens on its own. The older Keep AI chat closed always and Open AI chat by default choices are gone with them.

Board filter behavior

  • All boards — shows every chat across all your accessible boards.
  • One board — shows only chats from that board.
  • Default is All boards, so all your chats appear by default when you open the chat.

Run /chat or switch to the Chat view to start a conversation. Then use the board filter above the chat list to switch between "All boards" and a specific board.

Agent Chat sidebar status

When you open an agent chat with an agent that supports status visibility, the chat sidebar displays real-time per-agent status instead of a static green dot.

Available status indicators

  • Active — the agent is currently processing a task or message.
  • Idle — the agent is idle but available, with an optional duration indicating how long it has been idle.
  • Idle with duration — same as Idle, but explicitly shows the elapsed time (in minutes) since the last activity.
  • Out of tokens — the agent has exhausted its token budget and cannot process further requests until refreshed.
  • Inactive — the agent has been turned off or has no recent activity; it is not responding.

How status changes are shown

  • The status is computed server-side at request time and shown as text immediately next to the agent name.
  • Changing from one status to another updates in real time without needing to refresh the page.
  • If an agent is explicitly turned off, it always shows Inactive until you restore the agent or the chat session closes.

Agent Chat auto-scroll behavior

Agent Chat automatically scrolls to the most recent messages as new content arrives, including queued and typing indicators, so you never miss updates during active conversations.

Scrolling behavior

  • When you are already at the bottom of the chat list and new messages arrive or queued statuses appear, the window follows them.
  • If you scroll up to view earlier messages and new messages arrive, the scroll position stays where you left it until you scroll back down.
  • When a new message appears while at the bottom, Chat immediately follows to keep the latest message in view.

This behavior applies across all supported channels and helps you stay aligned with agent progress without manually paging through the thread.

{"title":"AI Features","slug":"docs-features-ai-features","excerpt":"AI-powered task creation, voice dictation, text enhancement, and an intelligent co-worker built into your workflow.","category":"AI & Productivity","html":"

For tools and limits, see What AI chat can do.

AI is woven through every part of Hypertask — create tasks, filter your board, smart-label workloads, and manage daily operations without leaving the workflow you already use.

  1. AI-assisted task creation
  • Click AI in the top-right corner of any board, open the Ask Hypertask AI panel, and describe a task in plain English.
  • AI parses the description and creates a task pre-assigned to you with a title, description, and relevant tags (task types, priorities, area).
  • Review the generated task before saving; edit fields or refine the prompt and generate again.
  1. Prompt-based filtering
  • In the Board Filter, type natural-language constraints like:
  • show me top-priority bugs
  • tasks assigned to Valentin and due this week
  • Use combinations such as high priority and not blocked, and press Enter to apply.
  1. Smart labels
  • Open a label (or the Manage Tags screen) and create a new label marked as a smart label.
  • In the "Smart label — AI keeps this label on matching tasks" field, define which tasks should carry it, for example:
  • backend issue, involves DB, high impact
  • Save; AI immediately classifies the board up to 500 existing tasks and adds the label to matches. Smart labels show a sparkle icon in label lists.
  • New tasks are classified when created; edited tasks are re-classified when title or description change; updating the prompt re-runs classification for the entire board.
  1. AI usage without a signed-in user
  • AI usage can now be recorded and stored as usage tracks even when calls don't originate from a signed-in user.
  • This allows external agents or systems invoking the AI APIs to function without requiring active authentication, while still producing usage records available to admins.
  1. Batch-powered background workloads
  • Background smart labels and other AI classification runs that involve many tasks are routed to Anthropic's Batch API at half price, allowing cost-efficient processing at scale.
  • Matching tasks receive their labels automatically; activity is logged in the task activity feed.
  • AI writes a compact representation of your content and sends it to the embed service, which can reject very long or empty text or refuse very long or empty text. On these failures, the upsert silently rotates the text and upserts without final vectors instead of failing, so comments and pages remain searchable with the relevant tags even when vectors aren't generated.
  • You don't see extra UI for this—it happens invisibly in the background with consistent results.
  1. AI Chat suggestions for tickets
  • Open AI Chat in a ticket panel to get context-aware suggestions tailored to that ticket's specific information.
  • Previously, suggestions could be generic or fail entirely when the server returned "No output generated"; Haiku 5.5 now returns proper suggestions that match the ticket context.
  1. Faster agent task lists
  • AI agents are now much quicker to load their task lists, especially after server warm-up.
  • Previously slow database reads that fetched task lists have been optimized: the slowest 5% of calls improved from ~129 ms down to ~40 ms. The improvement consistently benefits agents on both warm and cold servers, making AI-driven workflows feel far more responsive.
  1. AI Chat histories
  • A spinner marks chats that are replying. The sidebar header and conversation list show it. Each chat keeps its own indicator. It disappears when replying finishes, fails, or stops.
  • Open AI Chat from the right rail or press Ctrl/Cmd + I to see a list of conversations.
  • In the full-screen chat view (desktop), the history list pages as the window resizes, and you scroll to load more older chats. Pick or filter from that list to open a chat.
  • On mobile, the list is limited; tap an entry to open its history.
  • The docked chat always shows your most recent chats inline; use the full-screen view for history navigation.
  • Your agents are listed in an Agents section at the top of the chat title list. Pick one to switch the chat to that agent's conversation in place. Its name shows in the chat title, and choosing it never sends a message.
  • You can also type @ in the chat box. Agents are listed first, then boards and other items. Press Enter or click to add the agent as a chip and continue writing; nothing is sent until you press Send.
  • Drag the desktop chat edge to resize. Your account remembers this width in this browser.
  • Closing, reloading, and changing boards keep your choice. A narrow window temporarily reduces the displayed width. Widening restores your choice.
  1. Comment summaries preserve open questions
  • When AI summarizes your comments, it now accurately reflects whether questions have been answered or remain unresolved.
  • Comment summaries display Open: ... for unanswered questions instead of inventing an answer, and retain "still unresolved" language when appropriate.
  1. Bulk archiving avoids server errors
  • Agents that attempt to archive many tasks see a clear refusal message instead of a server crash.
  • An earlier incident had agents trying to archive 31 Done tickets per day, triggering a 500 error. The fix now returns a direct not allowed response, keeping workflows smooth and errors visible for observers.

Run chats together

Start a reply, then open another chat. Each chat replies independently. There is no two-chat limit. Existing usage limits still apply.

Follow-ups wait only for their own chat. They send in order, even while you read another chat. Select Stop in a chat to stop that reply; other chats keep running.

Keep a conversation across tickets

Pin AI chat open in its menu, then open another ticket. Your selected conversation and earlier messages stay in the sidebar. New messages use the ticket you are viewing as context.

Select New chat to start a separate conversation. Creating a ticket with the task writer puts that ticket's own introduction in the conversation you have open; it never opens the chat for you.

Image generation removed

Hypertask no longer generates new images. Existing images and uploads remain unchanged.

Image generation is absent from team settings. Check Settings → Team → Default models and AI features. The Ctrl+K image generation shortcut was removed. Image model mentions were also removed.

Where AI appears

AreaWhat AI does
Task creationParses your description into a task with title, description, priority, and tags.
Board filteringUnderstands natural-language constraints and builds dynamic filters.
Smart LabelsKeeps labels on tasks that match your AI prompt; changes to tasks or the prompt trigger reclassification.
AI ChatGlobal assistant for questions, summarization, and quick actions, with full-screen history paging.
Ticket AI suggestionsProvides context-specific suggestions in ticket panels that mirror the ticket's subject and related data.
Bulk AI workloadsHeavy classification runs use the Batch API to handle large boards efficiently; background jobs go through Anthropic's half-price Batch endpoint. Usage is recorded as usage tracks regardless of whether a signed-in user is present.
Agent task listsOptimized reads for quick agent workloads; significant speedup for the slowest dataset slices.
Task summariesSummarize the current task says what the task is first, then where it stands, then up to three open points. It does not open with a next action.
Comment summariesSummarize comments and preserve whether questions remain open for human follow-up.

When the chat opens and closes

The AI chat stays where you put it.

  • It opens when you open it, and closes when you close it. Moving between tickets, boards, My Tasks and the inbox leaves it as it was.
  • It keeps the same conversation while you move around a team. A new ticket no longer starts a new thread behind your back.
  • Creating a task leaves it as it was too. A closed chat stays closed; an open one stays open.
  • Reloading a tab keeps the state you left: open stays open, closed stays closed.

Task creation with AI writer

  1. Open the New Task box — Use Ctrl+J on desktop or Cmd+J to open the New Task creator from boards, the inbox, or any view. On the Tasks page, click New Task in the toolbar.

To change the destination, press Ctrl+Shift+B (or Cmd+Shift+B on Mac). The board picker lists recently visited boards first, then sorts ties alphabetically. It remembers board visits in this browser. Search for a board and press Enter, or click its name.

  1. Describe your task — Enter a brief description of the work you need done. You can type directly or let AI expand your ideas. The model chip under the note shows the model that will write the task: click it to pick another model or effort level, or use Reset to default to go back to the board's default.
  1. Let AI write the task — Reviews your inputs and generates a complete, structured task with a title, description, priority, and relevant tags. AI respects your board's templates and style when available.
  1. Review and refine — Edit any field in the generated task. You can press Ctrl+K (desktop) or Cmd+K (Mac) in the description area to refine the AI's work, regenerate, or add more detail.
  1. Save the task — When you're satisfied, click Create (or Enter) to save the task and add it to the board. The task appears immediately in the appropriate column or section.
  1. Answer the follow-up questions — The new task opens with the AI chat sidebar next to it. Under Questions and ideas for this ticket, it shows up to three one-tap chips based on your original note and your board's rules, such as a next action to take, a job to split out, or an open decision to settle. Click one to send it in the same chat. When nothing fits, no chips appear.

Creating tickets through AI Chat

Ask AI Chat to create a ticket. Its saved link appears before writing finishes. Open it while its description is being written. The finished title, description, priority and size follow. Saved title or description edits stop automatic replacement. If writing fails, the saved ticket remains. Chat tells you its description is unfinished. Finish that ticket instead of creating another.

AI writer failure reasons

Fix When the AI writer fails to generate a task, the Ctrl+J New Task box and the AI Task Writer now show you the real reason for the failure instead of hiding it. Your note is still saved as a task, so you don't lose your work:

  • Error messages displayed — Common errors like quota limits, missing context, or prompt format issues show explainable messages.
  • Task created anyway — Your original description or note is preserved as a task, so you can retry AI later or edit it manually.
  • Applies everywhere — This fix covers task creation from boards, the inbox, and when editing task descriptions.

If AI generation is not available (for example, your team has not configured an AI key), the text you entered appears without modification, keeping your workflow uninterrupted.

AI Task Writer

The AI Task Writer is a prompt-based task creation flow that generates complete, shippable tickets from paste inputs.

How it works today

The Task Writer uses the board's saved custom instructions whenever you write a ticket with Ctrl+J compose, ask AI chat to create a ticket, or use the CLI/MCP task writer.

  • Board format — Keeps the section layout shared by past tickets, such as Problem, Hypothesis, Control, Variation, and a scoring section, while keeping each section short.
  • Custom fields — Fills the board's Number, Select, Text, Date, and Checkbox fields when the instructions or past tickets show what to use. For example, a score field can match the score in the title. Values that do not fit the field are skipped.

It also uses search to find related tickets instead of inventing them.

Using the Task Writer

  • From a board: Ctrl+J / Cmd+J and select Create with AI — Task Writer.
  • From the command palette: Ctrl+K — search for "Task Write" and select it.
  • From a task: Click the AI icon in the task header and select Task Writer.

After the Task Writer generates a draft, you can refine it just like any other AI-generated comment or description.

When Ctrl+J or AI chat writes a task description or comment that references an uploaded image or image link, the image appears inline in the text by default. Ask for "attachment only" or "link only" to keep it as an attachment or link instead.

Included AI allowance

Free gets a small starter AI allowance on fast budget models. Pro includes more AI on managed models with no keys needed. BYOK uses your own model keys. Owners and board admins see percent used in Settings > AI Usage.

Background AI, including smart labels and summaries, counts toward the same allowance as interactive AI when it uses Hypertask's key.

Calls using your own provider key do not use the included allowance.

When the included allowance is reached, further calls on Hypertask's key are refused. Your own-key calls can continue.

Demo chat requires an active demo guest session. If prompted, start the demo again to keep chatting.

When AI is not available

Behavior change AI features now show clear guidance when a team does not have an AI key configured. Previously, teams without an AI key would see server errors when trying to use AI in agents or the CLI. Now, users receive a concise message directing them to add an AI key through the Appearance & AI Models settings page:

"AI features require an AI key. Configure your AI key in Appearance & AI Models."

This applies to AI-powered task creation, filters, smart labels, and agent workflows that invoke AI.

Settings

  • Choose your preferred AI model in the Appearance & AI Models settings page. Different models may produce different responses.
  • If a provider rejects your own AI key during chat, the message names that key and tells you to update it in Settings, then AI, then Bring your own key.
  • Adjust leniency of AI-assisted task creation in the same settings area if you prefer more precise or broader suggestions.
  • Smart label accuracy can be tuned by sharpening or relaxing your prompt; see the "How it stays current" details in the Smart Labels reference.

Smart labels and prompts are a best-effort AI signal. They do not substitute for human review. Ensure your prompt manages edge cases or exceptions directly, for example: "NOT: schema changes on branches not yet merged."

Use smart labels together with filters and saved views to create reusable patterns for recurring workloads (e.g., on-call issues, quick fillers, enterprise integrations).

{"title":"Using the AI Task Writer in Hypertask (Ctrl+J / Cmd+J)","slug":"using-the-ai-task-writer-in-hypertasks-ctrlj-cmdj","excerpt":"The AI Task Writer is a powerful feature in Hypertask that enhances productivity by assisting with AI-powered task creation and organization within your Kanban boar","category":"cat-12130247","html":"

\n

Key Features

  1. AI-Assisted Task Creation: Generate detailed tasks by typing a prompt.

  2. Context-Aware Responses: Utilizes existing board context for relevant task descriptions.

  3. Dynamic Information Retrieval: Accesses current project information before generating tasks.

  4. Custom Instructions: Tailor the AI's output to your specific requirements.

  5. Seamless Integration: Accessible via the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+J (Windows) or Cmd+J (Mac) when focused on a task description.

How to Use the AI Task Writer

  1. Open a task and focus on the description field.

  2. Press Ctrl+J (Windows) or Cmd+J (Mac) to activate the AI Task Writer.

  3. Enter your prompt or request in the chat interface.

  4. The AI analyzes your prompt and the existing board context.

  5. Review the generated task description and relevant details.

  6. Edit or refine the AI-generated content as needed.

  7. Save the task with the new information.

Applications

The AI Task Writer can assist with various task types:

  • Software development specifications

  • App or website project outlines

  • Marketing campaign tasks

  • Sales objectives

  • Bug reports

  • Product descriptions

  • General task creation and organization

Benefits

  • Time Savings: Reduce time spent on manual task description writing.

  • Contextual Relevance: Utilize board-specific information for accurate task details.

  • Consistency: Encourage standardized task descriptions across team members.

  • Idea Generation: Overcome writer's block and generate new ideas.

  • Adaptability: Suitable for teams of various sizes and industries.

Best Practices

  1. Ensure you're focused on the task description field before activating the AI Task Writer.

  2. Review and edit AI-generated content to ensure accuracy and alignment with project goals.

  3. Use clear and specific prompts for better results.

  4. Combine AI suggestions with your own expertise and project knowledge.

  5. Experiment with different prompt styles to find what works best for your needs.
